claims.statement: In Slavic mythology, Perun (Перун) is the highest god of the pantheon and god of sky, thunder, lightning, storms, rain, law, war, fertility and oak trees.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Slavia, Perun (Перун) adalah dewa tertinggi dalam jajaran dewa, dewa langit, guruh, petir, badai, hujan, hukum, perang, kesuburan, dan pohon ek.
claims.quote: In Slavic mythology, Perun (Cyrillic: Перун ) is the highest god of the pantheon and the god of sky, thunder, lightning, storms, rain, law, war, fertility and oak trees.

claims.statement: His other attributes were fire, mountains, wind, iris, eagle, firmament, horses and carts, and weapons: hammer, axe (Axe of Perun) and arrow.
claims.statement_id: Atribut lain Perun adalah api, gunung, angin, bunga iris, elang, cakrawala, kuda dan kereta, serta senjata berupa palu, kapak (Kapak Perun), dan anak panah.
claims.quote: His other attributes were fire, mountains, wind, iris, eagle, firmament ... horses and carts, and weapons (hammer, axe (Axe of Perun), and arrow).

claims.statement: The supreme god in Kievan Rus in the 9th-10th centuries, Perun was first associated with stone weapons and later with metal ones.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai dewa tertinggi di Rus Kiev pada abad ke-9 sampai ke-10, Perun mula-mula dikaitkan dengan senjata dari batu, kemudian dengan senjata logam.
claims.quote: The supreme god in the Kievan Rus' during the 9th-10th centuries, Perun was first associated with weapons made of stone and later with those of metal.

claims.statement: To this day, in a number of Slavic languages the word perun means "thunder" or "lightning bolt".
claims.statement_id: Hingga kini, dalam sejumlah bahasa Slavia kata perun berarti "guruh" atau "sambaran petir".
claims.quote: To this day, the word perun in a number of Slavic languages means "thunder," or "lightning bolt".

claims.statement: As early as the 6th century he was mentioned in De Bello Gothico, a historical source by the Eastern Roman historian Procopius.
claims.statement_id: Sejak abad ke-6 ia sudah disebut dalam De Bello Gothico, sumber sejarah karya sejarawan Romawi Timur Procopius.
claims.quote: As early as the 6th century, he was mentioned in De Bello Gothico, a historical source written by the Eastern Roman historian Procopius.

claims.statement: In 980, when Prince Vladimir the Great took the throne of Kiev, he erected statues of five pagan gods before his palace, discarding them after his Christianization in 988; Perun was chief among them, with a silver head and a golden moustache.
claims.statement_id: Pada tahun 980, ketika pangeran Vladimir Agung naik takhta di Kiev, ia mendirikan arca lima dewa pagan di depan istananya, yang kemudian ia singkirkan setelah masuk Kristen pada 988; Perun adalah yang utama, digambarkan berkepala perak dan berkumis emas.
claims.quote: In 980, when prince Vladimir the Great came to the throne of Kiev, he erected statues of five pagan gods in front of his palace which he soon thereafter discarded after his Christianization in 988. Perun was chief among these, represented with a silver head and a golden moustache.

claims.statement: Perun is strongly correlated with the near-identical Perkūnas/Pērkons of Baltic mythology, suggesting a common Proto-Indo-European thunder god origin or borrowing.
claims.statement_id: Perun sangat berkaitan dengan Perkūnas/Pērkons yang hampir identik dari mitologi Baltik, yang menunjukkan asal bersama dari dewa guruh Proto-Indo-Eropa atau peminjaman.
claims.quote: Perun is strongly correlated with the near-identical Perkūnas/Pērkons from Baltic mythology, suggesting either a common derivative of the Proto-Indo European thunder god

claims.statement: The root *perkwu probably first meant oak, but in Proto-Slavic it became *per-, meaning "to strike, to slay".
claims.statement_id: Akar *perkwu semula mungkin berarti pohon ek, tetapi dalam bahasa Proto-Slavia berkembang menjadi *per- yang berarti "memukul, membunuh".
claims.quote: The root *perkwu originally probably meant oak, but in Proto-Slavic this evolved into *per- meaning "to strike, to slay".

claims.statement: Perun's lightning bolts were believed to be stones and stone arrows; folk belief held fulgurites, belemnites and sometimes prehistoric stone tools found in the ground to be remains of these weapons.
claims.statement_id: Kilat Perun dipercaya berupa batu dan anak panah batu; menurut kepercayaan rakyat, fulgurit, belemnit, dan kadang perkakas batu prasejarah yang ditemukan di tanah adalah sisa senjata itu.
claims.quote: Perun's lightning bolts were believed to be stones and stone arrows. According to folk beliefs, fulgurites, belemnites, and sometimes even the remains of prehistoric stone tools found in the ground are remains of these weapons.

claims.statement: The weapons of Perun protected against bad luck, evil magic, disease and lightning itself.
claims.statement_id: Senjata Perun melindungi dari nasib buruk, sihir jahat, penyakit, dan juga dari petir itu sendiri.
claims.quote: The weapons of Perun protected against bad luck, evil magic, disease, and – naturally enough – lightning itself.

claims.statement: Perun can be shown to have been married to the Sun, but he shared his wife with his enemy Veles, as each night the Sun was thought to dive into the underworld, the realm of the dead ruled by Veles.
claims.statement_id: Perun dapat ditunjukkan menikahi Matahari, tetapi ia berbagi istri dengan musuhnya Veles, karena setiap malam Matahari dianggap terbenam ke dunia bawah, alam orang mati yang dikuasai Veles.
claims.quote: it can also be shown that Perun was married to the Sun. He, however, shared his wife with his enemy Veles, as each night the Sun was thought of as diving behind the horizon and into the underworld, the realm of the dead over which Veles ruled.

claims.statement: Perun's shrines stood on mountain tops or hills, or in sacred groves under ancient oaks, as places of worship and sacrifice (a bull, an ox, a ram and eggs).
claims.statement_id: Tempat pemujaan Perun berada di puncak gunung atau bukit, atau di hutan keramat di bawah pohon ek tua; di sana dilakukan ibadah dan persembahan berupa banteng, sapi, domba jantan, dan telur.
claims.quote: Shrines of Perun were located either on top of mountains or hills, or in sacred groves underneath ancient oaks. These were general places of worship and sacrifices (with a bull, an ox, a ram, and eggs).

claims.statement: Besides the tree, Perun was associated with a day (Thursday) and a material (tin).
claims.statement_id: Selain pohon, Perun juga dikaitkan dengan satu hari, yaitu Kamis (Thursday), dan dengan satu bahan, yaitu timah.
claims.quote: In addition to the tree association, Perun had a day association (Thursday) as well as the material association (tin).

claims.statement: He ordered the statues of Perun he had once erected to be torn down in disgrace and dragged through the streets while beaten with sticks, then cast into rivers and not allowed to land on the shore.
claims.statement_id: Ia memerintahkan agar arca-arca Perun yang dulu didirikannya sendiri dirobohkan dengan hina dan diseret di jalan sambil dipukuli tongkat, lalu dibuang ke sungai dan tidak dibiarkan terdampar di tepi.
claims.quote: He ordered that the statues of Perun which he himself had erected formerly, be dethroned, torn down with great dishonor and dragged through the streets as they were beaten with sticks. The idols were then cast into rivers and not permitted to land on the shore.

claims.statement: Perun is one of the most revered gods of Slavic neopaganism (rodnovery), seen as a thunderer, god of warriors and rival of Veles, embodying spring storms that fertilize the earth.
claims.statement_id: Perun adalah salah satu dewa yang paling dihormati dalam neopaganisme Slavia (rodnovery); ia dianggap dewa guruh, dewa para pejuang, dan saingan Veles, serta perwujudan badai musim semi yang menyuburkan bumi.
claims.quote: Perun is one of the most revered gods in Slavic neopaganism (rodnovery). He is considered a thunderer, the god of warriors, and a rival of Veles, also embodying spring thunderstorms that fertilize the earth.

claims.statement: The Baltic tribes widely worshipped the thunderer Perkunas, a main Baltic deity sharing attributes with Perun: axe amulets, a fiery four-pointed symbol and the oak as chief tree.
claims.statement_id: Suku-suku Baltik memuja dewa guruh Perkunas, salah satu dewa utama mereka, yang memiliki atribut sama dengan Perun: jimat berbentuk kapak, simbol api berujung empat, dan pohon ek sebagai pohon utama.
claims.quote: The Baltic tribes had a widespread cult of the thunderer Perkunas, one of the main deities of the Baltic pantheon. With Perun, this deity also shares common attributes (amulets in the form of an axe, a fiery four-pointed symbol, oak as the main tree)

claims.statement: Among South Slavs the mountain plant Iris germanica is known in folklore as perunika ("Perun's plant") and sometimes bogisha ("god's plant"), believed to grow from ground struck by lightning.
claims.statement_id: Di kalangan Slavia Selatan, tanaman gunung Iris germanica dikenal dalam cerita rakyat sebagai perunika ("tanaman Perun") dan kadang bogisha ("tanaman dewa"), dan dipercaya tumbuh dari tanah yang tersambar petir.
claims.quote: Among South Slavs, a mountain plant Iris germanica is known in folklore as perunika ("Perun's plant") and sometimes also as bogisha ("god's plant"), and was believed to grow from ground that had been struck by lightning.

claims.statement: Bulgarians and Macedonians believe the Bulgarian mountain Pirin, one of the highest in the Balkan Peninsula, was named after Perun.
claims.statement_id: Orang Bulgaria dan Makedonia percaya bahwa Pirin, salah satu gunung tertinggi di Semenanjung Balkan, dinamai menurut Perun.
claims.quote: The Bulgarian and Macedonian people believe that the name of the Bulgarian mountain Pirin, one of the highest mountains of the Balkan Peninsula, was named after Perun.

claims.statement: Perun is one of the principal deities of eastern and northern Slavic mythology; in pre-Christian Kyivan Rus he was the chief god, god of thunder, lightning and rain, ruler of the heavens and later god of war.
claims.statement_id: Perun adalah salah satu dewa utama dalam mitologi Slavia timur dan utara; di Rus Kyiv sebelum Kristen ia dewa tertinggi, dewa guruh, kilat, dan hujan, penguasa langit, dan kemudian dewa perang.
claims.quote: Perun. One of the principal deities in eastern and northern Slavic mythology. In pre-Christian Kyivan Rus’ this was the chief god—the god of thunder, lightning, and rain, the ruler of the heavens, and, later, the god of war.

claims.statement: In 980 a wooden statue of Perun with a silver head and golden moustache stood on Perun Hill in Kyiv; his feast, with sacrifices, took place in July.
claims.statement_id: Pada tahun 980 arca kayu Perun berkepala perak dan berkumis emas berdiri di Bukit Perun di Kyiv; hari raya Perun dirayakan dengan persembahan pada bulan Juli.
claims.quote: In 980 a wooden statue of Perun with a silver head and golden moustache stood on Perun Hill in Kyiv. Perun's feast, celebrated with sacrifices, took place in July.

claims.statement: After adopting Christianity, Prince Volodymyr the Great had Perun's statue cast into the Dnipro River and built Saint Basil's Church on its site.
claims.statement_id: Setelah memeluk Kristen, Pangeran Volodymyr (Vladimir) Agung memerintahkan arca Perun dilempar ke Sungai Dnipro dan membangun Gereja Santo Basil di tempatnya.
claims.quote: After adopting Christianity Prince Volodymyr the Great ordered Perun's statue to be cast into the Dnipro River and on its site built Saint Basil's Church.

claims.statement: The Christian church replaced the cult of Perun with that of Saint Elijah, to whom all of Perun's qualities were transferred.
claims.statement_id: Gereja Kristen menggantikan pemujaan Perun dengan pemujaan Santo Elia, yang menerima semua sifat Perun.
claims.quote: The Christian church replaced the cult of Perun with the cult of Saint Elijah (feast day: 2 August, or 20 July OS), to whom all of Perun's qualities were transferred.

claims.statement: The Lemkos still regard the expression "May Perun strike you dead" as the most terrible curse.
claims.statement_id: Orang Lemko masih menganggap ungkapan "Semoga Perun menyambarmu mati" sebagai kutukan paling mengerikan.
claims.quote: The Lemkos still consider the expression ‘May Perun strike you dead’ as the most terrible curse.

claims.statement: The author analyses Perun as a supreme storm god of Old Slavic pagan religion and mythology, correlated with rock, thunder, lightning, rain, war and justice.
claims.statement_id: Penulis menganalisis Perun sebagai dewa badai tertinggi dalam agama dan mitologi pagan Slavia Kuno, yang berkaitan dengan batu, guruh, kilat, hujan, perang, dan keadilan.
claims.quote: The author analyses Perun, a supreme Storm-God in Old-Slavic pagan religion and mythology, which is correlated to rock, thunder, lightning and rain, war and justice.

claims.statement: For more than a century, scholars of Slavic mythology have assumed a connection between the German iris (Iris germanica) and the cult of Perun.
claims.statement_id: Selama lebih dari seabad, para ahli mitologi Slavia menerima anggapan yang menghubungkan tanaman iris Jerman (Iris germanica) dengan pemujaan dewa Perun.
claims.quote: For more than a century, scholars of Slavic mythology have adopted the assumption connecting the German iris (Iris germanica) plant and the cult of the god Perun.

claims.statement: The author concludes there are no grounds for linking the plant to the cult of Perun, the thunder god; the name "perunika" comes from its feather-like (perasti) leaves.
claims.statement_id: Penulis menyimpulkan tidak ada dasar untuk mengaitkan tanaman itu dengan pemujaan Perun, dewa guruh; nama "perunika" berasal dari daunnya yang mirip bulu (perasti).
claims.quote: the author concludes that there are no grounds for linking the plant to the cult of Perun, the god of thunder. The motivation for the name “perunika” comes from its dominant feather-like (perasti) leaves

claims.statement: Perun was worshipped by the Varangian (Scandinavian) warriors hired by Oleg and Igor against Byzantium; for them the purely Slavic Perun likely replaced the Scandinavian Thor, also a thunderer.
claims.statement_id: Perun dipuja para prajurit Varangia (Skandinavia) yang disewa Oleg dan Igor dalam kampanye melawan Bizantium; kemungkinan besar bagi mereka Perun menggantikan Thor dari Skandinavia, yang juga dewa guruh.
claims.quote: Perun was worshipped by the Varangian (Scandinavian) warriors hired by Oleg and Igor during the campaigns against Byzantium ... It is likely that the purely Slavic god Perun replaced for them the Scandinavian Thor, also the thunderer.

claims.statement: Perun (Перун) is the chief god of Slavic mythology and a thunder god; in Russian he is also called Pyerun, and in Polish Piorun.
claims.statement_id: Perun (Перун) adalah dewa utama mitologi Slavia dan dewa guruh; dalam bahasa Rusia ia juga disebut Pyerun, dan dalam bahasa Polandia Piorun.
claims.quote: ペルーン（ウクライナ語 / キリル表記：Перун、ラテン表記：Perun）またはペルンは、スラヴ神話の主神であり、雷神。ロシア語ではほかにピィエルン (Pyerun)、またポーランド語ではピョルンまたはピオルン (Piorun)

claims.statement: Like many thunder gods he has the form of a bearded middle-aged man; he flies on a millstone, hurling lightning and thunder.
claims.statement_id: Seperti banyak dewa guruh lain, ia berwujud lelaki paruh baya berjanggut; ia terbang di atas batu gilingan sambil melepaskan kilat dan guruh.
claims.quote: 類似する多くの雷神と同じように、髭を生やした中年男性の姿をしている。 石臼に乗って空を飛びながら稲妻を放ち雷鳴を轟かせる。

claims.statement: The Finnic peoples had a god Ukko with functions and attributes similar to the Slavic and Baltic deities.
claims.statement_id: Bangsa-bangsa Finnik memiliki dewa Ukko dengan fungsi dan atribut yang mirip dengan dewa Slavia dan Baltik.
claims.quote: The Finnic peoples had a deity Ukko, which had similar functions and attributes with the Slavic and Baltic deities.

claims.statement: In Ivanov and Toporov's reconstruction the enmity between Perun and Veles starts with Veles's theft of Perun's son, wife or, usually, cattle; Perun attacks Veles with lightning bolts, Veles is finally killed, and whatever he stole is released as rain falling from the skies.
claims.statement_id: Menurut rekonstruksi Ivanov dan Toporov, permusuhan Perun dan Veles bermula dari pencurian putra, istri, atau terutama ternak Perun oleh Veles; Perun menyerang Veles dengan petir, Veles akhirnya dibunuh, dan apa yang dicurinya dilepaskan sebagai hujan dari langit.
claims.quote: Their enmity is, according to them, Veles's theft of Perun's son, wife, or, usually, cattle. ... Perun attacks Veles with his lightning bolts. ... In the end, he is killed by Perun and in this ritual death, whatever Veles stole is released in the form of rain falling from the skies.

claims.statement: Téra rejects the theory: there is not a single piece of evidence that Veles fought Perun, and nothing is known of Veles's draconic or serpentine nature.
claims.statement_id: Téra menolak teori itu: tidak ada satu bukti pun bahwa Veles melawan Perun, dan tidak diketahui apa pun tentang sifat naga atau ularnya.
claims.quote: "We have not a single piece of evidence that Veles fought Perun, and we know nothing about Veles’s draconic or serpentine nature."

claims.statement: According to Lyle, Vala is equated with Veles in the Slavic context, and his opponent, corresponding to Indra, is Perun, the thunder god.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Lyle, Vala disamakan dengan Veles dalam konteks Slavia, dan lawannya, setara dengan Indra, adalah Perun sang dewa guruh.
claims.quote: Vala is equated with Veles in the Slavic context and his opponent, corresponding to Indra, is Perun, the thunder god

claims.statement: In the form of the story Lyle postulates, Perun, as a bird of prey at the top of the tree, can fly and attacks and defeats Veles, after which all the other young gods of light are freed.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bentuk kisah yang diandaikan Lyle, Perun sebagai burung pemangsa di puncak pohon dapat terbang, menyerang dan mengalahkan Veles, lalu semua dewa terang lainnya dibebaskan.
claims.quote: However, Perun, as bird of prey (eagle or falcon) at the top of the tree, can fly and he attacks and defeats Veles, after which, ... in this postulated form of the story, all the other young gods of light are freed.

claims.statement: Lyle herself calls the form of the story speculative for now, hoping further evidence may clarify it.
claims.statement_id: Lyle sendiri menyebut bentuk kisah itu masih spekulatif, dengan harapan bukti lebih lanjut dapat menjelaskannya.
claims.quote: The actual form of the story is speculative at present, although it can be hoped that further evidence may be adduced that will clarify it,

claims.statement: In the 971 treaty quoted from the Primary Chronicle, the Rus swear that if they break it they may be cursed by Perun and Volos and cut down by their own weapons.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kutipan perjanjian 971 dari Kronik Utama, pihak Rus bersumpah bahwa bila melanggar mereka terkutuk oleh Perun dan Volos dan akan ditebas oleh senjata mereka sendiri.
claims.quote: As I have sworn to the Greek emperors, and with me the boyars and all Rus’, so shall we uphold the true treaty. And if we do not fulfill anything of what has been stated above, I and those who are subject to me, may we be cursed by our god in whom we believe, by Perun and by Volos ... may we be cut down by our own weapons.

claims.statement: Besides his firestone arrows, Perun had an equally destructive weapon: mythical golden apples, which in many Slavic folk accounts are a talisman of ultimate destruction.
claims.statement_id: Selain panah api batu, Perun memiliki senjata yang tak kalah merusak: apel emas mitos, yang dalam banyak kisah rakyat Slavia menjadi jimat kehancuran pamungkas.
claims.quote: Perun also had another type of weapon in his arsenal, as destructive as his firestone arrows, but even more unusual: mythical golden apples. ... the golden apple appears as a talisman of ultimate destruction.

claims.statement: Human sacrifices to Perun, one boy and one girl, were chosen by lot.
claims.statement_id: Persembahan manusia untuk Perun, seorang anak laki-laki dan seorang anak perempuan, dipilih dengan undian.
claims.quote: Human sacrifices to Perun (one boy and girl) were chosen by lot.

claims.statement: According to the Primary Chronicle, when the pagans of Kyivan Rus made an agreement with Byzantium they swore an oath to Perun.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Kronik Utama, ketika orang-orang pagan Rus Kyiv membuat perjanjian dengan Bizantium, mereka bersumpah demi Perun.
claims.quote: According to the Primary Chronicle, when the pagans of Kyivan Rus’ entered into an agreement with Byzantium, they swore an oath to Perun.

claims.statement: In Slavic folklore the rusalka (русалка) is a female entity, often malicious toward people and frequently associated with water; counterparts elsewhere in Europe include the French Melusine and the Germanic Nixie.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Slavia, rusalka (русалка) adalah sosok perempuan yang sering memusuhi manusia dan sering dikaitkan dengan air; padanannya di Eropa lain antara lain Melusine dari Prancis dan Nixie dari dunia Jermanik.
claims.quote: In Slavic folklore, the rusalka (plural: rusalki; Cyrillic: русалка, Russian pronunciation ... is a female entity, often malicious toward mankind and frequently associated with water. It has counterparts in other parts of Europe, such as the French Melusine and the Germanic Nixie.

claims.statement: In northern Russia the rusalka was also known by names such as vodyanitsa; in Ukraine she was called a mavka.
claims.statement_id: Di Rusia utara rusalka juga dikenal dengan berbagai nama seperti vodyanitsa; di Ukraina ia disebut mavka.
claims.quote: In northern Russia, the rusalka was also known by various names such as the vodyanitsa ... In Ukraine, the rusalka was called a mavka.

claims.statement: The term "rusalka" derives from "rusalija", which entered Slavic via Byzantine Greek "rousália" from the Latin "Rosālia", a name for Pentecost and the adjacent days.
claims.statement_id: Istilah "rusalka" berasal dari "rusalija", yang masuk ke bahasa Slavia melalui bahasa Yunani Bizantium "rousália" dari kata Latin "Rosālia", nama untuk Pentakosta dan hari-hari di sekitarnya.
claims.quote: The term "Rusalka" derives from "rusalija" ... which entered Slavic languages, via Byzantine Greek "rousália" ... from the Latin "Rosālia" as a name for Pentecost and the days adjacent to it.

claims.statement: According to Vladimir Propp, pagan Slavs linked rusalki with fertility and did not consider them evil before the 19th century; they came out of the water in spring to bring life-giving moisture to the fields.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Vladimir Propp, bangsa Slavia pagan mengaitkan rusalka dengan kesuburan dan tidak menganggapnya jahat sebelum abad ke-19; rusalka keluar dari air pada musim semi untuk membawa kelembapan pemberi kehidupan ke ladang.
claims.quote: According to Vladimir Propp, the original "rusalka" was an appellation used by pagan Slavic peoples, who linked them with fertility and did not consider rusalki evil before the 19th century. They came out of the water in the spring to transfer life-giving moisture to the fields

claims.statement: In 19th-century versions the rusalka is a restless, dangerous being no longer alive, associated with the unclean spirit.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi abad ke-19, rusalka adalah makhluk yang sudah mati, gelisah, dan berbahaya, yang dikaitkan dengan roh najis.
claims.quote: In 19th-century versions, a rusalka is an unquiet, dangerous being who is no longer alive, associated with the unclean spirit.

claims.statement: Most stories say the soul of a young woman who died in or near a river or lake returns to haunt it; this undead rusalka is not always malevolent and may die in peace if her death is avenged.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kebanyakan cerita, arwah perempuan muda yang mati di atau dekat sungai atau danau kembali menghantui perairan itu; rusalka mayat hidup ini tidak selalu jahat dan dapat mati dengan tenang bila kematiannya dibalas.
claims.quote: It is accounted by most stories that the soul of a young woman who had died in or near a river or a lake would come back to haunt that waterway. This undead rusalka is not invariably malevolent, and would be allowed to die in peace if her death is avenged.

claims.statement: Her main purpose is to lure young men with her looks or voice into the depths, entangle their feet in her long hair and drown them.
claims.statement_id: Tujuan utamanya adalah memikat pemuda dengan rupa atau suaranya ke kedalaman perairan, lalu menjerat kaki mereka dengan rambut panjangnya dan menenggelamkan mereka.
claims.quote: Her main purpose is, however, to lure young men, seduced by either her looks or her voice, into the depths of said waterways where she would entangle their feet with her long hair and submerge them.

claims.statement: They killed their victims by tickling them to death or forcing them into a frenzied dance.
claims.statement_id: Mereka membunuh korban dengan menggelitikinya sampai mati atau memaksanya ikut serta dalam tarian yang liar.
claims.quote: They killed their victims by tickling them to death or forcing them to participate in a frenzied dance.

claims.statement: In Ukrainian stories rusalki were often linked with water, in Belarus with forest and field; usually pictured as beautiful naked maidens, in some areas they were hideous and hairy.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita dari Ukraina rusalka sering dikaitkan dengan air, di Belarus dengan hutan dan ladang; biasanya mereka digambarkan sebagai gadis cantik tanpa busana, tetapi di beberapa daerah sebagai makhluk buruk rupa dan berbulu.
claims.quote: In stories from Ukraine, they were often linked with water. In Belarus they were linked with the forest and field. They were usually pictured as beautiful naked maidens, but in some areas they were imagined as hideous and hairy.

claims.statement: Rusalki were believed most dangerous during Rusalka Week in early June, when they left the water to swing on birch and willow branches at night.
claims.statement_id: Rusalka dipercaya paling berbahaya pada Pekan Rusalka di awal Juni, ketika mereka keluar dari air untuk berayun di dahan pohon birch dan willow pada malam hari.
claims.quote: The rusalki were believed to be at their most dangerous during the 'Rusalka week' ... in early June. At this time, they were supposed to have left their watery depths in order to swing on branches of birch and willow trees by night.

claims.statement: Swimming that week was strictly forbidden, lest a swimmer be dragged to the river bed.
claims.statement_id: Selama pekan itu berenang dilarang keras, agar perenang tidak diseret ke dasar sungai.
claims.quote: Swimming during this week was strictly forbidden, lest mermaids drag a swimmer down to the river bed.

claims.statement: According to a folklorist, the dominant image today is mermaid-like but with legs rather than a fish tail; formerly she was more complex, closer to a nature spirit found by water, in fields, forests and mountains.
claims.statement_id: Menurut seorang ahli folklor, gambaran yang kini dominan menyerupai putri duyung tetapi berkaki, bukan berekor ikan; dulu gambarannya lebih rumit dan lebih mirip roh alam yang ditemukan di dekat air, ladang, hutan, dan gunung.
claims.quote: the currently dominant presents her as something like a mermaid, though she is pictured as having legs rather than a fish tail ... In the past, her image was more complex and she more closely resembled a nature spirit, found not only near water but in fields, forests, and mountains, rather like the vila

claims.statement: In 1901 Antonín Dvořák composed the opera Rusalka.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1901 Antonín Dvořák menggubah opera Rusalka.
claims.quote: 1901 – Rusalka, an opera by Antonín Dvořák.

claims.statement: In most traditions the rusalka is a fish-woman living on the river bed, arising from women who died in the river.
claims.statement_id: Menurut sebagian besar tradisi, rusalka adalah perempuan ikan yang tinggal di dasar sungai dan berasal dari perempuan yang meninggal di sungai.
claims.quote: Menurut sebagian besar tradisi, rusalka merupakan perempuan ikan, yang tinggal di dasar sungai. Rusalka berasal dari para perempuan yang meninggal di sungai.

claims.statement: The rusalka cannot stay long above water, but her comb can produce water to wet her hair; if her hair dries, she dies.
claims.statement_id: Rusalka tidak bisa lama di atas permukaan air, tetapi sisirnya dapat mengeluarkan air untuk membasahi rambutnya; jika rambutnya kering, rusalka akan mati.
claims.quote: Rusalka tidak bisa tinggal lama di atas permukaan, tetapi sisir mereka bisa mengeluarkan air untuk membasahi rambut mereka, jika rambutnya kering maka rusalka akan mati.

claims.statement: In most beliefs rusalki always have loose hair, which can be fair, black, greenish or completely green.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kebanyakan kepercayaan rambut rusalka selalu terurai, dan warnanya bisa pirang, hitam, kehijauan, atau hijau sepenuhnya.
claims.quote: In most beliefs rusalki always have loose hair ... The hair of the rusalka can be fair, black, greenish or completely green.

claims.statement: Veles, also known as Volos, is a chthonic underworld god of Slavic mythology, called a cattle god (skotij bogъ) in contemporary sources, though various hypotheses give him a much broader sphere.
claims.statement_id: Veles, juga dikenal sebagai Volos, adalah dewa dunia bawah dalam mitologi Slavia; sumber sezaman menyebutnya dewa ternak (skotij bogъ), tetapi menurut berbagai hipotesis wilayah kuasanya jauh lebih luas.
claims.quote: Veles, also known as Volos, is a chthonic god of the underworld in Slavic mythology, described in contemporary sources as a cattle god (skotij bogъ), but according to various hypotheses, he had a much broader sphere of influence.

claims.statement: His role as protector of cattle may link to wealth and rule of the underworld, imagined as a pasture where souls grazed; comparatively he can be read as a god of magic, knowledge, divination and poetry.
claims.statement_id: Fungsinya sebagai pelindung ternak mungkin berkaitan dengan kekayaan dan kekuasaan atas dunia bawah, yang dibayangkan sebagai padang rumput tempat jiwa manusia merumput; lewat perbandingan, ia dapat ditafsirkan sebagai dewa sihir, pengetahuan, ramalan, dan puisi.
claims.quote: His function as protector of cattle may be connected to both wealth and rule of the underworld, which was imagined as a pasture where human souls grazed. Through comparative methods, he can be interpreted as a deity of magic, knowledge, divination, and poetry.

claims.statement: As guardian of the boundary between the living and the dead, he was also god of the wilderness, hunting and animals; he guaranteed oaths, punishing breakers by "turning them yellow".
claims.statement_id: Sebagai penjaga batas antara dunia orang hidup dan orang mati, ia juga dewa alam liar, perburuan, dan hewan; ia menjamin sumpah dan menghukum pelanggarnya dengan "membuat mereka menguning".
claims.quote: As the guardian of the boundary between the world of the living and the dead, he was also a god of the wilderness, hunting and animals. He was also a guarantor of oaths, punishing their violation by "turning them yellow"

claims.statement: According to the Life of Vladimir, he ordered the idol of Volos, called the cattle god, thrown into the Pochaiv River.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Riwayat Vladimir, ia memerintahkan agar berhala Volos, yang disebut dewa ternak, dilempar ke Sungai Pochaiv.
claims.quote: He commanded that the idol of Volos, whom they called the cattle god, be thrown into the Pochaiv River

claims.statement: Veles is sometimes wrongly identified with a dragon or serpent, a hypothesis from Ivanov and Toporov's reconstruction published in 1974.
claims.statement_id: Veles kadang keliru disamakan dengan naga atau ular; hipotesis ini berasal dari rekonstruksi Ivanov dan Toporov yang terbit pada 1974.
claims.quote: Veles is sometimes incorrectly identified with a dragon or a serpent. This hypothesis, based on the reconstruction by Ivanov and Toporov and published in 1974

claims.statement: In that reconstruction Veles as a serpent slithers from underworld caves up the world tree toward Perun's domain; Perun strikes with lightning, Veles flees by hiding or turning into trees, animals or people, and is finally killed by Perun.
claims.statement_id: Dalam rekonstruksi itu, Veles berwujud ular merayap dari gua dunia bawah dan melilit naik pohon dunia Slavia menuju wilayah Perun; Perun menyerangnya dengan petir, Veles lari dengan bersembunyi atau berubah menjadi pohon, hewan, atau manusia, dan akhirnya dibunuh Perun.
claims.quote: They present Veles, in the form of a serpent, who slithers from the caves of the underworld and coils up the Slavic world tree towards Perun's heavenly domain. Perun attacks Veles with his lightning bolts. Veles flees, hiding or transforming himself into trees, animals or people. In the end, he is killed by Perun

claims.statement: The theory was later rejected even by its author Toporov; for Slavic mythology it conjectures a conflict between Perun and Veles.
claims.statement_id: Teori ini kemudian ditolak bahkan oleh pencetusnya sendiri, Toporov; dalam mitologi Slavia teori itu menduga adanya konflik antara Perun dan Veles.
claims.quote: It was later rejected even by its own author Toporov. In terms of Slavic mythology, it conjectures the conflict between the two gods, Perun and Veles.

claims.statement: The Pleiades are most likely connected with Veles in some Slavic languages, e.g. Old Russian Volosyni or Bulgarian Vlascite.
claims.statement_id: Gugus bintang Pleiades dalam beberapa bahasa Slavia kemungkinan besar berkaitan dengan Veles, misalnya Volosyni dalam bahasa Rusia Kuno atau Vlascite dalam bahasa Bulgaria.
claims.quote: The constellation of the Pleiades is most likely connected with Veles in some Slavic languages, such as Old Russian Volosyni or Bulgarian Vlascite

claims.statement: His mythological nature and powers resemble, though not identically, those of Varuna, Velnias, Odin (marginally), Hermes, Afsati and Hades.
claims.statement_id: Sifat dan kekuatan mitologisnya mirip, meski tidak sepenuhnya identik, dengan Varuna, Velnias, Odin (sedikit), Hermes, Afsati, dan Hades.
claims.quote: His mythological nature and powers are similar, though not entirely identical, to those of Varuna, Velnias, Odin (marginally), Hermes, Afsati and Hades.

claims.statement: Veles is depicted as a horned serpent with a long beard.
claims.statement_id: Veles digambarkan sebagai ular bertanduk dengan janggut panjang.
claims.quote: Veles wird als gehörnte Schlange mit einem langen Bart dargestellt.

claims.statement: After Christianization Veles was reinterpreted as the Devil, appearing so in proverbs; Saint Blasius took over his role as cattle protector, probably due to the similar name.
claims.statement_id: Setelah Kristenisasi, Veles ditafsirkan ulang sebagai Iblis (Teufel) dan namanya muncul dalam peribahasa; peran pelindung ternak diambil alih Santo Blasius, mungkin karena kemiripan nama.
claims.quote: Nach der Christianisierung wurde Veles zum Teufel umgedeutet, sein Name taucht in dieser Funktion in Sprichwörtern auf. Die Rolle des Viehbeschützers übernahm, vermutlich aufgrund der Namensähnlichkeit, der Heilige Blasius.

claims.statement: In the treaty with Byzantium the Rus swore to be cursed by Perun and by Volos, the cattle god, and become yellow as gold if they broke it.
claims.statement_id: Dalam perjanjian dengan Bizantium, orang Rus bersumpah: semoga kami dikutuk oleh dewa kami, oleh Perun dan oleh Volos, dewa ternak, dan menjadi kuning seperti emas bila melanggar.
claims.quote: may we be cursed by our god in whom we believe, by Perun and by Volos, the cattle god (skotij bogъ), and may we become yellow as gold

claims.statement: Svarog is a Slavic god perhaps associated with fire and smithing, once read as a sky god on a now-rejected etymology; he is named only in the Primary Chronicle, problematic to interpret, as the Slavic equivalent of the Greek Hephaestus.
claims.statement_id: Svarog adalah dewa Slavia yang mungkin berkaitan dengan api dan pandai besi, dan dulu ditafsirkan sebagai dewa langit berdasarkan etimologi yang kini ditolak; ia hanya disebut dalam Primary Chronicle, yang sulit ditafsirkan, sebagai padanan Slavia dewa Yunani Hephaestus.
claims.quote: Svarog is a Slavic god who may be associated with fire and blacksmithing and who was once interpreted as a sky god on the basis of an etymology rejected by modern scholarship. He is mentioned in only one source, the Primary Chronicle, which is problematic in interpretation. He is presented there as the Slavic equivalent of the Greek god Hephaestus.

claims.statement: The root svar derives from Proto-Slavic *sъvarъ, made of the prefix *sъ- "good, own" and the stem *varъ "fire, heat".
claims.statement_id: Akar svar berasal dari Proto-Slavia *sъvarъ, terdiri atas awalan *sъ- yang berarti "baik, milik sendiri" dan akar *varъ yang berarti "api, panas".
claims.quote: The root svar derives from the Proto-Slavic *sъvarъ, which consists of the prefix *sъ- meaning "good, (ones') own" and the stem *varъ "fire, heat"

claims.statement: The *sъvarъ stem is also the origin of words related to blacksmithing.
claims.statement_id: Akar *sъvarъ juga menjadi asal kata-kata yang berkaitan dengan pekerjaan pandai besi.
claims.quote: The *sъvarъ stem is also the origin of words related to blacksmithing.

claims.statement: In the Slavic translation of the Chronicle of John Malalas, glosses render Hephaestus, Greek god of fire and smithing, as Svarog, and his son the sun god Helios as Dazhbog.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan Slavia Kronik John Malalas, glos menerjemahkan Hephaestus, dewa api dan pandai besi Yunani, sebagai Svarog, dan putranya, dewa matahari Helios, sebagai Dazhbog.
claims.quote: In this translation, in glosses, the Greek god of fire and smithing Hephaestus is translated as Svarog, and his son, the sun god Helios, is translated as Dazhbog

claims.statement: During the reign of this Hephaestus (Svarog) in Egypt, tongs fell from the sky and he began to forge weapons, since before then people beat each other with sticks and stones.
claims.statement_id: Pada masa pemerintahan Hephaestus (Svarog) di Mesir, sebuah penjepit jatuh dari langit dan ia mulai menempa senjata, karena sebelumnya orang saling memukul dengan tongkat dan batu.
claims.quote: During the reign of this Hephaestus in Egypt, at the time of his reign, tongs fell from the sky and he began to forge weapons, as before that they beat each other with sticks and stones.

claims.statement: After Christianization Svarog was preserved in toponymy and vocabulary.
claims.statement_id: Setelah Kristenisasi, nama Svarog bertahan dalam nama tempat dan kosakata.
claims.quote: After Christianization, Svarog was preserved in toponymy and vocabulary.

claims.statement: In the Russian dialect of Novgorod the obsolete word svarog, meaning "fire" and "blacksmith", survives.
claims.statement_id: Dalam dialek Rusia Novgorod masih tersimpan kata usang svarog yang berarti "api" dan "pandai besi".
claims.quote: In the Russian dialect (Novgorod) the obsolete word сва́рог, svarog meaning "fire" and "blacksmith", is preserved.

claims.statement: According to the glosses Svarog is the Slavic equivalent of Hephaestus, father of Dazhbog, and creator of monogamy.
claims.statement_id: Menurut glos tersebut, Svarog adalah padanan Slavia Hephaestus, ayah Dazhbog, dan pencipta aturan perkawinan monogami.
claims.quote: According to the glosses Svarog is: (1) the Slavic equivalent of Hephaestus, the Greek god of fire and smithing, (2) the father of Dazhbog, and (3) the creator of monogamy.

claims.statement: Some scholars suggest Svarozhits means "young Svarog" or is a diminutive of Svarog, but most disagree, as the suffix -its, -ich is usually patronymic.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian ahli menduga Svarozhits berarti "Svarog muda" atau bentuk kecil dari Svarog, tetapi kebanyakan ahli tidak setuju karena akhiran -its, -ich biasanya akhiran patronimik.
claims.quote: Some scholars have suggested that Svarozhits means 'young Svarog' or is a diminutive of Svarog. ... However, most scholars disagree with this interpretation. The suffix -its, -ich (from Proto-Slavic *-iťь) is most often a patronymic suffix

claims.statement: Svarog (Russian: Сварог) is a sun god in Slavic mythology, and also a fire spirit or god.
claims.statement_id: Svarog (bahasa Rusia: Сварог) adalah dewa matahari dalam mitologi Slavia, sekaligus roh atau dewa api.
claims.quote: スヴァローグ（ロシア語: Сварог、 古東スラヴ語: Сварогъ、 英語: Svarog）とはスラヴ神話における太陽神であり、火の精霊または神でもある。

claims.statement: Aleksander Gieysztor interpreted Svarog as celestial fire (the sun), Perun as atmospheric fire (the thunderbolt) and Svarozhits-Dazhbog as earthly fire.
claims.statement_id: Aleksander Gieysztor menafsirkan Svarog sebagai api langit (matahari), Perun sebagai api di udara (petir), dan Svarozhits-Dazhbog sebagai api bumi.
claims.quote: Aleksander Gieysztor interpreted Svarog as celestial fire (the sun), Perun as atmospheric fire (the thunderbolt), and Svarozhits-Dazhbog as earthly fire (fire).

claims.statement: In Polish the name Svarog is Swaróg.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Polandia nama Svarog adalah Swaróg.
claims.quote: bahasa Polandia: Swaróg , bahasa Kroasia: Svarog

claims.statement: In Slavic mythology the vodyanoy (водяной, literally "he from the water" or "watery") is a water spirit; Czech and Slovak tales call him vodník (Hastrman), Ukrainian tales vodyanyk.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Slavia, vodyanoy (водяной, harfiah "yang dari air" atau "berair") adalah roh air; dalam dongeng Ceko dan Slowakia ia disebut vodník (Hastrman), dan dalam dongeng Ukraina vodyanyk.
claims.quote: In Slavic mythology, vodyanoy (Russian: водяной , IPA ... lit. '[he] from the water' or 'watery') is a water spirit. In Czech and Slovak fairy tales, he is called vodník (or in Germanized form: Hastrman ), and often referred to as Wassermann in German sources. In Ukrainian fairy tales, he is called “водяник“ (vodyanyk).

claims.statement: He may appear as a naked, pot-bellied, bald man with a hat and belt of reeds, while other accounts give him green hair and a long green beard and many depictions show him as a man-like frog; the variety is attributed to his shape-shifting.
claims.statement_id: Ia bisa tampil sebagai lelaki telanjang berperut buncit dan botak bertopi serta bersabuk alang-alang, sementara kisah lain memberinya rambut hijau dan janggut hijau panjang, dan banyak penggambaran menjadikannya katak berwujud manusia; perbedaan ini dikaitkan dengan kemampuannya berubah wujud.
claims.quote: He may appear to be a naked man with a pot belly (and bald-headed) wearing a hat and belt of reeds and rushes, conflicting with other accounts ascribing him green hair and a long green beard, while many depictions restore him as an anthropormophic frog. The varying look has been attributed in commentary to his shape-shifting ability.

claims.statement: When angered the vodyanoy breaks dams, washes away mills and drowns people and animals, so fishermen, millers and bee-keepers sacrifice to appease him; he sometimes drags people to his underwater dwelling as slaves.
claims.statement_id: Saat marah, vodyanoy menjebol bendungan, menghanyutkan kincir air, dan menenggelamkan manusia serta hewan, sehingga nelayan, penggiling, dan peternak lebah memberinya persembahan; kadang ia menyeret orang ke kediamannya di bawah air untuk dijadikan budak.
claims.quote: When angered, the vodyanoy breaks dams, washes down water mills, and drowns people and animals. Consequently, fishermen, millers, and also bee-keepers make sacrifices to appease him. The vodyanoy would sometimes drag people down to his underwater dwelling to serve him as slaves.

claims.statement: In Russia the vodyanoy is sometimes called dedushka vodyanoy ("Water-Grandfather") or vodyanik.
claims.statement_id: Di Rusia vodyanoy kadang disebut dedushka vodyanoy ("Kakek Air") atau vodyanik.
claims.quote: In Russia, the vodyanoy is sometimes called the dedushka vodyanoy (Дѣдушка-водяной , "Water-Grandfather") or vodyanik (водяник ).

claims.statement: He is said to dwell in a slough, kettle hole or whirlpool of a river, pond or lake, and especially liked to live near a watermill.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikatakan tinggal di lubuk, cekungan, atau pusaran sungai, kolam, atau danau, dan terutama suka tinggal di dekat kincir air.
claims.quote: He is said to dwell in a slough (омут ), kettle hole (Котловина ), or a whirlpool of a river, pond or lake, and liked especially to live near a watermill.

claims.statement: He can shape-shift, which has been suggested to explain his varied descriptions.
claims.statement_id: Ia mampu berubah wujud, dan hal ini diajukan sebagai penjelasan atas gambaran rupanya yang beragam.
claims.quote: He has the capability of shape-shifting, which has been suggested as an explanation of its varied descriptions.

claims.statement: When a watermill is built, a pig, cattle, sheep or even a human (or a chicken) must be sacrificed to appease the vodyanik.
claims.statement_id: Ketika kincir air dibangun, harus dipersembahkan babi, sapi, domba, bahkan manusia (atau ayam) untuk menenangkan vodyanik.
claims.quote: When a watermill is built, a sacrifice of pig, cattle, sheep, or even human (or a chicken) must be made to appease the vodyanik.

claims.statement: A fisherman can also gain the vodyanoy's boon of a bountiful catch, for example after returning a child accidentally netted.
claims.statement_id: Nelayan juga bisa mendapat anugerah vodyanoy berupa tangkapan berlimpah di jaringnya, misalnya setelah mengembalikan anak yang tak sengaja terjaring.
claims.quote: The fisherman can also benefit from the boon of the vodyanoy, receiving a bountiful harvest in their fishing nets. He may receive this reward after returning a child which was accidentally netted.

claims.statement: The vodyanik "owns" all fish and aquatic creatures, which explains his ability to deliver fish; he especially chooses the wels catfish as his mount.
claims.statement_id: Vodyanik "memiliki" semua ikan dan makhluk air, dan kuasa itu menjelaskan kemampuannya memberi ikan; ia terutama memilih ikan lele besar (wels catfish) sebagai tunggangan.
claims.quote: The vodyanik "owns" all the fish and aquatic creatures, and his control over them explains his ability to deliver fish. The vodyanik selects in particular the sheatfish (сом ; Silurus glanis, aka "wels catfish") as his mount to ride on.

claims.statement: He takes a wife or wives: water-nymphs or drowned, unhappy girls cursed by their parents; according to Afanasyev the water-nymph is known in Russia by various names, including rusalka.
claims.statement_id: Ia beristri satu atau lebih, yaitu peri air atau gadis malang yang tenggelam dan dikutuk ayah atau ibunya; menurut Afanasyev, peri air itu dikenal di Rusia dengan berbagai nama, termasuk rusalka.
claims.quote: He is known to take on a wife (or wives), and espouses "water-nymphs or drowned and unhappy girls who have been cursed by their fathers or mothers". According to Afanasyev, the "water-nymph" ("water-maiden") is known by various names in Russia, including the rusalka.

claims.statement: Vodyanoys are believed to have a ruler, the Tsar Vodyanik, an old man with a club who can rise to the sky on a black cloud and create new rivers and lakes.
claims.statement_id: Para vodyanoy dipercaya punya penguasa, Tsar Vodyanik, lelaki tua bersenjata gada yang dapat naik ke langit di atas awan hitam dan menciptakan sungai serta danau baru.
claims.quote: It is believed that vodyanoys have a ruler: the Tsar Vodyanik, or the Vodyan Tsar. He is described as an old man armed with a club, who can rise to the sky sitting on a black cloud and create new rivers and lakes.

claims.statement: A farmer fording his livestock makes a sign of the cross over the river as protection against this.
claims.statement_id: Petani yang menyeberangkan ternaknya membuat tanda salib di atas sungai sebagai perlindungan agar ternaknya tidak ditunggangi vodyanik.
claims.quote: The farmer fording his livestock will make a sign of cross (emblem of Perun's weapon) over the river as protection from this happening.

claims.statement: He is also described as an old man with green hair and a long green beard, which whitens as the moon wanes, as the immortal vodyanoy ages or rejuvenates with the moon's phases.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga digambarkan sebagai lelaki tua berambut dan berjanggut hijau panjang; janggutnya memutih saat bulan menyusut, karena vodyanoy yang abadi menua atau menjadi muda lagi mengikuti fase bulan.
claims.quote: He is also described as an old man with green hair and (long) green beard The green beard turns white with when the moon wanes, as the immortal Vodyanoy ages or rejuvenates with the phases of the moon.

claims.statement: He can appear as a giant moss-covered fish, a log or even a small-winged flying tree trunk skimming the water.
claims.statement_id: Ia dapat muncul sebagai ikan raksasa berlumut, sebatang kayu, bahkan batang pohon terbang bersayap kecil yang meluncur di atas permukaan air.
claims.quote: He can appear as a giant moss-covered fish, a log or even a flying tree-trunk with small-wings, skimming over the water's surface.

claims.statement: Czech and Slovak vodníci can also look like ordinary humans, but water often drips from their clothes, making the disguise easy to spot.
claims.statement_id: Vodník Ceko dan Slowakia juga bisa tampil sebagai manusia biasa, tetapi pakaiannya sering meneteskan air sehingga penyamarannya mudah dikenali.
claims.quote: The Czech and Slovak vodníci (plural of vodník) can also take on an appearance of ordinary humans, but often with water dripping from their clothing, which makes their false identity easily discernable.

claims.statement: The vodyanoy was believed to cause people to drown.
claims.statement_id: Vodyanoy dipercaya menjadi penyebab orang tenggelam.
claims.quote: Vodyanoy dipercaya sebagai penyebab orang tenggelam.

claims.statement: Perkūnas was the common Baltic thunder god and second most important deity after Dievas; in Lithuanian and Latvian myth he is documented as god of sky, thunder, lightning, storms, rain, fire, war, law, order, fertility, mountains and oak trees.
claims.statement_id: Perkūnas (Perkūns, Parkuns) adalah dewa guruh bersama bangsa Baltik dan dewa terpenting kedua setelah Dievas; dalam mitologi Lituania dan Latvia ia tercatat sebagai dewa langit, guruh, petir, badai, hujan, api, perang, hukum, ketertiban, kesuburan, gunung, dan pohon ek.
claims.quote: was the common Baltic god of thunder, and the second most important deity in the Baltic pantheon after Dievas. In both Lithuanian and Latvian mythology, he is documented as the god of sky, thunder, lightning, storms, rain, fire, war, law, order, fertility, mountains, and oak trees.

claims.statement: The theonym is said to come from the root *per- "to beat" or *perkʷ- "oak", so it can be translated literally as "the Striker" or "the Lord of Oaks".
claims.statement_id: Nama dewa ini dikatakan berasal dari akar *per- "memukul" atau *perkʷ- "pohon ek", sehingga dapat diterjemahkan secara harfiah "Sang Pemukul" atau "Penguasa Pohon Ek".
claims.quote: This theonym is said to derive from the root *per- "to beat" or from root *perkʷ- "oak", and the theonym itself was later given various extensions in different languages. Therefore, the theonym can be literally translated as "the Striker" or "the Lord of Oaks".

claims.statement: Most information on Perkūnas comes from folk songs, legends and tales mostly collected late, in the 19th century; Lithuanian Perkūnas has many onomatopoeic names, such as Dundulis.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian besar keterangan tentang Perkūnas berasal dari lagu rakyat, legenda, dan dongeng yang kebanyakan baru dikumpulkan pada abad ke-19; Perkūnas Lituania punya banyak nama tiruan bunyi, misalnya Dundulis.
claims.quote: Most information about Perkūnas comes from folklore songs, legends, and fairy tales. Because most of them were collected rather late in the 19th century ... Lithuanian Perkūnas has many alternative onomatopoeic names, like Dundulis

claims.statement: Perkūnas is mentioned in many sources on Lithuanian religion and mythology.
claims.statement_id: Perkūnas disebut dalam banyak sumber tentang agama dan mitologi Lituania.
claims.quote: Perkūnas minimas daugelyje lietuvių religijos ir mitologijos šaltinių.

claims.statement: Perkūnas is pictured as middle-aged, armed with an axe and arrows, riding a two-wheeled goat-drawn chariot, like Thor or the Celtic Taranis.
claims.statement_id: Perkūnas digambarkan sebagai lelaki paruh baya bersenjata kapak dan anak panah, mengendarai kereta beroda dua yang ditarik kambing, seperti Thor atau Taranis dari Kelt.
claims.quote: Perkūnas is pictured as middle-aged, armed with an axe and arrows, riding a two-wheeled chariot harnessed with goats, like Thor or Celtic Taranis.

claims.statement: In the Prussian triad of gods Perkūnas symbolizes the height of fertile (and vegetative) forces, manliness, success and cosmic elements: sky, rain, thunder and lightning.
claims.statement_id: Dalam trias dewa Prusia, Perkūnas melambangkan puncak kekuatan kesuburan (termasuk tumbuhan), kejantanan, keberhasilan, dan unsur kosmos: langit, hujan, guruh, dan petir.
claims.quote: Prūsų dievų trejete Perkūnas simbolizuoja aukščiausią derlingų (ir vegetatyvinių) jėgų pakilimą, vyriškumą, sėkmę, kosmologinius elementus – dangų, lietų, griaustinį, žaibą.

claims.statement: His weapons include an axe or sledgehammer, stones, a sword, lightning bolts, a bow and arrows, a club and an iron or fiery knife.
claims.statement_id: Senjata Perkūnas antara lain kapak atau palu godam, batu, pedang, petir, busur dan panah, gada, serta pisau besi atau berapi.
claims.quote: They include an axe or sledgehammer, stones, a sword, lightning bolts, a bow and arrows, a club, and an iron or fiery knife.

claims.statement: He fights the devil and evil forces; folklore most often says Perkūnas lives between heaven and earth, in the clouds, ruling thunder and lightning.
claims.statement_id: Perkūnas bertarung melawan iblis (velnias) dan kekuatan jahat; dalam cerita rakyat ia paling sering dikisahkan tinggal di antara langit dan bumi, di awan, dan memerintah guruh dan petir.
claims.quote: Kovoja su velniu, piktosiomis galiomis. Tautosakos kūriniuose dažniausiai pasakojama, kad Perkūnas gyvena tarp dangaus ir žemės, debesyse, valdo griaustinį ir žaibus.

claims.statement: He has a two-wheeled cart drawn by horses or goats, and as he drives across the sky the rumble of its (usually iron) wheels causes thunder.
claims.statement_id: Ia punya kereta beroda dua yang ditarik kuda atau kambing, dan saat ia melaju di langit derak rodanya (biasanya dari besi) menimbulkan guruh.
claims.quote: Turi dvirates vežėčias, pakinkytas žirgais arba ožiais, jomis važinėjasi dangumi taip, kad jo ratų (dažniausiai geležinių) dardėjimas sukelia griaustinį.

claims.statement: Folk works most often tell that Perkūnas lives between heaven and earth, in the clouds, and rules thunder and lightning.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat paling sering dikisahkan bahwa Perkūnas tinggal di antara langit dan bumi, di awan, dan memerintah guruh dan petir.
claims.quote: Tautosakos kūriniuose dažniausiai pasakojama, kad Perkūnas gyvena tarp dangaus ir žemės, debesyse, valdo griaustinį ir žaibus.

claims.statement: Perkūnas is also connected to Thursday, the Thunderer's day in many traditions, and early sources associate him with the Roman god Jupiter.
claims.statement_id: Perkūnas juga dikaitkan dengan hari Kamis (Thursday), hari Sang Penguruh dalam banyak tradisi, dan dalam sumber awal ia disamakan dengan dewa Romawi Jupiter.
claims.quote: Perkūnas is also connected to Thursday. Thursday is the day of the Thunderer in many traditions ... Perkūnas is associated with the Roman god Jupiter in early sources.

claims.statement: Thursday was held to be Perkūnas's day, when some farm work was forbidden.
claims.statement_id: Kamis dianggap hari Perkūnas, dan pada hari itu sebagian pekerjaan pertanian dilarang.
claims.quote: Perkūno diena laikytas ketvirtadienis, tą dieną buvo draudžiama dirbti kai kuriuos žemės ūkio darbus

claims.statement: Perkūnas is the Baltic god of lightning, one of the most important Baltic gods, serving as god of thunder, rain, mountains, oak trees and the sky in Lithuanian and Latvian mythology.
claims.statement_id: Perkūnas (Pērkons, Parkuns) adalah dewa petir Baltik, salah satu dewa terpenting dalam mitologi Baltik, yang berperan sebagai dewa guntur, hujan, pegunungan, pohon ek, dan langit dalam mitologi Lituania dan Latvia.
claims.quote: adalah dewa petir Baltik dan merupakan salah satu dewa paling penting dalam mitologi Baltik. Ia berperan sebagai dewa guntur, hujan, pegunungan, pohon ek dan langit dalam mitologi Lituania dan Latvia.

claims.statement: In Latvian mythology Perkūnas is called Father Perkūnas, Old Father and Dievulis; he brings storms, foul weather and rain, and folklore links him with the Sun, his wife.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Latvia, Perkūnas disebut Bapa Perkūnas (Tėvas Perkūnas), Bapa Tua, dan Dievulis; ia bertugas mendatangkan badai, cuaca buruk, dan hujan, dan dalam cerita rakyat dikaitkan dengan Matahari (Saulė) sebagai istrinya.
claims.quote: Latvių mitologijoje Perkūnas vadinamas Tėvu Perkūnu, Senuoju tėvu, Dievuliu. Jam priskiriama audros, darganų, lietaus sukėlimo funkcija. Tautosakoje siejamas su Saule, Perkūno mote

claims.statement: Smoczyński suggests the base form is the eastern dialect word perū́nas, "lightning", borrowed from Middle Belarusian.
claims.statement_id: Smoczyński mengusulkan bahwa bentuk dasarnya adalah kata dialek timur perū́nas, "petir", yang dipinjam dari bahasa Belarus Pertengahan.
claims.quote: Smoczyński suggests that the basic form is the dialectal (eastern) word perū́nas "lightning", which is borrowed from Middle Belarusian

claims.statement: Sometimes seven or nine Perkūnai are called brothers; Lithuanian says "Perkūnų yra daug" ("there are many thunders").
claims.statement_id: Kadang disebut tujuh atau sembilan Perkūnai bersaudara; dalam bahasa Lituania dikatakan "Perkūnų yra daug" ("ada banyak guruh").
claims.quote: Sometimes there are seven or nine Perkūnai referred to as brothers. It is said in Lithuanian "Perkūnų yra daug" ("there are many thunders").

claims.statement: Perkūnas fights the devil and evil powers.
claims.statement_id: Perkūnas bertarung melawan iblis (velnias) dan kekuatan-kekuatan jahat.
claims.quote: Kovoja su velniu, piktosiomis galiomis.

claims.statement: In some plots the devil steals Perkūnas's stone or axe; some researchers read this as a mythic struggle between the sky and the chthonic world.
claims.statement_id: Ada kisah ketika iblis (velnias) mencuri batu atau kapak Perkūnas; sebagian peneliti menafsirkannya sebagai pertarungan mitis antara langit dan dunia bawah.
claims.quote: Yra siužetų, kuriuose velnias pavagia iš Perkūno akmenį arba kirvį. Jie kai kurių tyrinėtojų aiškinami kaip mitinė dangaus ir chtoniškojo pasaulio kova

claims.statement: The etymology of the name is unclear; it is linked to Latin quercus, "oak", or derived from Lithuanian perti, "to beat, to strike".
claims.statement_id: Etimologi namanya tidak jelas; dikaitkan dengan kata Latin quercus, "pohon ek", atau diturunkan dari kata Lituania perti, "memukul, menghantam".
claims.quote: Vardo etimologija nėra aiški, siejamas su lotynų kalbos žodžiu quercus – ąžuolas; kildinamas iš lietuvių kalbos žodžio perti – mušti, smogti.

claims.statement: In some folklore records Thursday is explained as Perkūnas's wedding day, which never happened because the devil stole his bride.
claims.statement_id: Dalam beberapa catatan cerita rakyat, Kamis dijelaskan sebagai hari pernikahan Perkūnas yang batal karena iblis mencuri pengantinnya. Kadang pula disebut ada tujuh atau sembilan Perkūnai bersaudara.
claims.quote: Kai kuriuose tautosakos užrašymuose ketvirtadienis aiškinamas ir kaip vestuvių diena, kurios neįvyko velniui pavogus Perkūno nuotaką.

claims.statement: The main linguistic evidence for the reconstructed thunder god is said to include the Baltic thunder god Perkun and the Slavic thunder god Perun.
claims.statement_id: Bukti linguistik utama untuk dewa guruh rekonstruksi itu dikatakan antara lain dewa guruh Baltik Perkun dan dewa guruh Slavia Perun.
claims.quote: The main linguistic evidence is said to be the Baltic god of thunder Perkun , the Slavic god of thunder Perun

claims.statement: In folklore he is depicted as an elderly but still strong, tall, red-bearded man.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat ia digambarkan sebagai lelaki tua yang masih kuat, tinggi, dan berjanggut merah.
claims.quote: Tautosakoje vaizduojamas kaip senyvas, bet dar stiprus, aukštas rudabarzdis vyras

claims.statement: A taboo on Perkūnas's name is thought to have existed; to avoid saying it, people used onomatopoeic substitutes such as Brazdeikis and Dundulis.
claims.statement_id: Diduga ada tabu menyebut nama Perkūnas; untuk menghindarinya, ia disebut dengan nama pengganti tiruan bunyi seperti Brazdeikis dan Dundulis.
claims.quote: Manoma, egzistavo Perkūno vardo tabu. Vengiant tarti jo vardą, jis būdavo vadinamas garsažodinės kilmės vardo pakaitalais: Brazdeikiu, Dunduliu

claims.statement: The Alkonost (Алконост) is a legendary woman-headed bird in Russian folklore, related to the Sirin.
claims.statement_id: Alkonost (Алконост) adalah burung legendaris berkepala perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Rusia, berkerabat dengan Sirin.
claims.quote: is a legendary woman-headed bird in Russian folklore, related to the Sirin.

claims.statement: The Alkonost possibly originated from Xrafstar in Persian folklore.
claims.statement_id: Alkonost mungkin berasal dari Xrafstar dalam cerita rakyat Persia.
claims.quote: It possibly originated from Xrafstar in Persian folklore.

claims.statement: The Alkonost often symbolises good things like happiness and paradise, while the Sirin symbolises negative forces like natural disasters and misfortune.
claims.statement_id: Alkonost sering melambangkan hal-hal baik seperti kebahagiaan dan surga, sedangkan Sirin melambangkan kekuatan negatif seperti bencana alam dan kemalangan.
claims.quote: The Alkonost often symbolizes positive things like happiness and paradise, while the Sirin tends to symbolize negative forces like natural disasters and misfortune.

claims.statement: Both creatures are associated with foretelling or causing death; the Alkonost, with many other bird-human hybrids, is said to live in Rai, where the dead live.
claims.statement_id: Kedua makhluk dikaitkan dengan meramalkan atau mendatangkan kematian; Alkonost, bersama banyak makhluk campuran burung-manusia lain, dikatakan tinggal di Rai, tempat orang mati.
claims.quote: Both creatures are associated with foretelling or causing death. The Alkonost, along with many other mythological bird human hybrids, is said to live in Rai, where the dead live.

claims.statement: The Alkonost sings beautiful songs; those who hear them forget everything they know and want nothing more ever again.
claims.statement_id: Alkonost menyanyikan lagu yang indah, dan yang mendengarnya melupakan semua yang diketahuinya dan tidak menginginkan apa pun lagi.
claims.quote: The Alkonost sings beautiful songs, and those who hear these songs forget everything they know and want nothing more ever again.

claims.statement: The Alkonost lays eggs on a beach and rolls them into the sea; while they are in the ocean there are no storms or disasters, but their hatching causes very violent storms.
claims.statement_id: Alkonost bertelur di pantai lalu menggulirkan telurnya ke laut; selama telur di laut tidak ada badai atau bencana, tetapi saat menetas timbul badai yang sangat dahsyat.
claims.quote: The Alkonost lays her eggs on a beach and then rolls them into the sea. During the time when the eggs are in the ocean, there are no storms or disasters. However, when the eggs hatch, the hatching causes very violent storms.

claims.statement: The Alkonost became popular when Christianity reached Russia, as it was believed to be a messenger from God to take away the pain of hardship, or was used to represent the human soul ascending to Heaven.
claims.statement_id: Alkonost menjadi populer saat agama Kristen masuk ke Rusia karena diyakini sebagai utusan Tuhan untuk menghapus derita kesusahan, atau dipakai sebagai lambang jiwa manusia yang naik ke surga.
claims.quote: The Alkonost became a popular figure when Christianity was introduced in Russia, as the Alkonost was believed to be a messenger from God meant to take away the pain of hardship. Alternately, the Alkonost was used to represent the human soul ascending to Heaven.

claims.statement: According to folk tales, on the morning of the Apple Feast of the Saviour the Sirin flies into the orchard and weeps; in the afternoon the Alkonost flies there rejoicing and laughing, and brushes dew from its wings, granting healing powers to all fruits on its tree.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita rakyat, pada pagi pesta apel Juru Selamat Sirin terbang ke kebun apel dan menangis; sore harinya Alkonost terbang ke sana, bergembira dan tertawa, lalu mengibaskan embun dari sayapnya sehingga semua buah di pohon tempatnya bertengger mendapat daya penyembuh.
claims.quote: According to folk tales, on the morning of the Apple Feast of the Saviour, the Sirin flies into the apple orchard and cries sadly. In the afternoon, the Alkonost flies to this place, beginning to rejoice and laugh. The Alkonost brushes dew from her wings, granting healing powers to all fruits on the tree she is sitting on.

claims.statement: The name derives from Greek ἀλκυών, "kingfisher"; the Alkonost is a sea bird symbolising God's providence and mercy, a mythical bird of paradise from Byzantine and Slavic literary legends.
claims.statement_id: Nama ini berasal dari kata Yunani ἀλκυών, "raja-udang"; Alkonost adalah burung laut yang melambangkan pemeliharaan dan belas kasih Tuhan, burung surga mitos dari legenda tertulis Bizantium dan Slavia.
claims.quote: от греч. ἀλκυών — зимородок) — морская птица, символизирующая Божий промысел и Божие милосердие; мифическая райская птица из книжных византийских и славянских легенд.

claims.statement: The Alkonost lays eggs on the seashore, sinks them into the deep and makes the sea calm for six days; its song is so beautiful that whoever hears it forgets everything in the world.
claims.statement_id: Alkonost bertelur di tepi laut, membenamkan telurnya ke kedalaman laut dan membuat laut tenang selama enam hari; nyanyiannya begitu indah sehingga yang mendengarnya melupakan segala hal di dunia.
claims.quote: Алконост несёт яйца на берегу моря, погружает их в глубину моря и делает его спокойным на шесть дней. Пение этой птицы настолько прекрасно, что услышавший его забывает обо всём на свете.

claims.statement: The figure arose from the ancient Greek myth of Alcyone, turned by the gods into a kingfisher.
claims.statement_id: Sosok ini muncul dari mitos Yunani kuno tentang Alkione, yang diubah para dewa menjadi burung raja-udang.
claims.quote: Образ возник из древнегреческого мифа об Алкионе, превращённой богами в зимородка.

claims.statement: The Russian lubok depicts the Alkonost as half bird, half woman with large feathers of various colours, a crown on its head and flowers of paradise in its hands.
claims.statement_id: Lubok Rusia menggambarkan Alkonost sebagai setengah burung setengah perempuan dengan bulu besar beraneka warna, kepala bermahkota dan memegang bunga surga.
claims.quote: Русский лубок изображает Алконоста полуптицей-полуженщиной с большими перьями, имеющими различную окраску. Голову венчает корона, в руках — райские цветы.

claims.statement: Because the phrase "the alkuon is a sea bird" was read as "alkuonest sea bird", the name "Alkonost" first appeared and then became fixed in Old Russian literature.
claims.statement_id: Karena frasa "alkuon adalah burung laut" terbaca sebagai "alkuonest burung laut", nama "Alkonost" untuk pertama kali muncul dan kemudian mapan dalam sastra Rusia Kuno.
claims.quote: в котором в результате прочтения «алкуон(ъ) есть морская птица» как «алкуонестъ морская птица» впервые читается имя «Алконост», закрепившееся в древнерусской литературе.

claims.statement: The Alkonosts are magical birds of happiness and hope, opposed to the Sirin, birds of grief and sorrow; the Alkonosts are well disposed to people, the Sirin less so.
claims.statement_id: Alkonost adalah burung ajaib kebahagiaan dan harapan, berlawanan dengan Sirin, burung duka dan kesedihan; Alkonost bersikap baik kepada manusia, Sirin kurang.
claims.quote: Die Alkonosty sind die magischen Vögel des Glücks und der Hoffnung. Im Gegensatz dazu stehen die Sirin, die Vögel der Trauer und des Kummers. Die Alkonosty sind den Menschen gut gesinnt, die Sirin hingegen weniger.

claims.statement: For the Russian Orthodox Church the Alkonost personifies the divine will; it lives in Paradise and leaves only to bring messages to our world.
claims.statement_id: Bagi Gereja Ortodoks Rusia, Alkonost adalah personifikasi kehendak ilahi; ia tinggal di surga dan hanya meninggalkannya untuk menyampaikan pesan ke dunia kita.
claims.quote: Für die Russisch-Orthodoxe Kirche ist die Alkonost die Personifikation des göttlichen Willens. Sie lebt im Paradies und verlässt es nur, um in unserer Welt Botschaften zu überbringen.

claims.statement: The sea then calms for six or seven days and is stirred up by a storm as soon as the young hatch.
claims.statement_id: Setelah telur diletakkan, laut tenang selama enam atau tujuh hari dan diguncang badai begitu anak-anaknya menetas.
claims.quote: Daraufhin beruhigt sich die See für sechs oder sieben Tage und wird durch einen Sturm aufgewirbelt, sobald die Jungen schlüpfen.

claims.statement: The Alkonost is a minor character in the opera The Legend of the Invisible City of Kitezh and the Maiden Fevroniya.
claims.statement_id: Alkonost adalah tokoh kecil dalam opera The Legend of the Invisible City of Kitezh and the Maiden Fevroniya.
claims.quote: The Alkonost is a minor character from the opera The Legend of the Invisible City of Kitezh and the Maiden Fevroniya

claims.statement: The Alkonost dwells on the paradise river Euphrates (Евфрат) and is often mentioned with another bird of paradise, the Sirin.
claims.statement_id: Alkonost berdiam di sungai surgawi Efrat (Евфрат) dan sering disebut bersama burung surga lain, Sirin.
claims.quote: Обитает на райской реке Евфрат. Часто упоминается вместе с другой райской птицей — Сирином.

claims.statement: Alkonost is featured in the digital card game Mythgard (2019) as a rare minion in the Dreni faction.
claims.statement_id: Alkonost muncul dalam gim kartu digital Mythgard (2019) sebagai kartu langka di faksi Dreni.
claims.quote: Alkonost is featured in the digital card game Mythgard (2019) as a rare minion in the Dreni faction.

claims.statement: Jarilo, also Yaryla, Yarilo, Iarilo, Juraj, Jurij or Gerovit, is an alleged East and South Slavic god of vegetation, fertility and springtime.
claims.statement_id: Jarilo, juga disebut Yaryla, Yarilo, Iarilo, Juraj, Jurij, atau Gerovit, adalah dewa vegetasi, kesuburan, dan musim semi Slavia Timur dan Selatan yang keberadaannya masih diduga.
claims.quote: alternatively Yaryla, Yarilo, Iarilo, Juraj, Jurij, or Gerovit, is an alleged East and South Slavic god of vegetation, fertility and springtime.

claims.statement: The Proto-Slavic root *jarъ means "spring" or "summer", "strong", "furious", "imbued with youthful life-force".
claims.statement_id: Akar kata Proto-Slavia *jarъ berarti "musim semi" atau "musim panas", "kuat", "garang", "penuh daya hidup muda".
claims.quote: means "spring" or "summer", "strong", "furious", "imbued with youthful life-force".

claims.statement: Jarilo is a Slavic mythological and ritual character tied to fertility, above all spring fertility, and sexual power, and the personification of one of the summer festivals in the Russian folk calendar.
claims.statement_id: Jarilo adalah tokoh mitologi dan ritual Slavia yang terkait dengan gagasan kesuburan, terutama kesuburan musim semi, dan daya seksual, serta personifikasi salah satu perayaan musim panas dalam kalender rakyat Rusia.
claims.quote: славянский мифологический и ритуальный персонаж, связанный с идеей плодородия, прежде всего весеннего, и сексуальной мощи, персонификация одного из летних праздников в русском народном календаре

claims.statement: By another interpretation Jarilo is a Slavic deity of spring fertility; contrary to popular belief, he was not a sun god.
claims.statement_id: Menurut tafsiran lain, Jarilo adalah dewa Slavia untuk kesuburan musim semi; berlawanan dengan anggapan umum, ia bukan dewa matahari.
claims.quote: по другой интерпретации славянское божество весеннего плодородия. Вопреки распространённому мнению, Ярила не был богом солнца.

claims.statement: Jarilo has a special role in agricultural rites, especially in spring; his figure resembles Kostroma, Kostrubonka and the Maslenitsa effigy.
claims.statement_id: Jarilo berperan khusus dalam upacara pertanian, terutama musim semi; sosoknya mirip dengan Kostroma (Кострома), Kostrubonka, dan boneka jerami Maslenitsa (Масленица).
claims.quote: Ярила играет особую роль в сельскохозяйственной обрядности, особенно весенней. Образ Ярилы сходен с образами Костромы, Кострубоньки, чучела Масленицы.

claims.statement: In a Kostroma village an effigy called Jarilo was laid in a coffin and carried around the village by an old man in rags, with lamentation instead of songs, and then buried in the field.
claims.statement_id: Di sebuah desa Kostroma, boneka bernama Jarilo dimasukkan ke peti mati dan diarak keliling desa oleh lelaki tua berpakaian compang-camping, diiringi ratapan alih-alih nyanyian, lalu dikubur di ladang.
claims.quote: Так, в Костромской деревне такое чучело под названием Ярило клали в гроб и давали носить по деревне старику, которого одевали в лохмотья, а вместо песен было оплакивание. После этого Ярило зарывали в поле.

claims.statement: The authentic sources on Jarilo are Great Russian and describe a festival dedicated to him.
claims.statement_id: Sumber autentik tentang Jarilo berasal dari Rusia Raya (великорусские) dan menggambarkan perayaan yang dipersembahkan untuknya.
claims.quote: Аутентичные источники по Яриле — великорусские. В них описывается посвящённое Яриле празднество.

claims.statement: Jarilo (Ярила), or Jarovit, also Yarilo, is in Slavic mythology the son of the thunder god Perun and his wife the goddess Mokosch, and the sun god of the Russian-speaking area.
claims.statement_id: Jarilo (Ярила), juga Jarovit atau Yarilo, dalam mitologi Slavia adalah putra dewa guntur Perun dan istrinya, dewi Mokosch, serta dewa matahari di wilayah berbahasa Rusia.
claims.quote: Jarilo (russ: Ярила) oder Jarovit, auch Yarilo ist in der slawischen Mythologie Sohn des Donnergottes Perun und seiner Gattin, der Göttin Mokosch und der Sonnengott im Russischen Sprachraum.

claims.statement: Jarilo's animal form is a horse, and he is associated with the colour green (vegetation).
claims.statement_id: Wujud hewan Jarilo adalah kuda, dan ia dikaitkan dengan warna hijau (vegetasi).
claims.quote: Seine Tiergestalt ist ein Pferd und er wird mit der Farbe grün (Vegetation) assoziiert.

claims.statement: In the yearly cycle Jarilo comes to unite in sacred marriage with his sister Mara/Morana and so unleash spring fertility.
claims.statement_id: Dalam siklus tahunan Jarilo datang untuk bersatu dalam pernikahan suci dengan saudarinya Mara/Morana dan dengan demikian melepaskan kesuburan musim semi.
claims.quote: um sich mit seiner Schwester Mara/Morana in heiliger Ehe zu vereinen und dadurch die Fruchtbarkeit im Frühling zu entfesseln.

claims.statement: His Christian interpretation is Saint George (Georg) and John (Johannes).
claims.statement_id: Dalam tafsiran Kristen, Jarilo dipadankan dengan Santo Georg dan Yohanes (Johannes).
claims.quote: Seine christliche Interpretation sind der Heilige Georg und Johannes

claims.statement: The only historical source naming this god is a 12th-century biography of the German bishop Otto of Bamberg.
claims.statement_id: Satu-satunya sumber sejarah yang menyebut dewa ini adalah biografi abad ke-12 tentang uskup Jerman Otto dari Bamberg.
claims.quote: Satu-satunya sumber bersejarah yang menyebutkan dewa ini adalah biografi abad ke-12 seorang uskup Jerman, Otto dari Bamberg.

claims.statement: Until the 19th century in Russia, Belarus and Serbia, a folk festival called Jarilo was held in late spring or early summer.
claims.statement_id: Hingga abad ke-19 di Rusia, Belarusia, dan Serbia, festival rakyat bernama Jarilo dirayakan pada akhir musim semi atau awal musim panas.
claims.quote: Sampai abad ke-19 di Rusia, Belarusia, dan Serbia, festival rakyat yang disebut Jarilo dirayakan pada akhir musim semi atau awal musim panas.

claims.statement: This youthful life-force was held sacred in Slavic pre-Christian religion, so the god personifying it was called Jarovit, or hypocoristically Jarilo.
claims.statement_id: Daya hidup muda ini dianggap suci dalam agama Slavia pra-Kristen, sehingga dewa yang mempersonifikasikannya disebut Jarovit, atau dengan nama akrab Jarilo.
claims.quote: This youthful life-force was considered sacred in the Slavic pre-Christian religion and the god personifying this sacred force was thus called Jarovit, or hypocoristically Jarilo.

claims.statement: In northern Croatia and southern Slovenia, especially White Carniola, a similar spring festival called Jurjevo, Zeleni Juraj or Zeleni Jurij (Green George) is dedicated to St. George.
claims.statement_id: Di Kroasia utara dan Slovenia selatan, khususnya White Carniola, festival musim semi serupa bernama Jurjevo, Zeleni Juraj, atau Zeleni Jurij (George Hijau) dipersembahkan untuk St. George.
claims.quote: Di Kroasia utara dan Slovenia selatan, khususnya White Carniola, festival musim semi serupa disebut Jurjevo, Zeleni Juraj atau Zeleni Jurij (George Hijau), yang sesuai namanya, didedikasikan untuk St. George

claims.statement: Mokosh is a Slavic goddess with no surviving narratives; she was named in sermons against paganism with the vilas but not described, and all modern descriptions are reconstructions.
claims.statement_id: Mokosh adalah dewi Slavia yang kisahnya tidak bertahan; ia disebut dalam khotbah-khotbah anti-pagan bersama para vila tanpa dijelaskan, dan semua gambaran modern tentangnya adalah rekonstruksi.
claims.quote: is a Slavic goddess. No narratives about this deity have survived: Mokosh was mentioned in various sermons (called Words and Teachings) against Paganism along with the vilas, but is not described by them, and all modern descriptions are reconstructions.

claims.statement: In academia the view spread that Mokosh's cult passed to the folk-Christian Paraskeva Friday, the personification of Friday associated with water and spinning.
claims.statement_id: Di kalangan akademik tersebar pendapat bahwa kultus Mokosh beralih kepada Paraskeva Friday dalam Kristen rakyat, personifikasi hari Jumat yang dikaitkan dengan air dan pemintalan.
