claims.quote: In academia, the opinion has spread that the cult of Mokosh has passed to the folk-Christian Paraskeva Friday, the personification of Friday associated with water and spinning.

claims.statement: Later studies criticised the identification with Paraskeva, because her link with spinning, water and Friday has Christian rather than pagan roots.
claims.statement_id: Kajian lanjutan mengkritik penyamaan dengan Paraskeva karena kaitan Paraskeva dengan pemintalan, air, dan hari Jumat berakar Kristen, bukan pagan.
claims.quote: In later studies, the idea of an identification with Paraskeva was criticized because Paraskeva's association with spinning, water, and Friday has Christian rather than pagan roots.

claims.statement: By etymological reconstruction Mokosh was a goddess of waters and fertility; most researchers say she was later reflected in bylinas and zagovory as Mat Zemlya, the personification of Earth in East Slavic folklore.
claims.statement_id: Menurut rekonstruksi etimologis, Mokosh adalah dewi air dan kesuburan; menurut sebagian besar peneliti, ia kemudian tercermin dalam bylina dan zagovory sebagai Mat Zemlya, personifikasi Bumi dalam cerita rakyat Slavia Timur.
claims.quote: According to etymological reconstruction, Mokosh was the goddess of waters and fertility. Later, according to most researchers, she was reflected in bylinas and zagovory as Mat Zemlya, the personification of Earth in East Slavic folklore.

claims.statement: At the end of the 19th century kikimora was recorded as Mokusha or Mokosha in the Russian North; this is explained by the kikimora being a demonised version of the goddess.
claims.statement_id: Pada akhir abad ke-19, di Rusia Utara tercatat nama kikimora sebagai Mokusha atau Mokosha; kesamaan ini dijelaskan dengan menganggap kikimora versi dewi ini yang dijadikan iblis.
claims.quote: at the end of the 19th century, the names kikimora as Mokusha or Mokosha were recorded in the Russian North. The coincidence is explained by kikimora being a demonized version of the goddess

claims.statement: Researchers have portrayed Mokosh as a goddess of love and birth, linked with night, the moon, spinning, sheep farming and women's economy.
claims.statement_id: Para peneliti menggambarkan Mokosh sebagai dewi cinta dan kelahiran yang terkait dengan malam, bulan, pemintalan, peternakan domba, dan ekonomi perempuan.
claims.quote: researchers have portrayed Mokosh as the goddess of love and birth, with a connection to night, the moon, spinning, sheep farming and women's economy.

claims.statement: This reconstruction conflicts with the etymological data, which show spinning could not have been her main role.
claims.statement_id: Rekonstruksi ini bertentangan dengan data etimologi, yang menunjukkan pemintalan tidak mungkin menjadi peran utama sang dewi.
claims.quote: This reconstruction disagrees with data on her etymology, which shows spinning could not have been the deity's main role.

claims.statement: The Slavic version of the basic myth theory depicts Mokosh as Perun's wife who cheated on him with Veles, so Perun killed her children; the theory is not recognised in academia.
claims.statement_id: Versi Slavia dari teori mitos dasar menggambarkan Mokosh sebagai istri Perun yang berselingkuh dengan Veles sehingga Perun membunuh anak-anak Mokosh; teori ini tidak diakui kalangan akademik.
claims.quote: based on ethnographic and linguistic data, depicts Mokosh as Perun's wife. It is believed Mokosh cheated on Perun with Veles, causing Perun to kill Mokosh's children. The theory has not been recognized in academia.

claims.statement: By the most reasonable and widespread etymology the name was formed from the Proto-Slavic stem *mok- "wet" with the suffix *-ošь; Vladimir Toporov and Vyacheslav Ivanov call this indisputable, reading the name as "She who is wet".
claims.statement_id: Menurut etimologi yang paling masuk akal dan tersebar luas, nama ini dibentuk dari akar Proto-Slavia *mok- "basah" dengan akhiran *-ošь; Vladimir Toporov dan Vyacheslav Ivanov menganggapnya tak terbantahkan dan mengartikan namanya "dia yang basah".
claims.quote: According to the most-reasonable and widespread etymology the theonym was formed by the suffixal method from the Proto-Slavic stem *mok- meaning "wet" with the suffix *-ošь. Vladimir Toporov and Vyacheslav Ivanov comment this etymology is "indisputable", understanding her name as "She who is wet".

claims.statement: In Old East Slavic texts the name Mokosh is written Mokošĭ (мокошь) and Mokŭšĭ (мокъшь).
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks Slavia Timur Kuno, nama Mokosh ditulis Mokošĭ (мокошь) dan Mokŭšĭ (мокъшь).
claims.quote: In Old East Slavic texts, the name Mokosh is rendered as Mokošĭ ( мокошь ), Mokŭšĭ ( мокъшь )

claims.statement: Unlike Macha, Mokosh was not a warrior, but from the 16th century her name was used for witches and healers, suggesting a possible role as a prophetess.
claims.statement_id: Berbeda dengan Macha, Mokosh bukan pejuang, tetapi sejak abad ke-16 namanya dipakai untuk menyebut penyihir dan penyembuh, yang menandakan kemungkinan fungsi sebagai peramal.
claims.quote: Mokosh, unlike Macha, was not a warrior, but from the 16th century her name was used to refer to witches and healers, indicating a possible function as a prophetess.

claims.statement: Celtologist Viktor Kalygin likened Mokosh to the Irish goddess Macha, originally in his view a fertility goddess.
claims.statement_id: Ahli Kelt Viktor Kalygin menyamakan Mokosh dengan dewi Irlandia Macha, yang menurutnya semula dewi kesuburan.
claims.quote: Celtologist Viktor Kalygin approximated Mokosh to the Irish goddess Macha, in his opinion originally the goddess of fertility.

claims.statement: With the Polabian goddess Siva, Mokosh (Mokosch) is the only historically attested female deity of the Slavic pantheon, and as mother goddess she oversees fertility, womanhood and the protection of sheep, spinning and weaving.
claims.statement_id: Bersama dewi Polabia Siva, Mokosh (Mokosch) adalah satu-satunya dewi yang terbukti secara historis dalam jajaran dewa Slavia, dan sebagai dewi ibu ia mengurus kesuburan, kewanitaan, serta perlindungan domba, pemintalan, dan tenun.
claims.quote: Sie ist neben der polabischen Göttin Siva die einzige bekannte historisch belegbare weibliche Gottheit des slawischen Pantheons und als Muttergöttin zuständig für Fruchtbarkeit, Weiblichkeit und den Schutz der Schafe und des Spinnens und Webens.

claims.statement: Mokosh was one of six deities for whom Prince Vladimir I set up statues in Kiev (Kiew) in 980, so she was one of the chief gods of the East Slavs.
claims.statement_id: Mokosh termasuk enam dewa yang patungnya didirikan Pangeran Vladimir I di Kiev (Kiew) pada tahun 980, sehingga ia tergolong dewa utama Slavia Timur.
claims.quote: Mokosch war eine der sechs Gottheiten, denen Fürst Vladimir I. 980 in Kiew Standbilder aufstellen ließ. Sie zählte also zu den Hauptgöttern der Ostslawen.

claims.statement: After Christianisation the protection of fields and livestock that had been Mokosh's task passed to Saint Paraskeva.
claims.statement_id: Setelah Kristenisasi, perlindungan ladang dan ternak yang menjadi tugas Mokosh dialihkan kepada Santa Paraskeva.
claims.quote: Nach der Christianisierung wurde der Schutz der Felder und des Viehs, der Mokosch oblag, der Heiligen Paraskeva übertragen.

claims.statement: In the 16th century women were still asked at confession whether they went to Mokosh.
claims.statement_id: Pada abad ke-16 perempuan masih ditanya dalam pengakuan dosa apakah mereka pergi kepada Mokosh.
claims.quote: Doch noch im 16. Jahrhundert wurden Frauen bei der Beichte gefragt, ob sie zu Mokosch gingen

claims.statement: Until the 19th century North Russian and Ukrainian folklore knew a female demon called Mokusch, with a big head and long hands, who came to peasant houses at night and spun loose fibre.
claims.statement_id: Hingga abad ke-19, cerita rakyat Rusia Utara dan Ukraina mengenal iblis perempuan bernama Mokusch, berkepala besar dan bertangan panjang, yang datang ke rumah petani pada malam hari dan memintal serat yang tergeletak.
claims.quote: bis zum 19. Jahrhundert hielt sich in der nordrussischen und ukrainischen Folklore die Vorstellung eines weiblichen Dämons namens Mokusch, mit großem Kopf und langen Händen, der nachts in die Bauernhäuser kam und das Werg spann, das offen herumlag

claims.statement: In written sources she is usually mentioned together with water spirits, the vilas (Vilen) and later the rusalkas (Rusalken).
claims.statement_id: Dalam sumber tertulis Mokosh biasanya disebut bersama roh air, yaitu vila (Vilen) dan kemudian rusalka (Rusalken).
claims.quote: In den schriftlichen Quellen wird sie meist zusammen mit Wassergeistern erwähnt, den Vilen, später den Rusalken.

claims.statement: She thus symbolises the "moist Mother Earth" and corresponds to the Iranian fertility goddess Ardvi Sur Anahita.
claims.statement_id: Karena itu Mokosh melambangkan "Ibu Bumi yang lembap" dan sepadan dengan dewi kesuburan Iran Ardvi Sur Anahita.
claims.quote: Sie symbolisiert demnach die „feuchte Mutter Erde“ und entspricht damit der iranischen Fruchtbarkeitsgöttin Ardvi Sur Anahita.

claims.statement: Svetovit, also Sventovit and Svantovit, is the god of abundance and war, chief god of the Slavic Rani tribe and later of all the Polabian Slavs.
claims.statement_id: Svetovit, juga dikenal sebagai Sventovit dan Svantovit, adalah dewa kelimpahan dan perang, dewa tertinggi suku Slavia Rani dan kemudian seluruh Slavia Polabia.
claims.quote: Svetovit, also known as Sventovit and Svantovit amongst other variants, is the god of abundance and war, and the chief god of the Slavic tribe of the Rani, and later of all the Polabian Slavs.

claims.statement: His organised cult was on the island of Rügen at Cape Arkona, where his main temple was also located.
claims.statement_id: Pemujaan terorganisasinya berada di pulau Rügen, di Tanjung Arkona, tempat kuil utamanya juga berada.
claims.quote: His organized cult was located on the island of Rügen, at Cape Arkona, where his main temple was also located.

claims.statement: According to medieval chroniclers, the god's statue had four heads and held a horn and a sword; a white horse, a saddle, a bit, a flag and eagles were dedicated to him.
claims.statement_id: Menurut penulis kronik abad pertengahan, patung dewa ini berkepala empat serta memegang tanduk dan pedang; kuda putih, pelana, tali kekang, panji, dan elang dipersembahkan kepadanya.
claims.quote: According to the descriptions of medieval chroniclers, the statue representing this god had four heads and held a horn and a sword. Dedicated to the deity were a white horse, a saddle, a bit, a flag, and eagles.

claims.statement: Once a year after the harvest a great festival was held for him; priests divined with the god's horn and horse, and at night the god himself rode a horse to fight his enemies.
claims.statement_id: Sekali setahun setelah panen diadakan perayaan besar untuknya; para pendeta meramal dengan tanduk dan kuda milik sang dewa, dan pada malam hari sang dewa sendiri menunggang kuda melawan musuh-musuhnya.
claims.quote: Once a year, after the harvest, a large festival was held in his honor. With the help of a horn and a horse belonging to the god, the priests carried out divinations, and at night the god himself rode a horse to fight his enemies.

claims.statement: His name can be translated "Strong Lord" or "Holy Lord"; it was often wrongly believed that his cult derived from St. Vitus.
claims.statement_id: Namanya dapat diterjemahkan "Tuan yang Kuat" atau "Tuan yang Suci"; dahulu sering keliru dipercaya bahwa kultus Svetovit berasal dari Santo Vitus.
claims.quote: His name can be translated as "Strong Lord" or "Holy Lord". In the past it was often mistakenly believed that the cult of Svetovit originated from St. Vitus.

claims.statement: Scholars of Slavic mythology often regard Svetovit as a Polabian hypostasis of the pan-Slavic god Perun; his cult was destroyed in 1168 by the Danes under Bishop Absalon and King Valdemar the Great.
claims.statement_id: Di kalangan ahli mitologi Slavia, Svetovit sering dianggap perwujudan Polabia dari dewa pan-Slavia Perun; kultusnya dihancurkan pada tahun 1168 oleh orang Denmark di bawah Uskup Absalon dan Raja Valdemar Agung.
claims.quote: Among scholars of Slavic mythology, Svetovit is often regarded as a Polabian hypostasis of Pan-Slavic god Perun. His cult was destroyed in 1168 by the Danes under Bishop Absalon and King Valdemar the Great.

claims.statement: The reading Sviatovid/Svietovid (Polish Światowid), "God seeing the four directions of the world", is entirely wrong and was invented by 19th-century Polish Romantics.
claims.statement_id: Bacaan Sviatovid/Svietovid (Polandia: Światowid), "dewa yang melihat empat penjuru dunia", sepenuhnya keliru dan diciptakan kaum Romantik Polandia abad ke-19.
claims.quote: A completely incorrect reading is Sviatovid / Svietovid (Polish Światowid) "God seeing the four directions of the world" invented by 19th century Polish Romantics

claims.statement: The prevailing view is that Proto-Slavic *svętъ meant "strong, mighty" and acquired the religious meaning "holy, sacred" only under Christian influence.
claims.statement_id: Pandangan yang dominan menyatakan bahwa *svętъ dalam bahasa Proto-Slavia berarti "kuat, perkasa" dan baru memperoleh makna religius "suci" karena pengaruh Kristen.
claims.quote: The prevailing view in the literature is that *svętъ in Proto-Slavic language meant "strong, mighty", and only under the influence of Christianity did it acquire the religious meaning of "holy, sacred".

claims.statement: Nowadays this view is sometimes criticised, and it is suggested that "holy, sacred" is the original Proto-Slavic meaning.
claims.statement_id: Kini pandangan itu kadang dikritik, dan diusulkan bahwa makna "suci" adalah makna asli Proto-Slavia.
claims.quote: Nowadays, however, this view is sometimes criticized and it is suggested that the meaning of "holy, sacred" should be considered original, Proto-Slavic.

claims.statement: Svantovit (also Svantevit, Swantewit, Sventevit, Svetovit, Svatovit, Świętowit, Svątevit, Suvid or Святовит) is a Slavic deity: war god, oracle giver and supreme god of the Rani on Rügen and other Elbe and Baltic Slavs, comparable to Perun among other Slavic tribes.
claims.statement_id: Svantovit (juga Svantevit, Swantewit, Sventevit, Svetovit, Svatovit, Świętowit, Svątevit, Suvid, atau Святовит) adalah dewa Slavia: dewa perang, pemberi orakel, dan dewa tertinggi suku Rani di Rügen serta Slavia Elbe dan Baltik lainnya, sebanding dengan Perun pada suku Slavia lain.
claims.quote: Svantovit (auch Svantevit, Swantewit, Sventevit, Svetovit, Svatovit, Świętowit, Svątevit, Suvid oder Святовит) ist eine slawische Gottheit. Er war der Kriegsgott, Orakelspender und die oberste Gottheit der Ranen auf Rügen und anderer Elb- und Ostseeslawen, vergleichbar mit dem obersten Gott Perun anderer slawischer Stämme.

claims.statement: Svantovit is four-headed, each head facing a cardinal direction, and each direction has its own colour: north white, west red, south black and east green.
claims.statement_id: Svantovit berkepala empat, tiap kepala menghadap satu arah mata angin, dan tiap arah punya warna sendiri: utara putih, barat merah, selatan hitam, dan timur hijau.
claims.quote: Svantovit ist vierköpfig, jeder Kopf schaut in eine Himmelsrichtung. Dabei wird jeder Himmelsrichtung eine eigene Farbe zugeordnet: Norden weiß, Westen rot, Süden schwarz und Osten grün.

claims.statement: At Cape Arkona (Kap Arkona) on Rügen stood a wooden statue showing him with four faces and a wine-filled horn, inside a square pillared temple within the Jaromarsburg.
claims.statement_id: Di Tanjung Arkona (Kap Arkona), pulau Rügen, berdiri patung kayu yang menggambarkannya bermuka empat dengan tanduk berisi anggur, di dalam kuil persegi bertiang di Jaromarsburg.
claims.quote: Auf Kap Arkona auf der Insel Rügen stand eine hölzerne Statue, die ihn mit vier Gesichtern und einem mit Wein gefüllten Horn darstellte. Die Statue befand sich in einem quadratischen, säulengetragenen Tempel innerhalb der Jaromarsburg.

claims.statement: The sanctuary was considered the spiritual centre of the Slavs, especially the Rani of Rügen, and was destroyed in 1168 by the Danish King Valdemar (Waldemar).
claims.statement_id: Tempat suci itu dianggap pusat rohani bangsa Slavia, terutama suku Rani di Rügen, dan dihancurkan pada tahun 1168 oleh Raja Denmark Valdemar (Waldemar).
claims.quote: Das Heiligtum galt als geistiges Zentrum der Slawen und insbesondere der auf Rügen ansässigen Ranen. Es wurde 1168 vom dänischen König Waldemar zerstört.

claims.statement: The Chronica Slavorum of Helmold von Bosau (12th century) describes the Svantovit oracle, which received many gifts and offerings from the whole Slavic and neighbouring non-Slavic world.
claims.statement_id: Chronica Slavorum karya Helmold von Bosau (abad ke-12) menggambarkan orakel Svantovit yang menerima banyak hadiah dan persembahan dari seluruh dunia Slavia dan tetangganya yang bukan Slavia.
claims.quote: Die Chronica Slavorum des Chronisten Helmold von Bosau (12. Jh.) beschreibt das Svantovit-Orakel, dem zahlreiche Geschenke und Opfergaben aus der gesamten slawischen und der benachbarten nichtslawischen Welt dargebracht wurden.

claims.statement: A stone relief in the church of Altenkirchen on Rügen, which one might take for Svantovit, shows a male figure with a large drinking horn; more likely it depicts a priest of the god.
claims.statement_id: Relief batu di gereja Altenkirchen, Rügen, yang mungkin dianggap menggambarkan Svantovit, menampilkan sosok lelaki dengan tanduk minum besar; namun lebih mungkin itu pendeta sang dewa.
claims.quote: Ein Steinrelief, das sich in der Kirche von Altenkirchen auf Rügen befindet und von dem man annehmen könnte, dass es Svantovit abbildet, zeigt ebenfalls eine männliche Figur mit einem großen Trinkhorn. Wahrscheinlicher ist aber, dass es sich dabei um einen Priester der Gottheit handelt.

claims.statement: Väinämöinen is a demigod, hero and central character of Finnish folklore and the main character of Elias Lönnrot's national epic Kalevala; he was described as an old, wise man with a potent, magical singing voice.
claims.statement_id: Väinämöinen adalah setengah dewa, pahlawan, dan tokoh sentral cerita rakyat Finlandia, serta tokoh utama epos nasional Kalevala karya Elias Lönnrot; ia digambarkan sebagai lelaki tua yang bijak dengan suara nyanyian yang kuat dan magis.
claims.quote: is a demigod, hero and the central character in Finnish folklore and the main character in the national epic Kalevala by Elias Lönnrot. Väinämöinen was described as an old and wise man, and he possessed a potent, magical singing voice.

claims.statement: The name Väinämöinen is often explained as coming from Finnish väinä "stream pool" or väineä "slow".
claims.statement_id: Nama Väinämöinen sering dijelaskan berasal dari kata Finlandia väinä "genangan arus" atau väineä "lambat".
claims.quote: The name Väinämöinen has often been explained as coming from the Finnish word väinä 'stream pool' or väineä 'slow'.

claims.statement: The first extant literary mention of Väinämöinen is in Mikael Agricola's 1551 list of Tavastian gods.
claims.statement_id: Penyebutan tertulis tertua tentang Väinämöinen terdapat dalam daftar dewa Tavastia karya Mikael Agricola tahun 1551.
claims.quote: The first extant mention of Väinämöinen in literature is in a list of Tavastian gods by Mikael Agricola in 1551

claims.statement: Agricola and other writers described Väinämöinen as the god of chants, songs and poetry; in many stories he was the central figure at the birth of the world.
claims.statement_id: Agricola dan penulis lain menggambarkan Väinämöinen sebagai dewa mantra, lagu, dan puisi; dalam banyak cerita ia tokoh pusat saat dunia lahir.
claims.quote: He and other writers described Väinämöinen as the god of chants, songs and poetry; in many stories Väinämöinen was the central figure at the birth of the world.

claims.statement: A 1674 letter by Johan Cajanus stated that in Kainuu Väinämöinen was called a son of a giant named Kaleva.
claims.statement_id: Surat tahun 1674 karya Johan Cajanus menyatakan bahwa di Kainuu Väinämöinen disebut putra raksasa bernama Kaleva.
claims.quote: A 1674 letter written by Johan Cajanus stated that in Kainuu, Väinämöinen was called a son of a giant named Kaleva.

claims.statement: Väinämöinen is often described as a shaman hero, a mythical tietäjä with magical abilities, secret knowledge and supreme singing skill; an old myth tells of his journey to the underworld.
claims.statement_id: Väinämöinen sering digambarkan sebagai pahlawan dukun, tietäjä mitis dengan kemampuan magis, pengetahuan rahasia, dan keahlian menyanyi tertinggi; ada mitos lama tentang perjalanannya ke dunia bawah.
claims.quote: Väinämöinen has often been described as a shaman hero, a mythical tietäjä, with magical abilities, secret knowledge and being the most skilled singer. There is an old myth of his katabasis (journey to the underworld).

claims.statement: In another well-attested myth Väinämöinen travels by boat, creates the kantele and plays it so well that even goddesses come to listen.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitos lain yang banyak tercatat, Väinämöinen berlayar, menciptakan kantele, dan memainkannya begitu indah hingga para dewi datang mendengarkan.
claims.quote: In another well attested myth, Väinämöinen goes on a journey on his boat, creates the Kantele and plays it so well even goddesses show up to listen to it.

claims.statement: In Karelia a bird lays an egg on Väinämöinen's knee; when he moves it, the eggs fall and break, forming earth and sky. His element is water, and many regions connect him with it.
claims.statement_id: Di Karelia, seekor burung bertelur di lutut Väinämöinen; ketika ia menggerakkannya, telur-telur jatuh dan pecah membentuk bumi dan langit. Unsur Väinämöinen adalah air, dan di banyak daerah ia dikaitkan dengannya.
claims.quote: In Karelia, Väinämöinen is involved with events before the creation of the world ... A bird lays an egg on Väinämöinen's knee, and when Väinämöinen moves it, the eggs fall down and break, forming the earth and the sky. Väinämöinen's element is water, and he is widely connected to it in many regions.

claims.statement: Väinämöinen defeats Joukahainen in a rune-singing battle through his superior knowledge of the world's beginning, since he himself formed the sea floor, set the stars in the sky and created mountains.
claims.statement_id: Väinämöinen mengalahkan Joukahainen dalam adu nyanyian rune berkat pengetahuannya tentang awal dunia, sebab dialah yang membentuk dasar laut, menaruh bintang di langit, dan menciptakan gunung.
claims.quote: Väinämöinen defeats Joukahainen in a runic singing battle with his superior knowledge over the events in the beginning of the world; after all, it was Väinämöinen himself who formed the bottom of the sea, set the stars in the sky and created mountains.

claims.statement: Some rune singers took this as Väinämöinen's death, while others believed he was still alive and would return one day.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian penyanyi rune menganggap kepergiannya ke pusaran air sebagai kematian Väinämöinen, sedangkan yang lain percaya ia masih hidup dan suatu hari akan kembali.
claims.quote: Some runic singers thought this meant the death of Väinämöinen, while others believed he was still alive and would return one day, real death still waiting for him in the future.

claims.statement: Elias Lönnrot, author of the Kalevala, disputed Väinämöinen's mythological background, claiming he was an ancient hero or an influential shaman who perhaps lived in the ninth century.
claims.statement_id: Elias Lönnrot, penulis Kalevala, membantah latar mitologis Väinämöinen dan menganggapnya pahlawan kuno atau dukun berpengaruh yang mungkin hidup pada abad kesembilan.
claims.quote: In the nineteenth century, some folklorists, most notably Elias Lönnrot, the writer of Kalevala, disputed Väinämöinen's mythological background, claiming that he was an ancient hero, or an influential shaman who lived perhaps in the ninth century.

claims.statement: Stripping away his direct godlike traits, Lönnrot made Väinämöinen the son of the primal goddess Ilmatar, whom Lönnrot himself invented.
claims.statement_id: Dengan menghapus sifat ketuhanan Väinämöinen yang langsung, Lönnrot menjadikannya putra dewi purba Ilmatar, yang diciptakan Lönnrot sendiri.
claims.quote: Stripping Väinämöinen from his direct godlike characteristics, Lönnrot turned Väinämöinen into the son of the primal goddess Ilmatar, whom Lönnrot had invented himself.

claims.statement: He grew for 730 years in the womb of his mother Ilmatar, daughter of the air, and has had wisdom and a magical voice since birth.
claims.statement_id: Väinämöinen tumbuh selama 730 tahun dalam rahim ibunya, Ilmatar sang putri udara, dan sejak lahir memiliki kebijaksanaan serta suara magis.
claims.quote: Er wuchs 730 Jahre lang im Leib seiner Mutter, der Lüftetochter Ilmatar, heran und besitzt seit seiner Geburt die Weisheit und eine magische Stimme.

claims.statement: The Kalevala tells that Väinämöinen kills a great pike and makes a kantele from its jawbone; with Lemminkäinen and Ilmarinen he also tries to steal the Sampo from Louhi.
claims.statement_id: Kalevala mengisahkan Väinämöinen membunuh ikan tombak besar dan membuat kantele dari tulang rahangnya; ia juga bersama Lemminkäinen dan Ilmarinen berusaha merampas Sampo dari Louhi.
claims.quote: Im Kalevala wird berichtet, dass Väinämöinen einen großen Hecht tötet und aus dessen Kieferknochen eine Kantele macht. Außerdem versucht er zusammen mit Lemminkäinen und Ilmarinen, das Sampo von Louhi zu rauben.

claims.statement: Väinämöinen then goes to the seashore, sings up a copper boat with his magical voice and leaves the realm of mortals; in his last words he says he will be needed again some day and will return.
claims.statement_id: Väinämöinen lalu pergi ke tepi laut, memanggil perahu tembaga dengan suara magisnya, dan meninggalkan alam fana; dalam kata-kata terakhirnya ia berkata suatu hari akan dibutuhkan lagi dan akan kembali.
claims.quote: Väinämöinen geht daraufhin an das Ufer des Meeres, singt sich mit seiner magischen Stimme ein Boot aus Kupfer herbei und verlässt das Reich der Sterblichen. In seinen letzten Worten sagt er, dass er irgendwann noch einmal gebraucht werden würde und dann zurückkehren werde.

claims.statement: In the Estonian national epic Kalevipoeg, Väinämöinen corresponds to the god Vanemuine.
claims.statement_id: Dalam epos nasional Estonia Kalevipoeg, Väinämöinen sepadan dengan dewa Vanemuine.
claims.quote: Im estnischen Nationalepos Kalevipoeg entspricht Väinämöinen dem Gott Vanemuine.

claims.statement: His story is continued in the fantasy novel Hammered (2011) by the American author Kevin Hearne.
claims.statement_id: Kisah Väinämöinen dilanjutkan dalam novel fantasi Hammered (2011) karya penulis Amerika Kevin Hearne.
claims.quote: So wird seine Geschichte in dem Fantasy-Roman Hammered (2011) des US-amerikanischen Autors Kevin Hearne fortgesponnen.

claims.statement: He shows this, among other things, by singing the rash Joukahainen down into a bog.
claims.statement_id: Kekuatan suaranya tampak antara lain ketika ia menenggelamkan Joukahainen yang gegabah ke rawa dengan nyanyiannya.
claims.quote: Dies zeigt er unter anderem, indem er den ungestümen Joukahainen durch sein Singen in einem Sumpf versinken ließ.

claims.statement: In Savonia Väinämöinen is also seen as the ruler of water.
claims.statement_id: Di Savonia, Väinämöinen juga dipandang sebagai penguasa air.
claims.quote: Väinämöinen is also seen as the ruler of water in Savonia.

claims.statement: The kikimora is a legendary creature, a female house spirit in Slavic mythology, whose role in the house is usually set beside the domovoy's.
claims.statement_id: Kikimora adalah makhluk legenda, roh rumah perempuan dalam mitologi Slavia, yang perannya di rumah biasanya disandingkan dengan domovoi.
claims.quote: Kikimora is a legendary creature, a female house spirit in Slavic mythology. Her role in the house is usually juxtaposed with that of the domovoy.

claims.statement: The kikimora can be a "bad" or "good" spirit depending on the homeowner's behaviour; more recently an image of her as a female swamp spirit has developed.
claims.statement_id: Kikimora bisa menjadi roh "jahat" atau "baik" bergantung pada perilaku pemilik rumah; belakangan berkembang gambaran kikimora sebagai roh rawa perempuan.
claims.quote: The kikimora can either be a "bad" or a "good" spirit, which will depend on the behavior of the homeowner. In more recent times, an image of kikimora as a female swamp spirit has developed.

claims.statement: Most sources link the suffix -mora with Proto-Slavic *morà ("nightly spirit, bad dream") and Proto-Germanic *marōn, as in English nightmare or French cauchemar.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian besar sumber mengaitkan akhiran -mora dengan Proto-Slavia *morà ("roh malam, mimpi buruk") dan Proto-Jermanik *marōn, seperti dalam kata Inggris nightmare atau Prancis cauchemar.
claims.quote: Most sources link the suffix -mora with the Proto-Slavic *morà ('nightly spirit, bad dream') and the Proto-Germanic *marōn (id.), as in the modern English nightmare or French cauchemar.

claims.statement: The kikimora originates from the 8th to 13th century, when Slavic paganism was slowly absorbed by Christianity; even after Christianity took hold, belief in her remained strong.
claims.statement_id: Asal-usul kikimora berasal dari abad ke-8 hingga ke-13, saat paganisme Slavia perlahan tergantikan agama Kristen; bahkan setelah Kristen mapan, kepercayaan pada kikimora tetap kuat.
claims.quote: The origin of the kikimora comes from the 8th to 13th century when Slavic paganism was slowly subsumed by Christianity. However, even after Christianity took hold in the Slavic regions, the belief of the kikimora was still strong.

claims.statement: The kikimora may have a dog's snout, a chicken's beak or resemble a goat-like being with glowing eyes and horns; she can have any animal's face or body part, is always female, and may appear as an old woman or a beautiful girl.
claims.statement_id: Kikimora bisa bermoncong anjing, berparuh ayam, atau menyerupai makhluk mirip kambing bermata menyala dan bertanduk; ia bisa memiliki bagian wajah atau tubuh hewan mana pun, selalu perempuan, dan bisa tampak sebagai nenek tua atau gadis cantik.
claims.quote: The kikimora might have the snout of a dog, a chicken beak or can even resemble a goat-like entity with glowing eyes and horns. In fact, it can take any part of an animal's face or body. It is always feminine and can appear as an old woman or a beautiful girl.

claims.statement: The swamp kikimora is usually described as a small, ugly, hunchbacked, thin and scruffy old woman with a pointed nose and dishevelled hair.
claims.statement_id: Kikimora rawa biasanya digambarkan sebagai nenek kecil, buruk rupa, bungkuk, kurus, dan kusut, berhidung runcing dan berambut acak-acakan.
claims.quote: The swamp kikimora is usually described as a small, ugly, hunchbacked, thin, and scruffy old woman with a pointed nose and disheveled hair.

claims.statement: The swamp kikimora was believed to frighten people, knock travellers off the road or even drown them, and to kidnap children.
claims.statement_id: Kikimora rawa dipercaya menakuti orang, menjatuhkan pelancong dari jalan, bahkan menenggelamkan mereka, dan juga menculik anak-anak.
claims.quote: It was believed that she frightens people, knocks travelers off the road or even drowns them. She also kidnaps children.

claims.statement: There are two kinds of kikimora: the one from the forest is married to the domovoi, and the one from the swamp is married to the leshy.
claims.statement_id: Ada dua jenis kikimora: yang berasal dari hutan bersuami domovoi, dan yang berasal dari rawa bersuami leshy.
claims.quote: There are two different kinds of kikimoras. The one that comes from the forest is married to the domovoi. The other one comes from the swamp ... and is married to leshy.

claims.statement: When the house is in order a kikimora looks after the chickens and housework; if not, she whistles, breaks dishes and makes noise at night; she also comes out at night to spin thread.
claims.statement_id: Bila rumah teratur, kikimora menjaga ayam dan pekerjaan rumah; bila tidak, ia bersiul, memecahkan piring, dan membuat keributan pada malam hari; ia juga keluar pada malam hari untuk memintal benang.
claims.quote: When the house is in order, a kikimora looks after the chickens and housework. If not, she whistles, breaks dishes, and makes noises at night. She also comes out at night to spin thread.

claims.statement: A kikimora would haunt a household if the house was not kept clean, the husband was lazy or abusive, or the children undisciplined; changing one's behaviour is believed to remove her.
claims.statement_id: Kikimora menghantui rumah tangga bila rumah tidak dijaga bersih, suami malas atau kasar, atau anak tidak disiplin; mengubah perilaku dipercaya mengusirnya dari rumah.
claims.quote: A kikimora would haunt a household if a woman did not keep a clean house, if a husband was lazy or abusive, or if children were poorly disciplined. Reversing one's behaviour is believed to remove her presence from the house.

claims.statement: The kikimora legend is the basis of Kikimora (op. 63), a tone poem for orchestra by Anatoly Lyadov.
claims.statement_id: Legenda kikimora menjadi dasar Kikimora (op. 63), puisi nada untuk orkestra karya Anatoly Lyadov.
claims.quote: The legendary kikimora provides the basis of Kikimora (op. 63), a tone poem for orchestra by Anatoly Lyadov.

claims.statement: The 2015 video game The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt and the 2019 TV series The Witcher depict kikimory as spider-like monsters unrelated to folkloric kikimoras.
claims.statement_id: Gim video The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt (2015) dan serial televisi The Witcher (2019) menampilkan kikimory sebagai monster mirip laba-laba yang tidak berhubungan dengan kikimora cerita rakyat.
claims.quote: The 2015 video game The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt and 2019 television series The Witcher both include depictions of kikimory, which are spider-like monsters that have no relation to folkloric kikimoras.

claims.statement: The kikimora is a female being of Slavic mythology who dwells in houses, is sometimes said to be married to the Domovoi, and usually lives behind the stove or in the cellar.
claims.statement_id: Kikimora adalah makhluk perempuan mitologi Slavia penghuni rumah, kadang dikatakan menikah dengan Domovoi, dan biasanya tinggal di balik tungku atau di ruang bawah tanah.
claims.quote: adalah makhluk perempuan dalam mitologi Slavia. Kikimora termasuk dalam makhluk penghun rumah dan kadang-kadang dikatakan menikah dengan Domovoi. Kikimora biasanya tinggal di balik kompor atau di gudang bawah tanah.

claims.statement: Builders displeased with a homeowner could invite a kikimora to haunt the house by placing a kikimora-like doll in the main beam or under the front corner.
claims.statement_id: Pekerja yang membangun rumah dan tidak senang pada pemiliknya bisa mengundang kikimora untuk menghantui rumah itu dengan menaruh boneka mirip kikimora di balok utama atau di bawah sudut depan rumah.
claims.quote: Jika para pekerja yang membangun rumah merasa tidak senang pada pemlik rumah maka mereka bisa mengundang Kikimora untuk menghantui rumah itu dengan cara menaruh sebuah boneka mirip Kikimora di balok utama atau di bawah sudut depan rumah.

claims.statement: Whoever sees the kikimora weaving will soon die; to calm her, all pots and pans must be washed with fern tea.
claims.statement_id: Siapa pun yang melihat kikimora sedang menenun akan segera mati; untuk menenangkannya, semua panci dan wajan harus dicuci dengan teh pakis.
claims.quote: Barang siapa yang melihat Kikimora sedang menenun maka dia akan segera mati. Untuk menentramkan Kikimora, seseorang harus mencuci semua panci dan wajan dengan teh pakis.

claims.statement: A snake stone or juniper twigs are hung over the henhouse to protect the chickens from the kikimora.
claims.statement_id: Batu ular atau ranting juniper digantung di atas kandang ayam untuk melindungi ayam dari kikimora.
claims.quote: Batu ular atau ranting junifer digantung di atas kadang ayam untuk melindungi ayam dari Kikimora.

claims.statement: She can reportedly be identified by her wet footprints; builders wanting to harm a house buyer would bring in a kikimora, and once inside she is hard to make leave.
claims.statement_id: Kikimora konon bisa dikenali dari jejak kakinya yang basah; tukang bangunan yang ingin mencelakai pembeli rumah akan mendatangkan kikimora, dan sekali masuk ia sulit diusir.
claims.quote: It is said that she can be identified by her wet footprints. When home builders wanted to cause harm to someone buying a house, they would bring in kikimora. Once she is inside, it is difficult to get her to leave.

claims.statement: Chernobog and Belobog are a pair of opposing deities alleged to be part of Polabian mythology.
claims.statement_id: Chernobog dan Belobog adalah sepasang dewa yang saling berlawanan dan diduga merupakan bagian mitologi Polabia.
claims.quote: are a pair of opposing deities alleged to be part of Polabian mythology.

claims.statement: The first written account of Chernobog is in the 12th-century Chronicle of the Slavs, describing him as a god of misfortune worshipped by the Wagri and Obodrites; Belobog is first noted in 16th-century literature as his opposite.
claims.statement_id: Catatan tertulis pertama tentang Chernobog ada dalam Kronik Bangsa Slavia abad ke-12, yang menyebutnya dewa kemalangan yang dipuja suku Wagri dan Obodrit; Belobog baru tercatat dalam tulisan abad ke-16 sebagai lawan Chernobog.
claims.quote: The first written account of Chernobog is in the 12th-century Chronicle of the Slavs, where he is described as a god of misfortune worshipped by the Wagri and Obodrites; while Belobog is first noted in 16th century literature in opposition to Chernobog.

claims.statement: Researchers disagree whether the two were truly part of Slavic folklore: many think both names authentic, others call them pseudo-deities; both appear in later sources, with Chernobog associated with the Christian devil.
claims.statement_id: Para peneliti berbeda pendapat apakah kedua dewa ini sungguh bagian kepercayaan Slavia: banyak ahli menganggap kedua nama itu asli, yang lain menganggapnya dewa semu; keduanya muncul dalam sumber kemudian, dan Chernobog dikaitkan dengan iblis Kristen.
claims.quote: Researchers disagree on whether the two deities were indeed part of Slavic folklore: while many scholars believe the two theonyms are authentic, others believe they are pseudo-deities. Both deities appear in later sources, however, with Chernobog being associated with the Christian devil.

claims.statement: The name Chernobog comes from Proto-Slavic "čĭrnŭ" (black) and "bogŭ" (god).
claims.statement_id: Nama Chernobog berasal dari kata Proto-Slavia "čĭrnŭ" (hitam) dan "bogŭ" (dewa).
claims.quote: Chernobog (dari bahasa Proto-Slavia "čĭrnŭ" yang berarti "hitam", dan "bogŭ" yang berarti "dewa")

claims.statement: The only historical sources on Chernobog are Christian ones depicting him as evil and accursed; it is unknown whether the ancient Slavs truly regarded him as evil.
claims.statement_id: Satu-satunya sumber sejarah tentang Chernobog berasal dari sumber Kristen yang menggambarkannya jahat dan terkutuk; tidak diketahui apakah orang Slavia kuno sungguh menganggapnya jahat.
claims.quote: Satu-satunya sumber sejarah berasal dari sumber Kristen yang menggambarkan dewa ini sebagai dewa yang jahat dan terkutuk, tetapi tidak diketahui apakah dewa ini benar-benar dianggap sebagai dewa yang jahat oleh orang-orang Slavia kuno.

claims.statement: The name was used by West Slavic tribes in the 12th century, so he is thought not to have been a very important or old god.
claims.statement_id: Nama Chernobog disebut oleh suku Slavia Barat pada abad ke-12, sehingga ia diduga bukan dewa yang sangat penting atau bukan dewa tua.
claims.quote: Nama ini disebutkan oleh suku-suku Slavia Barat pada abad ke-12, sehingga diduga ia bukan dewa yang sangat penting atau bukan dewa lama.

claims.statement: Chernobog (Чернобог; Czorneboh, Czernebog) is, in the mythology of the Baltic Slavs, an evil god who brings misfortune.
claims.statement_id: Chernobog (Чернобог; Czorneboh, Czernebog) dalam mitologi Slavia Baltik adalah dewa jahat yang membawa kemalangan.
claims.quote: Чернобог (Czorneboh, Czernebog) — в мифологии балтийских славян злой бог, приносящий несчастье.

claims.statement: Some scholars reconstruct the Belobog/Chernobog pair as an opposition of "light/dark", "good/evil" and "luck/misfortune".
claims.statement_id: Sebagian ahli merekonstruksi pasangan Belobog/Chernobog sebagai pertentangan "terang/gelap", "baik/jahat", dan "untung/malang".
claims.quote: Некоторыми учёными реконструируется пара Белобог/Чернобог, которая представляет собой противопоставление «светлое/тёмное», «добро/зло», «счастье/несчастье».

claims.statement: According to Helmold, at feasts and drinking the Slavs passed round a sacrificial cup, uttering not blessings but spells in the name of a good god and an evil god.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Helmold, dalam pesta dan perjamuan orang Slavia mengedarkan cawan persembahan sambil mengucapkan mantra, bukan berkat, atas nama dewa yang baik dan dewa yang jahat.
claims.quote: во время пиров и возлияний они пускают вкруговую жертвенную чашу, произнося при этом, не скажу благословения, а скорее заклинания от имени богов, а именно, доброго бога и злого

claims.statement: Therefore in their language they call the evil god the devil, or Chernobog, that is, the black god.
claims.statement_id: Karena itu, dalam bahasa mereka dewa jahat disebut iblis atau Chernobog, yaitu dewa hitam.
claims.quote: Поэтому злого бога они на своём языке называют дьяволом, или Чернобогом, то есть чёрным богом.

claims.statement: The Slavs worshipped Chernobog as an evil deity because they imagined all evil lay in his power, and so begged his mercy.
claims.statement_id: Orang Slavia memuja Chernobog sebagai dewa jahat karena mengira semua keburukan berada dalam kuasanya, sehingga memohon belas kasihnya.
claims.quote: Славяне для того почитали Чернобога, как злое божество, что они воображали, будто всякое зло находится в его власти, и потому просили его о помиловании

claims.statement: Chernobog is the main villain and final boss of the 1997 first-person shooter Blood.
claims.statement_id: Chernobog adalah penjahat utama dan bos terakhir dalam gim tembak orang pertama Blood (1997).
claims.quote: Чернобог является главным злодеем и финальным боссом в шутере от первого лица Blood 1997 года выпуска.

claims.statement: Chernobog is the main antagonist of the "Ночь на Лысой Горе/Аве Мария" segment of the 1940 animated feature "Фантазия".
claims.statement_id: Chernobog adalah antagonis utama segmen "Ночь на Лысой Горе/Аве Мария" dalam film animasi panjang tahun 1940 "Фантазия".
claims.quote: Чернобог — главный антагонист сегмента «Ночь на Лысой Горе/Аве Мария» из диснеевского полнометражного мультфильма 1940 года «Фантазия».

claims.statement: Belobog (Белобог) is a supposed West Slavic god of luck and happiness; several scholars consider the name Belobog invented.
claims.statement_id: Belobog (Белобог) adalah dewa untung dan kebahagiaan Slavia Barat yang keberadaannya hanya diduga; sejumlah ahli menganggap nama Belobog rekaan.
claims.quote: Белобог — предполагаемый западнославянский бог удачи и счастья. ... Ряд ученых считают имя Белобог вымышленным.

claims.statement: Among the Sorbs there were hills named Bjely boh, with positive meaning, and Corny boh, with negative meaning.
claims.statement_id: Di kalangan Sorbia (лужицких сербов) terdapat nama bukit Bjely boh yang bermakna positif dan Corny boh yang bermakna negatif.
claims.quote: У лужицких сербов существовали названия гор Bjely boh и Corny boh — с первым из них связывалась положительная семантика, со вторым — отрицательная.

claims.statement: A chronicle says of the Slavic gods that "Belobog is evil and Chernobog good", but several historians consider these excerpts forged.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah kronik menyebut tentang dewa Slavia bahwa "Belobog jahat, dan Chernobog baik", tetapi kutipan itu dianggap palsu oleh sejumlah sejarawan.
claims.quote: в которой говорится о божествах славян, в частности — «Белобог злой, а Чернобог добрый». Однако данные выдержки считаются рядом историков поддельными.

claims.statement: In that 17th-century source Belobog appears as a second name of Vit (Svetovit), whose temple stood in Arkona on Rügen.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sumber abad ke-17 itu, Belobog muncul sebagai nama kedua Vit (Svetovit), yang kuilnya berada di kota Arkona di pulau Rügen.
claims.quote: При этом Белобог выступает как второе имя Вита (Святовита), храм которого располагался в городе Арконе на острове Рюгене (Руяне).

claims.statement: Chernobog arose from a misinterpretation of Helmold's "Slavic Chronicle".
claims.statement_id: Chernobog muncul karena salah tafsir atas "Kronik Slavia" karya Helmold.
claims.quote: Появился из-за неправильной интерпретации "Славянской хроники Гельмольда"

claims.statement: Petrus Albinus mentions Chernobog in his Meissen Chronicle of 1590.
claims.statement_id: Petrus Albinus menyebut Chernobog dalam Kronik Meissen tahun 1590.
claims.quote: Чернобога упоминает Пётр Альбин в «Миснейской хронике» 1590 года:

claims.statement: The Turul is a mythological bird of prey, mostly depicted as a falcon, in Hungarian and Turkic tradition, and a national symbol of Hungarians.
claims.statement_id: Turul adalah burung pemangsa mitologis yang umumnya digambarkan sebagai falkon dalam tradisi Hungaria dan Turk, sekaligus lambang nasional bangsa Hungaria.
claims.quote: The Turul is a mythological bird of prey, mostly depicted as a falcon, in Hungarian tradition and Turkic tradition, and a national symbol of Hungarians.

claims.statement: The Turul is probably based on a large falcon; the Hungarian word turul meant one kind of falcon, and its origin is now thought most likely Turkic.
claims.statement_id: Turul kemungkinan didasarkan pada falkon besar; kata Hungaria turul berarti satu jenis falkon, dan asal katanya kini dianggap paling mungkin dari bahasa Turk.
claims.quote: The Turul is probably based on a large falcon. The Hungarian word turul meant one kind of falcon and the origin of the word is currently thought to be most likely Turkic

claims.statement: Toġrïl or toğrul means a medium to large bird of prey of the family Accipitridae, a goshawk or red kite.
claims.statement_id: Toġrïl atau toğrul berarti burung pemangsa sedang hingga besar dari famili Accipitridae, seperti elang alap atau elang merah.
claims.quote: Toġrïl or toğrul means a medium to large bird of prey of the family Accipitridae, goshawk or red kite.

claims.statement: In the legend of Emese, recorded in the Gesta Hungarorum and the Chronicon Pictum, the turul appears in Emese's dream when she was already pregnant.
claims.statement_id: Dalam legenda Emese yang tercatat di Gesta Hungarorum dan Chronicon Pictum, turul disebut muncul dalam mimpi Emese ketika ia sudah hamil.
claims.quote: In the legend of Emese, recorded in the Gesta Hungarorum and the Chronicon Pictum, the turul is mentioned as occurring in a dream of Emese, when she was already pregnant.

claims.statement: The Turul's role is a protector spirit shielding the infant Álmos from harm, a motif very similar to the Simurgh's role in the Iranian epic Shahnameh.
claims.statement_id: Peran turul adalah roh pelindung yang menjaga bayi Álmos dari bahaya, motif yang sangat mirip dengan peran Simurgh dalam epos Iran Shahnameh.
claims.quote: The Turul's role is one of a protector spirit that protects the infant Álmos from harm. This is a very similar motif to the role of the Simurgh in the Iranian epic Shahnameh.

claims.statement: In a second dream of the Hungarian tribal leader, eagles (the emblem of the Pechenegs, enemies of the Hungarians) attacked their horses and the Turul came and saved them.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mimpi kedua pemimpin suku Hungaria, elang-elang (lambang bangsa Pecheneg, musuh Hungaria) menyerang kuda-kuda mereka, lalu turul datang menyelamatkannya.
claims.quote: In a second dream by the leader of the Hungarian tribes, in which eagles (the emblem of the Pechenegs, enemies of the Hungarians ) attacked their horses and the Turul came and saved them.

claims.statement: The Turul's image and role are similar to the Norse Vedfolnir, which likewise perched on the tree of life.
claims.statement_id: Citra dan peran turul mirip dengan Vedfolnir dari mitologi Nordik, yang seperti turul bertengger di pohon kehidupan.
claims.quote: The image of the Turul and its role is similar to that of the Norse Vedfolnir, which like it perched on the tree of life.

claims.statement: In Hungarian tradition it originated as the clan symbol of the ruling Árpád dynasty in the 9th and 10th centuries.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi Hungaria, turul bermula sebagai lambang klan yang dipakai wangsa Árpád yang berkuasa pada abad ke-9 dan ke-10.
claims.quote: In Hungarian tradition, it originated as the clan symbol used in the 9th and 10th centuries by the ruling Árpád dynasty.

claims.statement: The Gesta Hunnorum et Hungarorum says the Árpád dynasty descended from the Turul clan, and the Gesta Hungarorum records the Turul as Árpád's totemic ancestor.
claims.statement_id: Gesta Hunnorum et Hungarorum menyebut wangsa Árpád keturunan klan Turul, dan Gesta Hungarorum mencatat bahwa leluhur totemik Árpád adalah turul.
claims.quote: The Gesta Hunnorum et Hungarorum mentioned that the Árpád dynasty descended from the gens (clan) Turul, and the Gesta Hungarorum recorded that the Árpád's totemic ancestor was the Turul.

claims.statement: According to the Gesta Hungarorum, a divine vision in the form of a falcon appeared in a dream to Álmos's mother, as if coming to her and impregnating her, and revealed that a torrent would come from her womb and glorious kings from her loins.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Gesta Hungarorum, penampakan ilahi berwujud falkon muncul dalam mimpi ibu Álmos, seakan mendatangi dan membuahinya, serta memberitahukan bahwa dari rahimnya akan mengalir arus deras dan lahir raja-raja mulia.
claims.quote: a divine vision appeared to his mother in a dream in the form of a falcon that, as if coming to her, impregnated her and made known to her that from her womb a torrent would come forth and from her loins glorious kings be generated

claims.statement: A pair of silver discs with a Turul motif was found at Rakamaz, Hungary, in a 10th-century Hungarian cemetery.
claims.statement_id: Sepasang cakram perak bermotif turul ditemukan di Rakamaz, Hungaria, dari pemakaman Hungaria abad ke-10.
claims.quote: A pair of silver disk with Turul motive was found in Rakamaz, Hungary from a 10th century Hungarian cemetery.

claims.statement: The central element of the Hungarian Defence Forces emblem is the Turul with outspread wings holding King Saint Stephen's sword in its claws.
claims.statement_id: Unsur utama lambang Angkatan Bersenjata Hungaria adalah turul bersayap terbentang yang mencengkeram pedang Raja Santo Stefanus (Saint Stephen).
claims.quote: The central element of the emblem of the Hungarian Defence Forces is the Turul bird with extended wings holding the sword of King Saint Stephen in its claws.

claims.statement: Of three large Turul statues, the last stands on a mountain near Tatabánya while the other two were destroyed; it is the largest bird statue in Europe and the largest bronze statue in Central Europe.
claims.statement_id: Dari tiga patung turul besar, yang terakhir berdiri di gunung dekat Tatabánya, sedangkan dua lainnya hancur; patung itu adalah patung burung terbesar di Eropa dan patung perunggu terbesar di Eropa Tengah.
claims.quote: The last of the three stands on a mountain near Tatabánya, Hungary, but the other two were destroyed. It is the largest bird statue in Europe, and the largest bronze statue in Central Europe.

claims.statement: The Turul is a mythological bird of Hungarian tradition often depicted like an eagle, and a national symbol of Hungary and Transylvania.
claims.statement_id: Turul adalah burung mitologis dalam tradisi Hungaria yang sering digambarkan seperti rajawali, dan merupakan lambang nasional Hungaria dan Transilvania.
claims.quote: Turul adalah burung mitologis yang sering kali digambarkan seperti rajawali dalam tradisi Hungaria. Burung ini merupakan lambang nasional Hungaria dan Transilvania.

claims.statement: A jiangshi (僵尸; 殭屍), also known as a Chinese hopping vampire, is a type of undead creature or reanimated corpse in Chinese legends and folklore.
claims.statement_id: Jiangshi (僵尸; 殭屍), juga dikenal sebagai vampir melompat Tiongkok, adalah jenis makhluk mayat hidup atau mayat yang bangkit kembali dalam legenda dan cerita rakyat Tiongkok.
claims.quote: A jiāngshī (simplified Chinese: 僵尸; traditional Chinese: 殭屍; pinyin: jiāngshī; Jyutping: goeng1 si1), also known as a Chinese hopping vampire, is a type of undead creature or reanimated corpse in Chinese legends and folklore.

claims.statement: Due to Hong Kong cinema, modern popular culture usually depicts it as a stiff corpse in Qing dynasty official garments.
claims.statement_id: Karena pengaruh sinema Hong Kong, dalam budaya populer modern jiangshi biasanya digambarkan sebagai mayat kaku berbusana resmi dinasti Qing.
claims.quote: Due to the influence of Hong Kong cinema, it is typically depicted in modern popular culture as a stiff corpse dressed in official garments from the Qing dynasty.

claims.statement: In popular culture it is usually shown hopping; in folklore it is more formidable, able to run in pursuit and, if old enough or full of enough yang energy, to fly.
claims.statement_id: Dalam budaya populer jiangshi umumnya digambarkan melompat; dalam cerita rakyat ia lebih menakutkan, bisa berlari mengejar, dan bila cukup tua atau cukup menyerap energi yang, juga bisa terbang.
claims.quote: In popular culture, it is commonly represented as hopping or leaping. In folkloric accounts, however, it is more formidable, capable of giving chase by running, and if sufficiently ancient or if it has absorbed sufficient yang energy, capable also of flight.

claims.statement: According to folklore, jiangshi came from the hills, soaring through the air, to devour the people's infants.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita rakyat, jiangshi datang dari perbukitan, melayang di udara, untuk memangsa bayi-bayi penduduk.
claims.quote: According to folkloric understandings, "jiāngshī came from the hills, soaring through the air, to devour the infants of the people".

claims.statement: Historian J. J. M. de Groot suggests the belief arose from natural horror at dead bodies, fed by unburied corpses in imperial China.
claims.statement_id: Sejarawan J. J. M. de Groot berpendapat bahwa kepercayaan pada jiangshi berasal dari kengerian alami saat melihat mayat, diperkuat oleh adanya jenazah yang tak dikuburkan di Tiongkok masa kekaisaran (imperial China).
claims.quote: Historian J. J. M. de Groot suggests that the belief in jiangshi was the result of the natural horror at the sight of dead bodies, nourished by the presence of unburied corpses in imperial China

claims.statement: The belief also partly derived from "corpse-driving", the repatriation of dead labourers' corpses across Xiang province (now Hunan) to their hometowns for burial in family graves.
claims.statement_id: Kepercayaan pada jiangshi sebagian juga berasal dari kebiasaan "mengantar mayat", yaitu memulangkan jenazah buruh melintasi provinsi Xiang (kini Hunan) ke kampung halaman untuk dimakamkan di makam keluarga.
claims.quote: The belief in jiangshi and its representation in the popular imagination was also partly derived from the habit of "corpse-driving", a practice involving the repatriation of the corpses of dead laborers across Xiang province (present-day Hunan) to their hometowns for burial in family gravesites.

claims.statement: The corpses were tied to bamboo sticks and carried by professional corpse-drivers for thousands of miles to their ancestral villages, giving the impression of a hopping corpse.
claims.statement_id: Jenazah diikat pada batang bambu dan dipikul oleh para pengantar mayat profesional sejauh ribuan mil ke desa leluhurnya, sehingga tampak seperti mayat yang melompat.
claims.quote: The corpses were trussed up against bamboo sticks and carried by professionals known as corpse-drivers and transported over thousands of miles to their ancestral villages, which gave the impression of a hopping corpse.

claims.statement: Qing dynasty scholar Ji Xiaolan, in his Yuewei Caotang Biji, classified reanimation into two kinds: a recently dead person returning to life, or a long-buried corpse that does not decompose.
claims.statement_id: Sarjana dinasti Qing Ji Xiaolan dalam bukunya Yuewei Caotang Biji menggolongkan sebab mayat bangkit menjadi dua: orang yang baru meninggal hidup kembali, atau mayat yang lama dikubur tetapi tidak membusuk.
claims.quote: The Qing dynasty scholar Ji Xiaolan mentioned in his book Yuewei Caotang Biji ... that the causes for a corpse to be reanimated can be classified in either of two categories: a recently deceased person returning to life, or a corpse that has been buried for a long time but does not decompose.

claims.statement: When the hun leaves the body after death but the po remains and takes control, the dead person becomes a jiangshi.
claims.statement_id: Bila roh hun meninggalkan tubuh setelah mati tetapi roh po tetap tinggal dan mengendalikan tubuh, orang itu menjadi jiangshi.
claims.quote: When the hun leaves the body after death but the po remains and takes control of the body, the dead person becomes a jiangshi.

claims.statement: An unburied corpse comes to life when struck by lightning, or when a pregnant cat (or a black cat in some tales) leaps across the coffin.
claims.statement_id: Mayat yang belum dikubur bisa hidup kembali setelah tersambar petir, atau bila kucing hamil (atau kucing hitam dalam sebagian kisah) melompati peti matinya.
claims.quote: The corpse comes to life after it is struck by a bolt of lightning, or when a pregnant cat (or a black cat in some tales) leaps across the coffin.

claims.statement: The character jiang in "jiangshi" literally means "hard" or "stiff".
claims.statement_id: Aksara jiang dalam "jiangshi" secara harfiah berarti "keras" atau "kaku".
claims.quote: in "jiangshi" literally means "hard" or "stiff".

claims.statement: Jiangshi are described with greenish-white skin, perhaps from fungus or mould on corpses, long hair and animal-like behaviour; they are ferocious, ravenous and extremely strong.
claims.statement_id: Jiangshi digambarkan berkulit putih kehijauan, mungkin dari jamur yang tumbuh pada mayat, berambut panjang, bisa berperilaku seperti hewan, buas, rakus, dan sangat kuat.
claims.quote: Jiangshi are described as having greenish-white skin, possibly deriving from fungus or mould growing on corpses. They have long hair and may behave like animals. They are ferocious, ravenous beings possessing extreme strength

claims.statement: Jiangshi are also said to be terrified of their own reflections.
claims.statement_id: Jiangshi juga dikatakan takut pada bayangannya sendiri.
claims.quote: Jiangshi are also said to be terrified of their own reflections.

claims.statement: Fulu, a Taoist talisman, is stuck on the forehead to immobilise jiangshi.
claims.statement_id: Fulu, jimat Tao, ditempel di dahi untuk melumpuhkan jiangshi.
claims.quote: Fulu (Taoist talisman), stuck on the forehead to immobilise them.

claims.statement: According to Yuan Mei's Zi Bu Yu, evil spirits withdraw when they hear a rooster's call.
claims.statement_id: Menurut buku Zi Bu Yu karya Yuan Mei, roh jahat mundur ketika mendengar kokok ayam jantan.
claims.quote: According to Yuan Mei's book Zi Bu Yu, "Evil spirits withdraw when they hear a rooster's call"

claims.statement: Peach is the essence of the Five Elements and can subdue evil auras and deter evil spirits.
claims.statement_id: Persik adalah inti Lima Unsur, mampu menundukkan aura jahat dan menangkal roh jahat.
claims.quote: "Peach is the essence of the Five Elements. It can subjugate evil auras and deter evil spirits."

claims.statement: Films such as Mr. Vampire and its sequels (Mr. Vampire II, III and IV) became comedy-horror cult classics and sparked a vampire craze in East Asia, including Taiwan and Japan.
claims.statement_id: Film seperti Mr. Vampire dan sekuelnya (Mr. Vampire II, III, dan IV) menjadi film kultus komedi-horor dan memicu demam vampir di Asia Timur, termasuk Taiwan dan Jepang.
claims.quote: Movies such as Mr. Vampire and its various sequels (Mr. Vampire II, Mr. Vampire III, and Mr. Vampire IV) became cult classics in comedy-horror and inspired a vampire craze in East Asia, including Taiwan and Japan.

claims.statement: Jiangshi are usually depicted as stiff corpses in Qing dynasty official dress, hopping with arms outstretched; they kill the living to absorb their qi, usually at night, and by day stay in coffins or hide in dark places like caves.
claims.statement_id: Jiangshi biasanya digambarkan sebagai mayat kaku berpakaian resmi Dinasti Qing yang melompat dengan lengan terentang; mereka membunuh makhluk hidup untuk menyerap qi pada malam hari, dan siang harinya berada di peti mati atau bersembunyi di tempat gelap seperti gua.
claims.quote: Mereka biasanya digambarkan sebagai mayat kaku mengenakan pakaian resmi dari Dinasti Qing, dan bergerak dengan melompat-lompat, dengan lengan terentang. Membunuh makhluk hidup untuk menyerap qi, atau "kekuatan hidup" mereka, biasanya pada malam hari, sedangkan di siang hari, mereka ada di dalam peti mati atau bersembunyi di tempat gelap seperti gua.

claims.statement: Holding one's breath keeps jiangshi from finding you since they are blind, though this contradicts the claim that they fear their own reflection.
claims.statement_id: Menahan napas membuat jiangshi tidak bisa menemukan orang karena mereka buta, meski hal ini bertentangan dengan pernyataan bahwa mereka takut pada bayangannya sendiri.
claims.quote: Holding one's breath, which makes the jiangshi unable to find you as they are blind, though this contradicts the earlier statement that they are afraid of their own reflection.

claims.statement: In Cantonese, "jiangshi" is pronounced goeng-si.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Kanton, "jiangshi" dibaca goeng-si.
claims.quote: "Jiangshi" dibaca goeng-si dalam bahasa Kanton.

claims.statement: The vila is a Slavic fairy similar to a nymph.
claims.statement_id: Vila adalah peri Slavia yang mirip nimfa.
claims.quote: is a Slavic fairy similar to a nymph.

claims.statement: The vila is widely known among the South Slavs, though some variants exist in West Slavic mythology too.
claims.statement_id: Vila dikenal luas di kalangan Slavia Selatan, tetapi beberapa variannya juga ada dalam mitologi Slavia Barat.
claims.quote: The vila is mostly known among South Slavs; however, some variants are present in the mythology of West Slavs as well.

claims.statement: According to Natalie Kononenko, vilas are female nature spirits with an ambivalent relationship with humans.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Natalie Kononenko, vila adalah roh alam perempuan yang hubungannya dengan manusia mendua.
claims.quote: According to Natalie Kononenko, the vilas are female spirits of nature who have an ambivalent relationship with humans.

claims.statement: In fairy tales vilas may act maliciously towards people (killing them, destroying crops) but may also help the hero with magical objects and mounts.
claims.statement_id: Dalam dongeng, vila bisa berbuat jahat kepada manusia (membunuh orang, merusak panen), tetapi juga bisa menolong pahlawan dengan memberi benda ajaib dan tunggangan.
claims.quote: In fairy tales, they may act with malice towards them (killing people, destroying crops) but may also help the hero by giving him magical objects and mounts.

claims.statement: Vilas confuse men's spirits with their arrows and steal children, leaving changelings in their place.
claims.statement_id: Vila mengacaukan jiwa laki-laki dengan panah mereka, serta mencuri anak dan menggantinya dengan anak tukaran.
claims.quote: They confuse men's spirits with their arrows. They steal children and substitute them with changelings.

claims.statement: The vilas' fondness for fighting recalls the Valkyrie and is unique in Slavic mythology.
claims.statement_id: Kegemaran vila bertempur mengingatkan pada Valkyrie dan unik dalam mitologi Slavia.
claims.quote: Their fondness for fighting is reminiscent of the teutonic Valkyrie and is unique in Slavic mythology.

claims.statement: There are three kinds of vile: those living on land and in forests, water nymphs, and cloud or air nymphs.
claims.statement_id: Ada tiga jenis vila: yang hidup di darat dan hutan, nimfa air, serta nimfa awan atau udara.
claims.quote: There are three kinds, those living on land and in forests ... water nymphs ... and cloud or air nymphs

claims.statement: Vile appear as swans, falcons, horses or wolves; cloud nymphs appear as a whirlwind.
claims.statement_id: Vila tampil sebagai angsa, elang, kuda, atau serigala; nimfa awan muncul sebagai angin puyuh.
claims.quote: They appear as swans, falcons, horses, or wolves; cloud nymphs appear as a whirlwind.

claims.statement: In Croatian and Serbian epic poetry, many heroes have a vila as an elective or blood sister.
claims.statement_id: Dalam puisi epik Kroasia dan Serbia, banyak pahlawan memiliki vila sebagai saudari angkat atau saudari sedarah.
claims.quote: In Croatian and Serbian epic poetry, many heroes have a vila as an elective or blood sister

claims.statement: Vilas have supernatural powers and are skilled in healing; they build splendid castles at the edges of clouds.
claims.statement_id: Vila memiliki kekuatan gaib dan pandai menyembuhkan; mereka membangun istana megah di tepi awan.
claims.quote: They possess supernatural powers and are able in the art of healing. They build splendid castles at the edges of clouds.

claims.statement: In Slovakia, vile are the restless souls of dead girls who lure young men into a deadly circle dance.
claims.statement_id: Di Slowakia, vila adalah arwah gelisah gadis yang telah meninggal, yang memikat pemuda ke tarian lingkaran yang mematikan.
claims.quote: In Slovakia, vile are the restless souls of deceased girls who lure young men into a deadly circle dance.

claims.statement: The etymology is unclear; one explanation derives it from the Slavic verb viti, "to wind around, twist, weave".
claims.statement_id: Etimologi nama vila tidak jelas; salah satu penjelasan menurunkannya dari kata kerja Slavia viti, "melilit, memintal, menganyam".
claims.quote: The etymology is unclear. Possible explanations are from the Slavic verb viti (вити, "to wind around, twist, weave")

claims.statement: In Czech tradition, víly are almost always malicious unless respected and avoided.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi Ceko, vila hampir selalu jahat kecuali dihormati dan dihindari.
claims.quote: Within the Czech tradition, víly are almost always malicious, unless respected and avoided.

claims.statement: The Wila (Russian вила, Polish wiła, Czech víla), also called Samowila or Samodiwa, is a female nature spirit of Slavic mythology.
claims.statement_id: Wila (bahasa Rusia вила, Polandia wiła, Ceko víla), juga disebut Samowila atau Samodiwa, adalah roh alam perempuan dalam mitologi Slavia.
claims.quote: Die Wila (russisch вила, ukrainisch віла, polnisch wiła, tschechisch víla, serbokroatisch-kyrillisch vila), auch Samowila oder Samodiwa, ist ein weiblicher Naturgeist der slawischen Mythologie.

claims.statement: In folk tales vile are beautiful girls with translucent bodies and long hair; losing even one hair means their death.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah rakyat, vila adalah gadis cantik bertubuh tembus pandang dan berambut panjang; kehilangan sehelai rambut saja berarti kematian baginya.
claims.quote: In den Volkserzählungen sind Wilen schöne Mädchen mit durchsichtigem Körper und langen Haaren. Verlieren sie auch nur ein einziges Haar, bedeutet dies ihren Tod.

claims.statement: Prokopios von Caesarea already reported their worship in pre-Christian cult in the 6th century, though he called them nymphs rather than using the Slavic name.
claims.statement_id: Prokopios von Caesarea sudah melaporkan pemujaan mereka dalam kultus pra-Kristen pada abad ke-6, tetapi ia tidak memakai nama Slavia dan menyebut mereka nimfa.
claims.quote: Über ihre Verehrung im Rahmen des vorchristlichen Kultes berichtet bereits Prokopios von Caesarea im 6. Jahrhundert. Er nennt allerdings nicht den slawischen Namen, sondern bezeichnet sie als Nymphen.

claims.statement: Related spirits are the rusalkas, whose worship is closely tied to the cult of the dead and who, unlike vile, are mostly harmful.
claims.statement_id: Roh yang berkerabat adalah rusalka, yang pemujaannya terkait erat dengan kultus orang mati dan yang, berbeda dari vila, umumnya membawa celaka.
claims.quote: Verwandte Geister sind die Rusalkas, deren Verehrung eng mit dem Totenkult verknüpft ist und die im Gegensatz zu den Wilen meist verhängnisvoll wirken.

claims.statement: Vile are mostly well-disposed towards humans, and marriages between a vila and a human also occur in the tales.
claims.statement_id: Vila umumnya bersikap baik kepada manusia, dan pernikahan antara vila dan manusia juga muncul dalam kisah-kisah.
claims.quote: Den Menschen gegenüber sind sie meist wohlgesinnt, auch Hochzeiten zwischen einer Wila und einem Menschen kommen in den Erzählungen vor.

claims.statement: Vile are described as group beings mainly tied to the water element, but also appear in forests, fields and mountains.
claims.statement_id: Vila digambarkan sebagai makhluk berkelompok yang terutama dikaitkan dengan unsur air, tetapi juga muncul di hutan, ladang, dan pegunungan.
claims.quote: Wilen oder Wil(l)is werden als Gruppenwesen beschrieben und überwiegend mit dem Wasserelement verbunden, treten aber auch in Wäldern, auf dem Feld und im Gebirge auf.

claims.statement: Vile are usually friendly to people but can take horrible revenge on those who insult them, ignore their orders or approach their circle dances uninvited; this general amiability sets them apart from the rusalki.
claims.statement_id: Vila biasanya ramah kepada manusia, tetapi bisa membalas dendam dengan mengerikan kepada orang yang menghina mereka, mengabaikan perintah mereka, atau mendekati tarian lingkaran mereka tanpa diundang; keramahan inilah yang membedakan mereka dari rusalka.
claims.quote: Vile are usually friendly to people, but they can take horrible revenge on those who insult them, disregard their orders, or approach their circle dances uninvited. Their general amiability distinguishes them from the rusalki.

claims.statement: In Balkan folklore, a dhampir is a mythical creature resulting from a union between a vampire and a human.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Balkan, dhampir adalah makhluk mitos hasil hubungan antara vampir dan manusia.
claims.quote: In Balkan folklore, a dhampir ... is a mythical creature that is the result of a union between a vampire and a human.

claims.statement: This union was usually between male vampires and human women; stories of female vampires mating with human men are rare.
claims.statement_id: Hubungan itu biasanya antara vampir laki-laki dan perempuan manusia; kisah vampir perempuan dengan laki-laki manusia jarang ada.
claims.quote: This union was usually between male vampires and female humans, while stories of female vampires mating with male humans are rare.

claims.statement: The word dhampir is Albanian, borrowed from South Slavic vampir; the shift v > dh is a feature of Albanian.
claims.statement_id: Kata dhampir adalah kata bahasa Albania yang dipinjam dari kata Slavia Selatan vampir; perubahan v menjadi dh adalah ciri bahasa Albania.
claims.quote: The word dhampir is an Albanian word which in turn is borrowed from South Slavic vampir. The shift v > dh is a feature of Albanian.

claims.statement: Elsewhere in the region, terms such as Serbian vampirović, vampijerović and vampirić (and Bosnian lampijerović), meaning "vampire's son", are used.
claims.statement_id: Di wilayah lain dipakai istilah seperti vampirović, vampijerović, dan vampirić dalam bahasa Serbia (dan lampijerović dalam bahasa Bosnia), yang berarti "putra vampir".
claims.quote: In the rest of the region, terms such as Serbian vampirović, vampijerović, vampirić (thus, Bosnian lampijerović, etc.) literally meaning "vampire's son", are used.

claims.statement: Legends say dhampirs were mostly ordinary community members, but they, especially males with a vampire father, could see invisible vampires and practise sorcery, often becoming vampire hunters from father to son.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, dhampir umumnya warga biasa, tetapi mereka, terutama laki-laki keturunan ayah vampir, dapat melihat vampir tak kasatmata dan mempraktikkan sihir, sering menjadi pemburu vampir turun-temurun dari ayah ke anak.
claims.quote: Legends state that dhampirs were, for the most part, normal members of the community. But dhampirs, especially males of paternal vampire descent, could see invisible vampires and practise sorcery, often starting careers as vampire hunters, which would be practiced for generations from father to son.

claims.statement: In Kosovo a dhampir (specifically a son) was seen as the chief magical agent for destroying vampires, and sometimes the only one able to see a vampire.
claims.statement_id: Di Kosovo, dhampir (khususnya putra) dipandang sebagai agen magis utama untuk membinasakan vampir, dan kadang dianggap satu-satunya yang mampu melihat vampir.
claims.quote: In Kosovo, a dhampir (specifically a son) was regarded as a "chief magical agent for the destruction of vampires", and sometimes the dhampir was thought to be the only one capable of seeing a vampire.

claims.statement: In Bulgarian folklore, possible signs include being very dirty and having a soft body with no nails or bones.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Bulgaria, tanda anak vampir antara lain sangat kotor, bertubuh lunak, serta tidak berkuku dan tidak bertulang.
claims.quote: In Bulgarian folklore, possible indications include being "very dirty", having a soft body, no nails or bones

claims.statement: Other signs were a prominent nose and unusually large ears, teeth or eyes.
claims.statement_id: Tanda lain adalah hidung yang menonjol serta telinga, gigi, atau mata yang lebih besar dari biasa.
claims.quote: In contrast, a pronounced nose was often a sign, as were larger than normal ears, teeth, or eyes.

claims.statement: In some areas a true dhampir had a slippery, jelly-like body and lived only a short life.
claims.statement_id: Di beberapa daerah, dhampir sejati dikatakan bertubuh licin seperti jeli dan berumur pendek.
claims.quote: in some areas, a true dhampir possessed a "slippery, jelly-like body and lived only a short life

claims.statement: Serbian ethnologist Tatomir Vukanović recorded that Muslims called half-vampire people "Dhampir" (male) and "Dhampiresa" (female).
claims.statement_id: Etnolog Serbia Tatomir Vukanović mencatat bahwa kaum Muslim menyebut orang setengah vampir "Dhampir" (laki-laki) dan "Dhampiresa" (perempuan).
claims.quote: Serbian ethnologist Tatomir Vukanović recorded that Muslims called half-vampire people "Dhampir" (masculine) and "Dhampiresa" (feminine).

claims.statement: A dhampir looks like an ordinary human but has the power to kill the undying vampire and the ability to detect vampires.
claims.statement_id: Penampilan dhampir tidak berbeda dari manusia biasa, tetapi ia memiliki kekuatan untuk membunuh vampir yang abadi serta kemampuan mendeteksi vampir.
claims.quote: 外見は普通の人間と変わらないが、不死である吸血鬼を殺す力を持つ。また、吸血鬼を探知する能力も備える。

claims.statement: Most dhampirs die soon after birth, but those who grow up sometimes use their abilities to make a living as vampire hunters.
claims.statement_id: Kebanyakan dhampir meninggal tak lama setelah lahir, tetapi yang tumbuh dewasa kadang memanfaatkan kemampuannya untuk mencari nafkah sebagai pemburu vampir.
claims.quote: 大抵は生まれてもすぐに死んでしまうが、成長した者は前述の能力を活かし、吸血鬼ハンターを生業とすることもある。

claims.statement: A dhampir's vampire hunt takes a ritual form: blowing a flute, running about and fighting an invisible foe, then declaring victory.
claims.statement_id: Perburuan vampir oleh dhampir berbentuk seperti ritual: meniup seruling, berlari ke sana kemari, dan bertarung dengan musuh tak terlihat, lalu menyatakan kemenangan.
claims.quote: ダンピールによる吸血鬼退治は、儀式のような形式を取る。笛を吹いたり、走り回ったり、目に見えない敵と戦った後、勝利を宣言する。

claims.statement: Someone who has become a vampire may return to the family of their human life, and some such vampires demand intercourse rather than blood.
claims.statement_id: Orang yang telah menjadi vampir kadang kembali kepada keluarganya semasa hidup, dan ada vampir yang saat itu meminta hubungan badan, bukan darah.
claims.quote: 吸血鬼になった者は、人間だったころの家族の下に戻ってくることがある。その際、血液ではなく性行為を要求する吸血鬼がいる。

claims.statement: The dhampir (ダンピール) is a human–vampire half-breed appearing in Eastern European and Russian legend.
claims.statement_id: Dhampir (ダンピール) adalah keturunan campuran manusia dan vampir yang muncul dalam legenda Eropa Timur dan Rusia.
claims.quote: ダンピール (Dhampir) は、東欧やロシアの伝説に登場する、ヒトと吸血鬼の混血。

claims.statement: The Sirin is a legendary creature in Russian folklore with a beautiful woman's head and a bird's body (usually an owl), often equated with the sirens of Greek mythology.
claims.statement_id: Sirin adalah makhluk legenda dalam cerita rakyat Rusia, berkepala perempuan cantik dan bertubuh burung (biasanya burung hantu), sering disamakan dengan siren dalam mitologi Yunani.
claims.quote: is a legendary creature in Russian folklore, with the head of a beautiful woman and the body of a bird (usually an owl), often equated with sirens in Greek mythology.

claims.statement: According to myth the Sirin lived in Iriy or around the Euphrates; she is considered the bird of happiness, related to the Alkonost, the bird of sorrow.
claims.statement_id: Menurut mitos, Sirin tinggal di Iriy atau di sekitar Sungai Efrat; ia dianggap burung kebahagiaan dan berkaitan dengan Alkonost, burung kesedihan.
claims.quote: According to myth, the Sirin lived in Iriy or around the Euphrates River. The Sirin is considered the bird of happiness; it is related to the Alkonost, the bird of sorrow.

claims.statement: The Sirin legend may be of Persian origin; the Pomors often drew her in Book of Genesis illustrations as birds sitting in paradise trees.
claims.statement_id: Legenda Sirin mungkin berasal dari Persia; orang Pomor sering menggambarkannya dalam ilustrasi Kitab Kejadian sebagai burung yang bertengger di pohon surga.
claims.quote: The legend of the Sirin may have a Persian origin. The Pomors often depicted the Sirin on illustrations in the Book of Genesis as birds sitting in paradise trees.

claims.statement: In the 17th–18th centuries the image of the Sirin changed and she came to symbolize world harmony, as she lives near paradise.
claims.statement_id: Pada abad ke-17–18, citra Sirin berubah dan ia mulai melambangkan keselarasan dunia karena tinggal di dekat surga.
