claims.quote: Later, in the 17th–18th centuries, the image of the Sirin changed and she started to symbolize world harmony (as she lives near paradise).

claims.statement: People then believed only happy people could hear the Sirin, and very few could see her, as she is as quick and elusive as human happiness.
claims.statement_id: Orang pada masa itu percaya hanya orang bahagia yang dapat mendengar Sirin, dan sangat sedikit yang bisa melihatnya karena ia secepat dan sesulit ditangkap seperti kebahagiaan manusia.
claims.quote: People in those times believed only happy people could hear the Sirin, while only very few could see one because she is as fast and difficult to catch as human happiness.

claims.statement: Instead of using her voice to lure sailors to death, the Sirin uses it to reward the virtuous; she was usually shown wearing a crown or a nimbus.
claims.statement_id: Alih-alih memakai suaranya untuk memikat pelaut menuju maut, Sirin memakainya untuk mengganjar orang saleh; ia biasanya digambarkan bermahkota atau berlingkaran cahaya.
claims.quote: However, instead of using its voice to lure sailors to their deaths, the Sirin uses it to reward the virtuous. She was usually portrayed wearing a crown or with a nimbus.

claims.statement: The Sirin sang beautiful songs to the saints, foretelling future bliss; the bird was dangerous, for men who heard her forgot everything on earth, followed her and finally died.
claims.statement_id: Sirin menyanyikan lagu indah bagi para santo, meramalkan kebahagiaan mendatang; burung ini berbahaya, karena laki-laki yang mendengarnya melupakan segala hal di bumi, mengikutinya, dan akhirnya mati.
claims.quote: The Sirin sang beautiful songs to the saints, foretelling future blisses. The bird was dangerous. Men who heard her would forget everything on earth, follow her, and ultimately die.

claims.statement: People tried to save themselves from the Sirin by firing cannons, ringing bells and making other loud noises to scare her off.
claims.statement_id: Orang berusaha menyelamatkan diri dari Sirin dengan menembakkan meriam, membunyikan lonceng, dan membuat bunyi keras lain untuk mengusirnya.
claims.quote: People would attempt to save themselves from the Sirin by shooting cannons, ringing bells and making other loud noises to scare the bird off.

claims.statement: According to folk tales, on the morning of the Apple Feast of the Saviour, the Sirin flies into the apple orchard and cries sadly.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kisah rakyat, pada pagi Pesta Apel Sang Juru Selamat, Sirin terbang ke kebun apel dan menangis sedih.
claims.quote: According to folk tales, on the morning of the Apple Feast of the Saviour, the Sirin flies into the apple orchard and cries sadly.

claims.statement: The Sirin is sometimes seen as a metaphor for God's word entering a man's soul, and sometimes for heretics tempting the weak.
claims.statement_id: Sirin kadang dipandang sebagai kiasan firman Tuhan yang masuk ke jiwa manusia, kadang sebagai kiasan bidah yang menggoda orang lemah.
claims.quote: The Sirin is sometimes seen as a metaphor for God's word going into the soul of a man. Sometimes she is seen as a metaphor of heretics tempting the weak.

claims.statement: In Russian folklore the Sirin was mixed up with the religious writer Ephrem the Syrian, so peasant poets such as Nikolay Klyuev used Sirin as a synonym for poet.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Rusia, Sirin dicampuradukkan dengan penulis religius Ephrem the Syrian, sehingga penyair petani seperti Nikolay Klyuev memakai Sirin sebagai sinonim untuk penyair.
claims.quote: In Russian folklore, Sirin was mixed with the revered religious writer, Ephrem the Syrian. Thus, peasant lyrists such as Nikolay Klyuev often used the Sirin as a synonym for poet.

claims.statement: The Sirin are magic birds of grief and sorrow, in contrast to the Alkonost, birds of happiness and hope; the Sirin are rather ill-disposed to humans, the Alkonost are not.
claims.statement_id: Sirin adalah burung ajaib duka dan kesedihan, berlawanan dengan Alkonost, burung kebahagiaan dan harapan; Sirin cenderung berniat buruk kepada manusia, sedangkan Alkonost tidak.
claims.quote: Die Sirin sind die magischen Vögel der Trauer und des Kummers. Im Gegensatz dazu stehen die Alkonost, die Vögel des Glücks und der Hoffnung. Die Sirin sind den Menschen eher böse gesinnt, die Alkonost hingegen nicht.

claims.statement: Sirin (Russian Сирин) is a legendary figure of Russian folk belief: birds resembling owls but with the head and breast of a beautiful woman.
claims.statement_id: Sirin (bahasa Rusia Сирин) adalah tokoh legenda kepercayaan rakyat Rusia, berupa burung yang mirip burung hantu tetapi berkepala dan berdada perempuan cantik.
claims.quote: Sirin (russisch Сирин) ist der Name einer Sagengestalt des russischen Volksglaubens. Es handelt sich um Vögel, die rein äußerlich Eulen ähneln, aber Kopf und Brust einer schönen Frau besitzen.

claims.statement: The Sirin is one of the prophetic birds of Russian folklore, with the Alkonost and Gamayun.
claims.statement_id: Sirin adalah salah satu burung peramal dalam cerita rakyat Rusia, bersama Alkonost dan Gamayun.
claims.quote: Elle est un des oiseaux prophétiques du folklore russe avec Alkonost et Gamayun.

claims.statement: The Sirin was also considered a siren or the equivalent of the Polish Wila.
claims.statement_id: Sirin juga dianggap sebagai siren atau padanan Wila Polandia.
claims.quote: Sirin était aussi considérée comme une sirène ou l’équivalent de la Wila polonaise.

claims.statement: The author Vladimir Nabokov published under the pseudonym Sirin.
claims.statement_id: Pengarang Vladimir Nabokov menerbitkan karya dengan nama samaran Sirin.
claims.quote: Author Vladimir Nabokov published under the pseudonym Sirin.

claims.statement: Few can see the Sirin, because she flies very fast.
claims.statement_id: Jarang ada yang bisa melihat Sirin karena ia terbang sangat cepat.
claims.quote: Rares sont ceux qui peuvent la voir, car elle vole très vite.

claims.statement: Her song bewitches people, who lose their memory, and only a happy man can hear it.
claims.statement_id: Nyanyiannya menyihir orang hingga mereka kehilangan ingatan, dan hanya orang bahagia yang dapat mendengarnya.
claims.quote: Son chant ensorcelle les gens qui en perdent la mémoire. Seul un homme heureux peut entendre ce chant.

claims.statement: Sirin or Sirine (Russian Сирин) is a Slavic mythological creature found especially in Russian legends.
claims.statement_id: Sirin atau Sirine (bahasa Rusia Сирин) adalah makhluk mitologi Slavia yang terutama ditemukan dalam legenda Rusia.
claims.quote: Sirin ou Sirine (en russe : Сирин) est une créature mythologique slave que l’on trouve plus particulièrement dans les légendes russes.

claims.statement: The Wawel Dragon, also known as the Dragon of Wawel Hill, is a famous dragon in Polish legend.
claims.statement_id: Naga Wawel, juga dikenal sebagai Naga Bukit Wawel (Dragon of Wawel Hill), adalah naga terkenal dalam legenda Polandia.
claims.quote: also known as the Dragon of Wawel Hill, is a famous dragon in Polish legend.

claims.statement: According to the earliest account (13th century), a dragon (holophagos, "one who swallows whole") plagued the capital Kraków, founded by the legendary King Krak.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kisah tertua (abad ke-13), seekor naga (holophagos, "yang menelan bulat-bulat") mengganggu ibu kota Kraków yang didirikan Raja Krak yang legendaris.
claims.quote: According to the earliest account (13th century), a dragon (holophagos, "one who swallows whole") plagued the capital city of Kraków established by legendary King Krak (or Krakus, Gracchus, etc.).

claims.statement: The man-eating monster was appeased with a weekly ration of cattle until the king's sons defeated it with decoy cows stuffed with sulfur.
claims.statement_id: Monster pemakan manusia itu ditenangkan dengan jatah ternak setiap minggu, sampai akhirnya dikalahkan putra-putra raja dengan sapi umpan berisi belerang.
claims.quote: The man-eating monster was being appeased with a weekly ration of cattle, until finally being defeated by the king's sons using decoy cows stuffed with sulfur.

claims.statement: But the younger prince murdered his elder brother to take sole credit and was afterwards banished.
claims.statement_id: Namun pangeran yang lebih muda membunuh kakaknya agar mendapat pujian sendirian, lalu diusir.
claims.quote: But the younger prince ("Krak the younger" or "Krak junior") murdered his elder brother to take sole credit, and was banished afterwards.

claims.statement: The oldest known telling comes from a 13th-century work attributed to the Bishop of Kraków and Polish historian Wincenty Kadłubek.
claims.statement_id: Kisah tertua yang diketahui berasal dari karya abad ke-13 yang dikaitkan dengan Uskup Kraków dan sejarawan Polandia, Wincenty Kadłubek.
claims.quote: The oldest known telling of the story comes from the 13th-century work attributed to Bishop of Kraków and historian of Poland, Wincenty Kadłubek.

claims.statement: They fed him a cattle skin stuffed with smouldering sulfur, causing his fiery death.
claims.statement_id: Mereka memberinya kulit sapi berisi belerang membara sehingga naga mati terbakar.
claims.quote: They fed him a cattle skin stuffed with smoldering sulfur, causing his fiery death.

claims.statement: Jan Długosz's 15th-century chronicle swapped the princes' roles: the younger son Lech was the killer and the elder son Krak Jr. the victim.
claims.statement_id: Kronik abad ke-15 karya Jan Długosz menukar peran kedua pangeran: putra bungsu bernama Lech menjadi pembunuh, sedangkan putra sulung Krak muda menjadi korban.
claims.quote: Jan Długosz's 15th-century chronicle, however, swapped the roles of the princes, claiming that the younger son named Lech was the killer, while the elder son named Krak, Jr. became the victim.

claims.statement: The dragon ate the burning bait and breathed fire just before dying; Długosz adds that it lived in a cave of Mount Wawel, where King Krak had built his castle.
claims.statement_id: Naga memakan umpan yang menyala dan mati sambil menyemburkan api sesaat sebelumnya; Długosz menambahkan bahwa naga tinggal di gua Gunung Wawel, tempat Raja Krak membangun istananya.
claims.quote: The dragon ate the burning meal and died breathing fire just before death. Długosz also adds the detail that the dragon lived in a cave of Mount Wawel upon which King Krak had built his castle.

claims.statement: Later, Marcin Bielski's Kronika Polska (1597) credited Skub or Skuba the Cobbler.
claims.statement_id: Kemudian Kronika Polska karya Marcin Bielski (1597) memberi jasa kepada Skub atau Skuba, si tukang sepatu.
claims.quote: Later, Marcin Bielski's Kronika Polska (1597) gave credit to Skub or Skuba the Cobbler

claims.statement: The dragon could not swallow it and drank water until it died; the shoemaker was then richly rewarded.
claims.statement_id: Naga tidak dapat menelan umpan itu dan minum air sampai mati; tukang sepatu itu kemudian diberi hadiah besar.
claims.quote: The dragon was unable to swallow this, and drank water until it died. Afterwards, the shoemaker was rewarded handsomely.

claims.statement: It is said to have lived in Smocza Jama (the dragon's cave) beneath Wawel Hill on the banks of the Vistula.
claims.statement_id: Naga itu konon tinggal di Smocza Jama (gua naga) di bawah Bukit Wawel di tepi Sungai Vistula (Weichsel).
claims.quote: Er soll in der Smocza Jama (Drachenhöhle) unter dem Wawelhügel an den Ufern der Weichsel gehaust haben.

claims.statement: One day a young shoemaker's apprentice named Dratewka took on the task; he filled a dead lamb with sulfur and left it before the dragon's lair.
claims.statement_id: Suatu hari seorang magang tukang sepatu muda bernama Dratewka menyanggupi tugas itu; ia mengisi bangkai domba dengan belerang dan meletakkannya di depan sarang naga.
claims.quote: Eines Tages meldete sich ein junger Schusterlehrling namens Dratewka für die Aufgabe. Er füllte ein totes Lamm mit Schwefel (nach manchen Versionen auch Ätzkali) und ließ es vor dem Drachenhort liegen.

claims.statement: The dragon drank until its belly burst with water and it died; Dratewka was allowed to marry the king's daughter and lived happily.
claims.statement_id: Naga minum terus sampai perutnya pecah karena air dan mati; Dratewka lalu boleh menikahi putri raja dan hidup bahagia.
claims.quote: Er trank so lange, bis er vor lauter Wasser im Bauch platzte und verendete. Dratewka durfte nun die Königstochter heiraten und lebte fortan glücklich mit ihr weiter.

claims.statement: In most versions the dragon preferred to eat young girls and could only be soothed by a monthly offering of a girl in front of its cave.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kebanyakan versi, naga lebih suka memangsa gadis muda dan hanya bisa ditenangkan dengan persembahan seorang gadis setiap bulan di depan guanya.
claims.quote: In den meisten Versionen bevorzugte der Drache junge Mädchen zu fressen, man konnte ihn nur durch die monatliche Darbietung eines Mädchens vor seiner Höhle besänftigen.

claims.statement: In 1970 a metal sculpture of the Wawel Dragon designed by Bronisław Chromy was set up in front of the dragon's cave.
claims.statement_id: Pada tahun 1970 patung logam Naga Wawel rancangan Bronisław Chromy dipasang di depan gua naga.
claims.quote: Im Jahr 1970 wurde eine Metallskulptur des Wawel-Drachen, entworfen von Bronisław Chromy, vor der Höhle des Drachen aufgestellt

claims.statement: As a special feature, the sculpture spits a flame from its nostrils via a natural-gas nozzle every five minutes or on receiving an SMS.
claims.statement_id: Keistimewaan patung itu: ia menyemburkan api dari lubang hidungnya lewat nosel gas alam setiap lima menit atau setelah menerima pesan SMS.
claims.quote: Als Besonderheit spuckt er mittels einer Erdgasdüse alle fünf Minuten, oder nach Empfang einer SMS-Nachricht, eine Fackelflamme aus seinen Nüstern.

claims.statement: The Late Triassic archosaur Smok wawelski was named after the Wawel Dragon.
claims.statement_id: Archosaurus Smok wawelski dari zaman Trias Akhir dinamai menurut Naga Wawel.
claims.quote: Der Archosaurier Smok wawelski aus der Obertrias wurde nach dem Wawel-Drachen benannt.

claims.statement: The Wawel Dragon (Polish: Smok Wawelski) is a dragon of Polish folk legend.
claims.statement_id: Naga Wawel (bahasa Polandia: Smok Wawelski) adalah naga dalam legenda rakyat Polandia.
claims.quote: Der Wawel-Drache (polnisch: Smok Wawelski) ist ein Drache in der polnischen Volkssage.

claims.statement: Every day the evil dragon cut a path of destruction through the land, killing citizens, burning their homes and devouring their livestock.
claims.statement_id: Setiap hari naga jahat itu membuat jalur kehancuran di negeri itu, membunuh warga, membakar rumah mereka, dan melahap ternak mereka.
claims.quote: An jedem Tag schlug der böse Drache einen Pfad der Zerstörung durch das Land, tötete die Bürger, steckte ihre Heime in Brand und verschlang ihr Vieh.

claims.statement: The mavka is a type of female spirit in Ukrainian folklore and mythology, a long-haired "Soul of the Forest" usually shown as a temptress luring men to their deaths.
claims.statement_id: Mavka adalah sejenis roh perempuan dalam cerita rakyat dan mitologi Ukraina; ia "jiwa hutan" berambut panjang yang biasanya digambarkan sebagai penggoda yang memikat laki-laki menuju kematian.
claims.quote: is a type of female spirit in Ukrainian folklore and mythology. The Mavka is a long-haired "Soul of the Forest", typically depicted as a temptress figure who lures men to their deaths.

claims.statement: All these terms derive from *navь, "the dead", and are cognate with a Bulgarian word.
claims.statement_id: Semua istilah ini berasal dari *navь, "orang mati", dan seasal dengan kata Bulgaria.
claims.quote: These terms all derive from *navь 'the dead', and are cognate with Bulgarian

claims.statement: The spirits known by this term were the souls of girls who died unnatural, tragic or premature deaths, particularly unbaptized babies.
claims.statement_id: Roh yang dikenal dengan istilah ini mewakili jiwa gadis yang mati secara tidak wajar, tragis, atau terlalu dini, terutama bayi yang belum dibaptis.
claims.quote: The spirits known by this term represented the souls of girls who had died unnatural, tragic or premature deaths, particularly unchristened babies.

claims.statement: Mavkas often appear as beautiful young girls who lure young men into the woods and "tickle" them to death; they have no reflection in water and cast no shadows.
claims.statement_id: Mavka sering tampil sebagai gadis muda cantik yang memikat pemuda ke hutan lalu "menggelitik" mereka sampai mati; mavka tidak memantulkan bayangan di air dan tidak berbayang.
claims.quote: Mavkas often appear in the form of beautiful young girls who entice and lure young men into the woods, where they "tickle" them to death. Mavkas have no reflection in water, nor do they cast shadows.

claims.statement: In some accounts they also helped farmers by tending cattle and driving out wild animals.
claims.statement_id: Menurut beberapa kisah, mereka juga membantu petani dengan menjaga ternak dan mengusir binatang liar.
claims.quote: In some accounts, they were also said to help farmers by looking after cattle and driving out wild animals.

claims.statement: A subtype of mavkas are the nyavkas, who behave the same but have "no back", so their spine and some inner organs can be seen.
claims.statement_id: Subjenis mavka adalah nyavka, yang berperilaku sama tetapi "tidak berpunggung", sehingga tulang belakang dan sebagian organ dalamnya terlihat.
claims.quote: A subtype of the Mavkas are the Nyavkas, which behave the same except for having "no back", meaning that their spine and some other insides can be seen

claims.statement: Mavkas and nyavkas were believed to live in groups in forests, mountain caves or sheds that they decorated with rugs.
claims.statement_id: Mavka dan nyavka dipercaya hidup berkelompok di hutan, gua gunung, atau gudang yang mereka hiasi permadani.
claims.quote: Mavkas and Nyavkas were believed to live in groups in forests, mountain caves, or sheds, which they decorated with rugs.

claims.statement: In spring they planted flowers in the mountains, where they lured young men and tickled them to death.
claims.statement_id: Pada musim semi mereka menanam bunga di pegunungan, tempat mereka memikat pemuda lalu menggelitiknya sampai mati.
claims.quote: In the spring, they planted flowers in the mountains, to which they enticed young men, whom they tickled to death.

claims.statement: If the soul lasted up to seven years without going to heaven, the baby would turn into a mavka and haunt the earth.
claims.statement_id: Bila jiwa itu bertahan hingga tujuh tahun tanpa masuk surga, bayi itu berubah menjadi mavka dan bergentayangan di bumi.
claims.quote: If the soul lived up to seven years and did not go to heaven, the baby would turn into a mavka and haunt the earth.

claims.statement: To save an unbaptized baby's soul, one must toss up a kerchief during the Pentecost holidays, say its name and add "I baptise you".
claims.statement_id: Untuk menyelamatkan jiwa bayi yang belum dibaptis, orang harus melempar kain kepala ke atas saat hari raya Pentakosta, menyebut namanya, dan menambahkan "aku membaptismu".
claims.quote: To save an unchristened baby's soul, one must throw up a kerchief during Pentecost holidays, say their name and add "I baptise you"

claims.statement: Mavkas are depicted in literature, most notably in Lesia Ukrainka's The Forest Song.
claims.statement_id: Mavka digambarkan dalam sastra, terutama dalam The Forest Song karya Lesia Ukrainka.
claims.quote: Mavkas are depicted in literature, most notably in Lesia Ukrainka's The Forest Song

claims.statement: The 2023 film Mavka: The Forest Song is based on Ukrainian mythology.
claims.statement_id: Film tahun 2023 Mavka: The Forest Song berdasarkan mitologi Ukraina.
claims.quote: The 2023 film Mavka: The Forest Song, is based on Ukrainian mythology.

claims.statement: Mawka (Ukrainian Мавка) is a female figure of Ukrainian mythology.
claims.statement_id: Mawka (bahasa Ukraina Мавка) adalah sosok perempuan dalam mitologi Ukraina.
claims.quote: Mawka (ukrainisch Мавка) ist eine weibliche Gestalt aus der ukrainischen Mythologie.

claims.statement: The word Mawka comes from Naw, Old Slavic for "the dead", a term for the spirits of mortals who died tragically and too early.
claims.statement_id: Kata Mawka berasal dari Naw, yang dalam bahasa Slavia Kuno berarti "orang mati", istilah untuk arwah manusia yang meninggal secara tragis dan terlalu cepat.
claims.quote: Das Wort Mawka kommt von Naw, was auf Altslawisch „Toter“ bedeutet und ein Begriff für Geister der Sterblichen, die tragisch und zu früh gestorben waren, ist.

claims.statement: Outwardly they are described as female figures, tall, round-faced, long-haired and sometimes naked.
claims.statement_id: Secara lahiriah mereka digambarkan sebagai sosok perempuan yang tinggi, berwajah bulat, berambut panjang, dan kadang telanjang.
claims.quote: Äußerlich werden sie als weibliche Figur, groß, mit einem runden Gesicht, langem Haar und manchmal nackt beschrieben.

claims.statement: The mavka differs from other female spirits in that her evil is unintentional; on seeing a young man she falls into a trance and realizes her actions too late.
claims.statement_id: Mavka berbeda dari roh perempuan lain karena kejahatannya tidak disengaja; saat melihat pemuda ia jatuh dalam keadaan tak sadar dan baru menyadari perbuatannya ketika sudah terlambat.
claims.quote: Mavka is different from other types of female spirits in that her evil is not intentional. At the sight of a young man, she falls into a trance and realizes her actions too late to change anything.

claims.statement: At Pentecost they held games, dances and orgies, accompanied by a demon on flute or pipes.
claims.statement_id: Saat Pentakosta mereka mengadakan permainan, tarian, dan pesta pora, diiringi setan yang memainkan seruling atau pipa.
claims.quote: they held games, dances, and orgies. A demon accompanied them on a flute or pipes.

claims.statement: A Slavic dragon is any dragon in Slavic mythology, including the Polish żmij and the Russian zmei (zmey, змей).
claims.statement_id: Naga Slavia adalah naga mana pun dalam mitologi Slavia, termasuk żmij dari Polandia dan zmei (zmey, змей) dari Rusia.
claims.quote: A Slavic dragon is any dragon in Slavic mythology, including the Polish żmij, Russian zmei (or zmey;

claims.statement: Its appearance combines the classical dragon and a snake (a winged serpent), less often shown with two legs and/or more than one head.
claims.statement_id: Wujudnya menyerupai perpaduan naga klasik dan ular (sebagai ular bersayap), lebih jarang digambarkan berkaki dua dan/atau berkepala lebih dari satu.
claims.quote: The physiognomy resembles a combination of the classical dragon and a snake (as a winged serpent), less often depicted with two legs and/or more than one head.

claims.statement: A zmei may be beast-like or human-like (dragon form in the air, human form on the ground), sometimes wooing women, but often the chief antagonist in Russian literature.
claims.statement_id: Zmei bisa berwujud binatang atau mirip manusia (berwujud naga di udara, manusia di darat), kadang merayu perempuan, tetapi sering menjadi musuh utama dalam sastra Rusia.
claims.quote: A zmei may be beast-like or human-like (assuming dragon form in air, human form on ground), sometimes wooing women, but often plays the role of chief antagonist in Russian literature.

claims.statement: In the Balkans the zmei type is generally regarded as benevolent, unlike malevolent dragons such as the lamia.
claims.statement_id: Di Balkan, zmei pada umumnya dianggap baik, berbeda dari naga jahat yang dikenal sebagai lamia.
claims.quote: In the Balkans, the zmei type is overall regarded as benevolent, as opposed to malevolent dragons known variously as lamia

claims.statement: Common motifs include Slavic dragons as masters of weather or water sources, their start in life as snakes, and both males and females having romances with humans.
claims.statement_id: Motif umum tentang naga Slavia antara lain perannya sebagai penguasa cuaca atau sumber air, asal-usulnya sebagai ular, dan bahwa naga jantan maupun betina bisa menjalin cinta dengan manusia.
claims.quote: Some of the common motifs concerning Slavic dragons include their identification as masters of weather or water sources; that they start life as snakes; and that both the male and female can be romantically involved with humans.

claims.statement: The Slavic terms descend from Proto-Slavic *zmьjь.
claims.statement_id: Istilah-istilah Slavia untuk naga berasal dari Proto-Slavia *zmьjь.
claims.quote: The Slavic terms descend from Proto-Slavic *zmьjь.

claims.statement: In Russian lore, when a serpent, lizard, rooster or carp reaches a certain age, such as 9 or 40 years, it turns into a flying zmei.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan Rusia, bila ular, kadal, ayam jantan, atau ikan mas mencapai umur tertentu, misalnya 9 atau 40 tahun, ia berubah menjadi zmei terbang.
claims.quote: or some other serpent, lizard, rooster, or carp achieves certain longevity, such as 9 years or 40 years, it transmutes into a flying zmei.

claims.statement: In the legends of Russia and Ukraine, the dragon-like Zmey Gorynych has three to twelve heads.
claims.statement_id: Dalam legenda Rusia dan Ukraina, makhluk mirip naga bernama Zmey Gorynych memiliki tiga sampai dua belas kepala.
claims.quote: In the legends of Russia and Ukraine, a particular dragon-like creature, Zmey Gorynych ... has three to twelve heads

claims.statement: There is a notion (thought to be inspired by tornadoes) of a Slavic dragon that dips its tail into a river or lake and siphons up water, ready to cause floods.
claims.statement_id: Ada gagasan (yang diduga diilhami angin puting beliung) tentang naga Slavia yang mencelupkan ekornya ke sungai atau danau dan menyedot airnya, siap menimbulkan banjir.
claims.quote: There is the notion (thought to be inspired by the tornado) of a Slavic dragon that dips its tail into a river or lake and siphons up the water, ready to cause floods.

claims.statement: In Bulgarian lore the zmei is sometimes a scaly serpent-like creature with four legs and bat wings, at other times half man, half snake with wings and a fish-like tail.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan Bulgaria, zmei kadang digambarkan sebagai makhluk mirip ular bersisik dengan empat kaki dan sayap kelelawar, kadang setengah manusia setengah ular dengan sayap dan ekor seperti ikan.
claims.quote: In Bulgarian lore, the zmei is sometimes described as a scale-covered serpent-like creature with four legs and bat's wings, at other times as half-man, half-snake, with wings and a fish-like tail.

claims.statement: Most of these dragon names are masculine forms of the Slavic word for "snake".
claims.statement_id: Sebagian besar nama naga Slavia adalah bentuk maskulin dari kata Slavia untuk "ular".
claims.quote: Die meisten der oben genannten Namen sind die männlichen Formen des slawischen Begriffes für „Schlange“

claims.statement: In Slovenia dragons are usually placed on the malevolent side and mostly depicted together with St. Georg.
claims.statement_id: Di Slovenia (Slowenien), naga biasanya digolongkan jahat dan sering digambarkan bersama Santo Georg (St. Georg).
claims.quote: Drachen sind in Slowenien normalerweise im böswilligen Bereich angesiedelt, und sie werden meist gemeinsam mit St. Georg dargestellt.

claims.statement: Dragons are not always hostile to humans; the Ljubljanski Zmaj protects the city of Ljubljana and so appears on its coat of arms.
claims.statement_id: Namun naga tidak selalu memusuhi manusia; Ljubljanski Zmaj (naga Ljubljana) melindungi kota Ljubljana dan karena itu tampil di lambang kotanya.
claims.quote: Drachen sind jedoch nicht immer dem Menschen feindlich gesinnt. So beschützt etwa der Ljubljanski Zmaj (Laibacher Drache) die Stadt Ljubljana und wird dafür auch auf dem Stadtwappen abgebildet.

claims.statement: The Slavic dragon is the counterpart of the classical European dragon in Slavic mythology.
claims.statement_id: Naga Slavia adalah padanan naga Eropa klasik dalam mitologi Slavia.
claims.quote: Der Slawische Drache ist die Entsprechung des klassischen europäischen Drachen in der slawischen Mythologie.

claims.statement: Zmei Gorynych is three-headed and green, walks on two hind legs, has rather small forelegs and can breathe fire.
claims.statement_id: Zmei Gorynytsch berkepala tiga dan berwarna hijau, berjalan dengan dua kaki belakang, berkaki depan kecil, dan dapat menyemburkan api.
claims.quote: Er ist dreiköpfig und grün, geht auf seinen zwei Hinterbeinen, besitzt eher kleine Vorderbeine und kann Feuer spucken.

claims.statement: The Polish smok (e.g. the Wawel Dragon of Kraków) and the Ukrainian or Belarusian smok or tsmok can also be included.
claims.statement_id: Smok dari Polandia (misalnya Naga Wawel dari Kraków) serta smok atau tsmok dari Ukraina dan Belarus juga dapat dimasukkan.
claims.quote: The Polish smok (e.g. Wawel Dragon of Kraków) or the Ukrainian or Belarusian smok (смок), tsmok (цмок), can also be included.

claims.statement: The Romanian zmeu could also be considered a "Slavic" dragon, but a non-cognate etymology has been proposed.
claims.statement_id: Zmeu dari Romania juga bisa dianggap naga "Slavia", tetapi ada usulan etimologi yang tidak seasal.
claims.quote: The Romanian zmeu could also be deemed a "Slavic" dragon, but a non-cognate etymology has been proposed.

claims.statement: There is a pan-Balkan notion that the zmei is a kind of "guardian-spirit dragon" against the "evil" kinds of dragon.
claims.statement_id: Ada gagasan di seluruh Balkan bahwa zmei adalah semacam "naga roh penjaga" yang melawan jenis-jenis naga "jahat".
claims.quote: There is a pan-Balkan notion that the zmei (known by various cognates) is a sort of "guardian-spirit dragon" against the "evil" types of dragon

claims.statement: A favourite theme of folk songs was the male zmey lover who may marry a woman and carry her to the underworld, or a female zmeitsa who falls for a shepherd.
claims.statement_id: Tema kesukaan lagu rakyat adalah zmey jantan yang menikahi perempuan dan membawanya ke dunia bawah, atau zmeitsa betina yang jatuh cinta kepada penggembala.
claims.quote: A favorite topic of folk songs was the male zmey-lover who may marry a woman and carry her to the underworld, or a female zmeitsa (zmeitza) who falls in love with a shepherd.

claims.statement: In Finnish folklore Ajatar is an evil female spirit described with a braid reaching her heels and breasts hanging to her knees.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Finlandia, Ajatar adalah roh perempuan jahat yang digambarkan berkepang rambut sampai ke tumit dan berpayudara menjuntai sampai ke lutut.
claims.quote: In Finnish folklore Ajatar is an evil female spirit. She is described as having "hair-plait reached to her heels and whose breasts hung down to her knees"

claims.statement: Through her ties to Hiisi and Lempo she is said to spread disease and pestilence; she is closely linked with serpents and modern art often shows her as a dragon or half-human, serpentine figure.
claims.statement_id: Lewat hubungannya dengan Hiisi dan Lempo, ia dikatakan menyebarkan penyakit dan wabah; ia erat dikaitkan dengan ular dan dalam seni modern sering digambarkan sebagai naga atau sosok setengah manusia setengah ular.
claims.quote: Through her connections with Hiisi and Lempo, she is said to spread disease and pestilence. She is closely associated with serpents, and is often depicted in modern art as a dragon or half-humanoid and serpentine figure.

claims.statement: Daniel Juslenius called Ajattara an evil witch and forest troll; according to Christian Erici Lencqvist she is an evil female forest haltija (spirit), frightening and fast, who leads people astray.
claims.statement_id: Daniel Juslenius menyebut Ajattara penyihir jahat dan troll hutan; menurut Christian Erici Lencqvist, Ajattara adalah haltija (roh) hutan perempuan yang jahat, menakutkan, cepat, dan menyesatkan orang.
claims.quote: Daniel Juslenius called Ajattara an evil witch and a forest troll. According to Christian Erici Lencqvist, Ajattara is a female evil forest haltija, who is scary and fast and drives people astray.

claims.statement: Eemil Nestor Setälä showed that Ajattara may appear in Western Finnish runic songs as Aattara in the origin of snakes.
claims.statement_id: Eemil Nestor Setälä menunjukkan bahwa Ajattara mungkin muncul dalam lagu rune Finlandia Barat sebagai Aattara dalam kisah asal-usul ular.
claims.quote: Eemil Nestor Setälä demonstrated that Ajattara might appear in Western Finnish runic songs as Aattara in the origin of snakes

claims.statement: The word "ajatar" possibly derives from the Finnish ajattaa, "to pursue" (also "to drive").
claims.statement_id: Kata "ajatar" mungkin berasal dari kata Finlandia ajattaa, "mengejar" (juga "menggiring").
claims.quote: The word “ajatar” is possibly derived from the Finnish word ajattaa, “to pursue" (also, "to drive").

claims.statement: For Ajatar, the verb ajaa takes the feminine suffix -tar, meaning "female pursuer".
claims.statement_id: Pada nama Ajatar, kata kerja ajaa diberi akhiran feminin -tar sehingga berarti "pengejar perempuan".
claims.quote: Applying this to Ajatar, the verb ajaa is suffixed by the feminine "-tar," translating as “female pursuer.”

claims.statement: The form "Ajatar" was coined by Matthias Castrén to standardize the name.
claims.statement_id: Bentuk "Ajatar" diciptakan Matthias Castrén untuk membakukan nama itu.
claims.quote: The form "Ajatar" was invented by Matthias Castrén to standarize the name.

claims.statement: Although Ajatar does not appear by name in documented Finnish folk songs, she appears in fiction inspired by the Kalevala and in modern fantasy.
claims.statement_id: Walaupun Ajatar tidak muncul dengan nama itu dalam lagu rakyat Finlandia yang terdokumentasi, ia muncul dalam fiksi yang terilhami Kalevala dan dalam tafsiran fantasi modern.
claims.quote: Although Ajatar does not appear by name in documented Finnish folk songs, she appears in fiction inspired by the Kalevala and in modern fantasy interpretations.

claims.statement: In the second act of Aleksis Kivi's play Kullervo (1860), Ajatar is ferocious and shameless, urging the hero to kill his master's family.
claims.statement_id: Dalam babak kedua drama Kullervo karya Aleksis Kivi (1860), Ajatar digambarkan buas dan tak tahu malu, mendorong tokoh utama membunuh keluarga majikannya.
claims.quote: In the second act of Aleksis Kivi's play, Kullervo (1860), Ajatar is described as ferocious and shameless, encouraging the protagonist to kill his master’s family.

claims.statement: Ajatar (also Ajattara or Aijo) is an evil forest spirit in dragon form in Finnish mythology; she is said to be the devil's mother, spread disease and plague and suckle serpents, and anyone who looks at her falls ill.
claims.statement_id: Ajatar (juga Ajattara atau Aijo) adalah roh hutan jahat berwujud naga dalam mitologi Finlandia; konon ia ibu iblis, menyebarkan penyakit dan wabah, menyusui ular, dan siapa pun yang memandangnya jatuh sakit.
claims.quote: Ajatar (auch Ajattara oder Aijo) ist ein böser Waldgeist in der Gestalt eines Drachen in der finnischen Mythologie. Es wird gesagt, dass Ajatar die Mutter des Teufels ist, Krankheiten und Seuchen verbreitet und Schlangen stillt. Jeder, der sie anschaut, wird dabei selbst krank.

claims.statement: According to other traditions, Ajatara is a bewitchingly beautiful female guardian spirit at whose feet the male gods lie.
claims.statement_id: Menurut tradisi lain, Ajatara adalah roh pelindung perempuan yang sangat memesona, yang dihormati para dewa laki-laki.
claims.quote: Anderen Überlieferungen zufolge ist Ajatara ein betörend schöner, weiblicher Schutzgeist, dem die männlichen Götter zu Füßen liegen.

claims.statement: In Finnish folklore the Ajattar, also spelled Aiatar, Ajattaro or Ajattara, is a spirit.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Finlandia, Ajattar, juga ditulis Aiatar, Ajattaro, atau Ajattara, adalah sebuah roh.
claims.quote: Dans le folklore finlandais, l'Ajattar, également écrit Aiatar, Ajattaro ou Ajattara, est un esprit connu sous le nom de

claims.statement: Ajatar is linked to the Lithuanian Aitvaras and the Estonian Äi, Äijo or Äijattar.
claims.statement_id: Ajatar dikaitkan dengan Aitvaras dari Lituania serta Äi, Äijo, atau Äijattar dari Estonia.
claims.quote: Ajatar est liée à l'Aitvaras lituanien et l'Äi, Äijo ou Äijattar estonien.

claims.statement: J. Mikkola linked the name to the Lithuanian aitvaras, "nightmare, kratt, will-o'-the-wisp".
claims.statement_id: J. Mikkola menghubungkan nama ini dengan kata Lituania aitvaras, "mimpi buruk, kratt, cahaya hantu".
claims.quote: J. Mikkola connected the name to the Lithuanian word aitvaras 'nightmare, kratt, will o' wisp'.

claims.statement: Christfried Ganander listed it as an evil being or witch, and in 1789 wrote that Ajattara meant a nightmare.
claims.statement_id: Christfried Ganander mencatatnya sebagai makhluk jahat atau penyihir, dan pada tahun 1789 menulis bahwa Ajattara berarti mimpi buruk.
claims.quote: but was also listed by Christfried Ganander as an evil being or a witch, just like Ajattara, which Ganander wrote meant a nightmare in 1789.

claims.statement: Poludnitsa (from Polden or Poluden, "half-day" or "midday") is a mythical character common to various Slavic countries of Eastern Europe.
claims.statement_id: Poludnitsa (dari Polden atau Poluden, "setengah hari" atau "tengah hari") adalah tokoh mitos yang dikenal di berbagai negeri Slavia di Eropa Timur.
claims.quote: Poludnitsa (from: Polden or Poluden, 'half-day' or 'midday') is a mythical character common to the various Slavic countries of Eastern Europe.

claims.statement: Poludnitsa is a noon demon in Slavic mythology, called in English "Lady Midday", "Noonwraith" or "noon witch".
claims.statement_id: Poludnitsa adalah iblis siang hari dalam mitologi Slavia; dalam bahasa Inggris ia disebut "Lady Midday", "Noonwraith", atau "noon witch".
claims.quote: Poludnitsa is a noon demon in Slavic mythology. She can be referred to in English as "Lady Midday", "Noonwraith" or "noon witch".

claims.statement: She was usually pictured as a young woman in white roaming field bounds; she attacked people working at noon, causing heatstroke and neck pain, sometimes even madness.
claims.statement_id: Ia biasanya digambarkan sebagai perempuan muda berbaju putih yang berkeliaran di pematang ladang; ia menyerang orang yang bekerja pada tengah hari, menyebabkan sengatan panas dan sakit leher, kadang bahkan kegilaan.
claims.quote: She was usually pictured as a young woman dressed in white that roamed field bounds. She assailed folk working at noon, causing heatstrokes and aches in the neck; sometimes she even caused madness.

claims.statement: Poludnitsa appears in the middle of hot summer days as whirling dust clouds and carries a scythe, sickle or shears.
claims.statement_id: Poludnitsa muncul di tengah hari musim panas yang terik dalam bentuk pusaran debu dan membawa sabit, arit, atau gunting.
claims.quote: Poludnitsa, who makes herself evident in the middle of hot summer days, takes the form of whirling dust clouds and carries a scythe, sickle or shears

claims.statement: She stops people in the field to ask hard questions or talk; anyone who fails to answer or changes the subject is beheaded or struck with illness.
claims.statement_id: Ia menghentikan orang di ladang untuk mengajukan pertanyaan sulit atau mengajak bercakap; siapa yang gagal menjawab atau mengalihkan pembicaraan akan dipenggal atau dibuat sakit.
claims.quote: She will stop people in the field to ask them difficult questions or engage them in conversation. If anyone fails to answer a question or tries to change the subject, she will cut off their head or strike them with illness.

claims.statement: She may appear as an old hag, a beautiful woman or a 12-year-old girl, and served to scare children from valuable crops; she is seen only in the hottest part of the day and personifies sunstroke.
claims.statement_id: Ia bisa tampil sebagai nenek tua, perempuan cantik, atau gadis berusia 12 tahun, dan berguna untuk menakuti anak agar menjauhi tanaman berharga; ia hanya terlihat pada saat paling panas dan merupakan personifikasi sengatan matahari.
claims.quote: She may appear as an old hag, a beautiful woman, or a 12-year-old girl, and she was useful in scaring children away from valuable crops. She is only seen on the hottest part of the day and is a personification of a sun-stroke.

claims.statement: According to belief, Poludnitsa loves to dance; if she sees a girl resting in the field, she wakes her and urges her to dance.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan, Poludnitsa suka menari; bila melihat gadis berbaring beristirahat di ladang, ia membangunkannya dan membujuknya menari.
claims.quote: Poludnitsa, according to beliefs, loves to dance. If she sees a girl lying down to rest in the field, she will wake her up and begin to persuade her to dance.

claims.statement: Poludnitsa cannot be beaten at dancing, but if such a girl is found, the noon spirit gives her a rich dowry.
claims.statement_id: Poludnitsa tak terkalahkan dalam menari, tetapi bila ada gadis yang sanggup mengalahkannya, roh tengah hari itu memberinya mas kawin yang kaya.
claims.quote: Poludnitsa cannot be beaten in dancing; however, if such a girl is found, the noon spirit will present her with a rich dowry.

claims.statement: In some accounts she symbolizes the midday star and is thus the sister of Zarya-Zarenitsa.
claims.statement_id: Dalam beberapa kisah, ia melambangkan bintang tengah hari sehingga bersaudara dengan Zarya-Zarenitsa.
claims.quote: In some accounts, she symbolizes the midday star, thereby being the sister of Zarya-Zarenitsa

claims.statement: In Wendish mythology, Přezpołdnica (Lower Sorbian; Připołdnica in Upper Sorbian) is known as Mittagsfrau ("Lady Midday") among German speakers of Lusatia.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Wendia, Přezpołdnica (Sorbia Hilir; Připołdnica dalam Sorbia Hulu) dikenal sebagai Mittagsfrau ("Nyonya Tengah Hari") di kalangan penutur bahasa Jerman di Lusatia.
claims.quote: In Wendish mythology, Přezpołdnica (in Lower Sorbian, Připołdnica in Upper Sorbian) is known as Mittagsfrau ("Lady Midday") among German speakers of Eastern Germany's Lusatia

claims.statement: The figure's origin is linked to a personification of sunstroke, the special atmosphere of a hot noon and remnants of belief in ancient gods and demons.
claims.statement_id: Asal-usul sosok Poludnitsa (Полудница) dihubungkan dengan personifikasi sengatan matahari, suasana khas siang yang terik, dan sisa kepercayaan pada dewa dan iblis kuno.
claims.quote: Происхождение образа связывают с олицетворением солнечного удара, особой атмосферой жаркого полдня и остатками верований в древних божеств и демонов

claims.statement: According to some beliefs, the poludnitsa guards grain and vegetables from people and from the scorching sun.
claims.statement_id: Menurut sebagian kepercayaan, poludnitsa menjaga tanaman biji-bijian dan sayuran dari manusia dan dari terik matahari.
claims.quote: По некоторым представлениям, полудница охраняет злаки и овощи от людей и палящих лучей солнца

claims.statement: Against poludnitsy people crossed themselves, said a prayer, sprinkled holy water on her or simply ran away.
claims.statement_id: Untuk melawan poludnitsa, orang membuat tanda salib, berdoa, memercikkan air suci kepadanya, atau melarikan diri.
claims.quote: Против полудниц использовались такие общие меры, как перекреститься, прочитать молитву, окропить её святой водой или попросту убежать от неё.

claims.statement: The poludnitsa was thought most dangerous to pregnant women, new mothers and small children; she punished new mothers who broke seclusion, stole and swapped infants and attacked older children.
claims.statement_id: Poludnitsa dianggap paling berbahaya bagi perempuan hamil, ibu yang baru melahirkan, dan anak kecil; ia menghukum ibu nifas yang melanggar pengasingan, mencuri dan menukar bayi, serta menyerang anak yang lebih besar.
claims.quote: Считалось, что полудница — наиболее опасна для беременных, недавно родивших и маленьких детей, она наказывает нарушивших изоляцию рожениц, ворует и подменяет младенцев, нападает на детей постарше.

claims.statement: Among the East Slavs, only Russians in north-western Russia believed in the poludnitsa.
claims.statement_id: Di antara bangsa Slavia Timur, hanya orang Rusia di barat laut Rusia yang mempercayai poludnitsa.
claims.quote: Среди восточных славян в полудницу верили только русские на северо-западе России

claims.statement: After the rest hour between twelve and one has passed, the Mittagsfrau loses her power.
claims.statement_id: Setelah jam istirahat antara pukul dua belas dan satu berlalu, Mittagsfrau kehilangan kekuatannya.
claims.quote: Nach Ablauf der Ruhestunde zwischen zwölf und eins verliert die Mittagsfrau ihre Macht.

claims.statement: Those visited by the Mittagsfrau can only save themselves by telling her about farm work, especially flax processing, until one o'clock.
claims.statement_id: Orang yang didatangi Mittagsfrau hanya bisa selamat dengan bercerita kepadanya tentang pekerjaan petani, terutama mengolah rami, sampai pukul satu.
claims.quote: Die von der Mittagsfrau Heimgesuchten können sich nur retten, indem sie ihr bis ein Uhr von der bäuerlichen Arbeit, insbesondere von der Flachsverarbeitung, erzählen.

claims.statement: According to most beliefs, the poludnitsa is hostile and very dangerous to people.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kebanyakan kepercayaan, poludnitsa bermusuhan dan sangat berbahaya bagi manusia.
claims.quote: Согласно большинству представлений, полудница — враждебна и очень опасна для людей.

claims.statement: The Mittagsfrau shares traits with the vile; both like to steal children and replace them with changelings.
claims.statement_id: Mittagsfrau memiliki ciri yang sama dengan vila; keduanya suka mencuri anak dan menggantinya dengan anak tukaran.
claims.quote: Sie besitzt gemeinsame Merkmale mit den Vilen. Beide stehlen gerne Kinder und vertauschen sie durch Wechselbälge.

claims.statement: Figures close to the poludnitsa include the polevik, the udelnitsa, the rusalka and other field figures.
claims.statement_id: Tokoh yang dekat dengan poludnitsa antara lain polevik, udelnitsa, rusalka, dan tokoh ladang lainnya.
claims.quote: Полуднице близки полевик, удельница, русалка и другие полевые персонажи

claims.statement: The bannik is a bathhouse (banya) spirit of Slavic mythology, usually a small naked old man with a long beard, covered in birch leaves from used bath brooms.
claims.statement_id: Bannik adalah roh rumah mandi (banya) dalam mitologi Slavia, biasanya digambarkan sebagai lelaki tua kecil telanjang berjanggut panjang yang tubuhnya tertutup daun birch sisa sapu mandi.
claims.quote: is a bathhouse (banya) spirit in Slavic mythology. He is usually described as a small, naked old man with a long beard, his body covered in the birch leaves left over from well used bath brooms.

claims.statement: Many accounts say he is a shapeshifter who can appear as a local person, or even as a stone or coal in the bathhouse oven.
claims.statement_id: Banyak kisah menyebut ia pengubah wujud yang bisa tampil sebagai warga setempat, atau bahkan sebagai batu atau arang di tungku pemanas banya.
claims.quote: Many accounts also claim that he is a shapeshifter and can appear as a local person to someone who stumbles across him, or even as a stone or coal in the oven heating the bathhouse.

claims.statement: The third (or fourth) firing was reserved for the bannik, and as he liked to invite demons and forest spirits to bathe with him, no Christian images were allowed.
claims.statement_id: Pemanasan ketiga (atau keempat, tergantung tradisi) disediakan bagi bannik, dan karena ia suka mengundang setan dan roh hutan mandi bersamanya, gambar Kristen tidak boleh dipasang.
claims.quote: The third firing (or fourth, depending on tradition) was reserved for the bannik, and, given his inclination to invite demons and forest spirits to share his bath, no Christian images were allowed lest they offend the occupants.

claims.statement: If disturbed while washing, the bannik might pour boiling water on the intruder or even strangle him.
claims.statement_id: Bila diganggu penyusup saat mandi, bannik bisa menyiramnya dengan air mendidih atau bahkan mencekiknya.
claims.quote: If disturbed by an intruder while washing, the bannik might pour boiling water over him, or even strangle him.

claims.statement: Offerings of fir branches, water and soap were left, ending with a formal thank-you spoken aloud.
claims.statement_id: Sesaji berupa ranting cemara, air, dan sabun ditinggalkan, ditutup dengan ucapan terima kasih yang diucapkan keras.
claims.quote: offerings of fir branches, water and soap were left, capped by a formal thank you uttered aloud.

claims.statement: To appease the bannik when a banya was rebuilt, a black hen was suffocated, left unplucked and buried under the threshold.
claims.statement_id: Untuk menenangkan bannik, saat banya dibangun kembali, seekor ayam hitam dicekik, dibiarkan berbulu, dan dikubur di bawah ambang bangunan.
claims.quote: In order to appease the bannik, upon the rebuilding of a banya, a black hen would be suffocated, left unplucked and buried beneath the building's threshold.

claims.statement: Most births took place in the banya, and the bannik was believed not truly happy until a child was born in his domain.
claims.statement_id: Kebanyakan kelahiran terjadi di banya, dan bannik dipercaya belum benar-benar senang atau tenang sampai ada anak lahir di wilayahnya.
claims.quote: Despite this, most births occurred inside the banya and it was believed that the bannik was not truly happy or settled until a child was born within his domain.

claims.statement: The bannik could predict the future; one stood with bare back in the half-open bath door, and he stroked it gently if all boded well or struck with his claws if trouble lay ahead.
claims.statement_id: Bannik dapat meramalkan masa depan; orang bertanya dengan berdiri berpunggung terbuka di pintu banya yang setengah terbuka, lalu bannik membelai lembut bila pertanda baik atau mencakar bila ada kesulitan.
claims.quote: The bannik had the ability to predict the future. One consulted him by standing with one's back exposed in the half-open door of the bath. The bannik would gently stroke one's back if all boded well; but if trouble lay ahead, he would strike with his claws.

claims.statement: Bannik (Russian Банник) is a household spirit of Slavic mythology.
claims.statement_id: Bannik (bahasa Rusia Банник) adalah roh rumah dalam mitologi Slavia.
claims.quote: Bannik (russisch Банник) ist ein Hausgeist aus der slawischen Mythologie.

claims.statement: He is said to live behind or under the stove; he is usually invisible, sometimes a small dirty old man with long hair, a beard and big hands, and can turn into cats, dogs, hares and frogs.
claims.statement_id: Ia konon tinggal di belakang atau di bawah tungku; biasanya tak kasatmata, kadang berwujud lelaki tua kecil yang kotor berambut panjang, berjanggut, dan bertangan besar, serta bisa berubah menjadi kucing, anjing, kelinci, dan katak.
claims.quote: Er soll hinter oder unter dem Ofen leben. Normalerweise ist er unsichtbar und manchmal hat er die Form eines kleinen, schmutzigen alten Mannes mit langen Haaren und einem Bart und großen Händen. Es kann sich in Tiere wie Katzen, Hunde, Hasen und Frösche verwandeln.

claims.statement: Because the banya is a dark, potentially dangerous place, the bannik is seen as a mischievous, sometimes harmful being.
claims.statement_id: Karena banya tempat yang gelap dan berpotensi berbahaya, bannik dipandang sebagai makhluk usil yang kadang mencelakai.
claims.quote: Da die Banja ein dunkler, potenziell gefährlicher Ort ist, wird der Bannik als schelmisches, manchmal schädliches Wesen angesehen.

claims.statement: Mothers with newborns were closely guarded in the banya, as the bannik was believed to try to abduct unbaptized children.
claims.statement_id: Ibu dengan bayi yang baru lahir dijaga ketat di banya karena bannik dipercaya mencoba menculik anak yang belum dibaptis.
claims.quote: Mütter mit Neugeborenen wurden in der Banja streng bewacht, da man glaubte, der Bannik würde versuchen, noch nicht getaufte Kinder zu entführen.

claims.statement: In Slavic tradition, especially in Russia and Ukraine, the bannik was the spirit of the banya, the bathhouse.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi Slavia, terutama di Rusia (Russland) dan Ukraina (Ukraine), bannik adalah roh banya, rumah mandi uap.
claims.quote: In slawischen Überlieferungen, insbesondere in Russland und der Ukraine, war der Bannik der Geist der Banja, des Badehauses.

claims.statement: Gamayun is a prophetic bird in Russian folklore, a symbol of wisdom and knowledge living on an island in the mythical east, close to paradise.
claims.statement_id: Gamayun adalah burung bernubuat dalam cerita rakyat Rusia, lambang kebijaksanaan dan pengetahuan, yang tinggal di pulau di timur yang mitis, dekat surga.
claims.quote: is a prophetic bird in Russian folklore. It is a symbol of wisdom and knowledge and lives on an island in the mythical east, close to paradise.

claims.statement: Gamayun is usually depicted as a large black bird with a woman's head, spreading divine messages and prophecies through her songs.
claims.statement_id: Gamayun biasanya digambarkan sebagai burung hitam besar berkepala perempuan yang menyebarkan pesan ilahi dan ramalan melalui nyanyiannya.
claims.quote: The Gamayun is normally depicted as a large black bird with a woman's head. She is said to spread divine messages and prophecies, which she imparts through her songs

claims.statement: The name may be of Persian origin, as the Huma bird appears in Persian mythology.
claims.statement_id: Nama Gamayun mungkin berasal dari Persia, karena burung Huma muncul dalam mitologi Persia.
claims.quote: The name may have a Persian origin as the Huma bird appears in Persian mythology.

claims.statement: Medieval Russian literature distinguished Gamayun, a bird of paradise spending its whole life in the air, from other mythical birds such as the Alkonost (which calms sea storms) and the Sirin (a female-faced bird that enchants people with its voice).
claims.statement_id: Kesusastraan Rusia abad pertengahan membedakan Gamayun, burung surga yang seumur hidup berada di udara, dari burung mitos lain seperti Alkonost (penenang badai laut) dan Sirin (burung berwajah perempuan yang memikat orang dengan suaranya).
claims.quote: Medieval Russian literature distinguished the Gamayun, a bird of paradise that spends its entire life in the air, from other mythological birds ... the Alkonost (a bird that calms sea storms), and the Sirin (a bird with a female face that is capable of enchanting people with its voice).

claims.statement: In books of the 17th–19th centuries, Gamayun is described as legless and wingless, ever-flying with the help of a tail, its fall foreshadowing the death of statesmen.
claims.statement_id: Dalam buku-buku abad ke-17 sampai ke-19, Gamayun digambarkan sebagai burung tanpa kaki dan tanpa sayap yang terus terbang dengan bantuan ekor, dan jatuhnya menandakan kematian negarawan.
claims.quote: In books dating to the 17th–19th centuries, the Gamayun is described as a legless and wingless bird, ever-flying with the help of a tail, foreshadowing the death of statesmen by her fall.

claims.statement: During the Silver Age of Russian poetry it often appeared as the source of tragic prophecies, as in Alexander Blok's "Gamayun, the Prophetic Bird".
claims.statement_id: Pada Zaman Perak puisi Rusia, Gamayun sering tampil sebagai sumber nubuat tragis, misalnya dalam sajak Alexander Blok "Gamayun, the Prophetic Bird".
claims.quote: During the Silver Age of Russian Poetry, it often appeared as the source of tragic prophecies, such as in Alexander Blok's Gamayun, the Prophetic Bird.

claims.statement: The Gamayun is depicted on the coat of arms of Smolensk.
claims.statement_id: Gamayun digambarkan pada lambang kota Smolensk.
claims.quote: The Gamayun is depicted on the coat of arms of Smolensk.

claims.statement: Gamajun (Russian: Гамаюн) is a prophetic bird from Slavic mythology.
claims.statement_id: Gamajun (bahasa Rusia: Гамаюн) adalah burung bernubuat dari mitologi Slavia.
claims.quote: Gamajun (russisch Гамаюн) ist ein prophetischer Vogel aus der slawischen Mythologie.

claims.statement: When it flies, a deadly storm from the east is unleashed; everyone fears its presence because its visions foretell only catastrophe without comfort or hope.
claims.statement_id: Ketika ia terbang, badai mematikan dari timur terpicu; kehadirannya ditakuti semua orang karena penglihatannya hanya meramalkan malapetaka tanpa penghiburan dan harapan.
claims.quote: Wenn er fliegt, wird ein tödlicher Sturm aus dem Osten ausgelöst. Die Anwesenheit des Gamajun wird von allen gefürchtet, da seine Visionen nur Katastrophen ohne Trost und Hoffnung vorhersagen.

claims.statement: Gamayun's popularity in Russian culture rose in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, when Wiktor Wasnezow painted "Gamajun, the Prophetic Bird".
claims.statement_id: Popularitas Gamayun dalam budaya Rusia meningkat pada akhir abad ke-19 dan awal abad ke-20, ketika Wiktor Wasnezow melukis "Gamajun, der prophetische Vogel".
claims.quote: Die Beliebtheit des Gamajun stieg in der russischen Kultur Ende des 19. und Anfang des 20. Jahrhunderts an, als Wiktor Wasnezow das Gemälde „Gamajun, der prophetische Vogel“ malte.

claims.statement: Despite a widespread misconception, there is no evidence of the gamayun bird in traditional Russian folklore.
claims.statement_id: Meskipun ada anggapan keliru yang tersebar luas, tidak ada data tentang keberadaan burung gamayun dalam folklor tradisional Rusia.
claims.quote: Несмотря на распространённое заблуждение, сведений о существовании птицы гамаюн в русском традиционном фольклоре нет

claims.statement: The origins of the image go back to the mythical humay bird of Iranian folklore.
claims.statement_id: Asal-usul citra Gamayun ditelusuri ke burung mitos humay dari folklor Iran.
claims.quote: Истоки образа восходят к мифической птице хумай из иранского фольклора

claims.statement: The visual image of the gamayun changed over time: first it acquired wings and legs, and later a female face.
claims.statement_id: Wujud visual burung gamayun berubah seiring waktu: mula-mula ia mendapat sayap dan kaki, kemudian wajah perempuan.
claims.quote: Визуальный образ птицы гамаюн претерпел изменение с течением времени: сначала у неё появились крылья и ноги ... а затем и женское лицо

claims.statement: In the 17th–18th centuries this bird was depicted on decorative applied art, cannons and banners.
claims.statement_id: Pada abad ke-17 dan ke-18 burung ini digambarkan pada karya seni dekoratif terapan, meriam, dan panji.
claims.quote: В XVII—XVIII веках эта птица изображалась на произведениях декоративно-прикладного искусства, пушках и знамёнах.

claims.statement: In Romanian mythology, strigoi are troubled spirits said to have risen from the grave, credited with turning into a beast, becoming invisible and gaining vitality from their victims' blood.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Romania, strigoi adalah arwah gelisah yang dikatakan bangkit dari kubur; mereka dianggap mampu berubah menjadi binatang, menjadi tak kasatmata, dan memperoleh daya hidup dari darah korbannya.
claims.quote: Strigoi in Romanian mythology are troubled spirits that are said to have risen from the grave. They are attributed with the abilities to transform into a beast, become invisible, and to gain vitality from the blood of their victims.

claims.statement: Bram Stoker's Dracula may be a modern interpretation of the strigoi through their historic links with vampirism.
claims.statement_id: Dracula karya Bram Stoker mungkin merupakan tafsiran modern atas strigoi melalui kaitan historis mereka dengan vampirisme.
claims.quote: Bram Stoker's Dracula may be a modern interpretation of the Strigoi through their historic links with vampirism.

claims.statement: Strigoi is a Romanian word from a root related to the Latin strix or striga, with the augmentative suffix -oi (feminine -oaică).
claims.statement_id: Strigoi adalah kata Romania dari akar yang berkaitan dengan istilah Latin strix atau striga, ditambah akhiran pembesar -oi (bentuk perempuan -oaică).
claims.quote: Strigòi is a Romanian word that originated from a root related to the Latin terms strix or striga with the addition of the augmentative suffix -oi (feminine -oaică).

claims.statement: It is related to the Romanian verb a striga, meaning "to scream".
claims.statement_id: Kata ini berkaitan dengan kata kerja Romania a striga, yang berarti "menjerit".
claims.quote: It is related to the Romanian verb a striga, which means "to scream".

claims.statement: One of the earliest mentions of a historical strigoi is the story of Jure Grando Alilović (1579–1656) from Istria.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu penyebutan paling awal tentang strigoi historis adalah kisah Jure Grando Alilović (1579–1656) dari wilayah Istria.
claims.quote: One of the earliest mentions of a historical strigoi is the story of Jure Grando Alilović (1579–1656) from the region of Istria.

claims.statement: Dimitrie Cantemir mentions striga in Descriptio Moldaviae (1714–1716), thinking them mostly Moldavian and Transylvanian beliefs, but associating them with witches or warlocks rather than blood-drinking undead.
claims.statement_id: Dimitrie Cantemir menyebut striga dalam Descriptio Moldaviae (1714–1716), menganggapnya terutama kepercayaan Moldavia dan Transilvania, tetapi mengaitkannya dengan penyihir, bukan vampir mayat hidup peminum darah.
claims.quote: Striga are mentioned by the Moldavian statesman and soldier Dimitrie Cantemir in his work Descriptio Moldaviae (1714–1716). He thought that the striga were mostly Moldavian and Transylvanian beliefs. However, he associated them with witches or warlocks rather than blood-drinking undead vampires.

claims.statement: Strigoi take milk from cows, the manna of the wheat and people's strength, stop the rains, bring hail and bring death among people and cattle.
claims.statement_id: Strigoi mengambil susu sapi, sari gandum, dan kekuatan orang, menahan hujan, mendatangkan hujan es, serta membawa kematian bagi manusia dan ternak.
claims.quote: The strigoi take the milk from the cows, take the manna of the wheat, the strength of the people, stop the rains, bring hail and bring death among men and cattle.

claims.statement: Strigoi viu is a living strigoi or sorcerer.
claims.statement_id: Strigoi viu adalah strigoi hidup atau tukang sihir.
claims.quote: Strigoi viu: a living strigoi or sorcerer.

claims.statement: Strigoi mort is a dead strigoi, the most dangerous, emerging from the grave to torment its family until its relatives die.
claims.statement_id: Strigoi mort adalah strigoi mati, yang paling berbahaya; mereka keluar dari kubur untuk menyiksa keluarganya sampai kerabatnya meninggal.
claims.quote: Strigoi mort: a dead strigoi, the most dangerous. They emerge from their graves in order to torment their families until their relatives die.

claims.statement: To kill one, the grave of the suspected strigoi is found, priests read the order, and an oak, yew or branch is struck into the heart or it is pierced with a nail or knife so it stays bound to the coffin.
claims.statement_id: Untuk membunuhnya, kubur orang yang diduga strigoi dicari, imam membacakan tata doa, lalu kayu ek, yew, atau dahan ditancapkan ke jantungnya, atau ditusuk paku atau pisau agar ia tetap terikat pada peti mati.
claims.quote: To kill them, the grave of the supposed strigoi is searched and the order is read to him by the priests and an oak, yew or branch is struck in his heart, it is pierced with a nail or a knife, to remain bound of the coffin

claims.statement: In Romanian mythology, strigoi are the evil souls of the dead, believed to leave the grave at night and turn into an animal or ghostly apparition to harm the living.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Romania, strigoi adalah jiwa jahat orang mati yang dipercaya keluar dari kubur pada malam hari dan berubah menjadi binatang atau sosok seperti hantu untuk mencelakai orang hidup.
claims.quote: Strigoii sunt, în mitologia românească, sufletele rele ale morților, despre care se crede că ar ieși noaptea din mormânt și s-ar transforma într-un animal sau într-o apariție fantomatică, pentru a pricinui relele celor vii.

claims.statement: There are living and dead strigoi; at the new moon they leave their graves or their bodies to dance or make mischief, and their night is Saint Andrew's Night (30 November).
claims.statement_id: Ada strigoi hidup dan strigoi mati; saat bulan baru mereka keluar dari kubur atau meninggalkan tubuhnya untuk menari atau berbuat jahat, dan malam mereka adalah malam Santo Andreas (30 November).
claims.quote: Exista strigoi vii și strigoi morți. Când este lună nouă, strigoii ies din morminte sau își părăsesc trupul și încep să danseze sau să facă tot felul de răutăți. Noaptea lor este aceea de Sfântul Andrei (30 noiembrie).

claims.statement: A strigoi is said to be bald on the crown of the head, not to eat garlic or onions, and to avoid incense.
claims.statement_id: Konon strigoi botak di ubun-ubun, tidak memakan bawang putih dan bawang merah, serta menghindari dupa.
claims.quote: Se zice că strigoiul este chel în creștetul capului. El nu mănâncă usturoi și ceapă, se ferește de tămâie

claims.statement: If a village suffers drought, it means a strigoaică (female strigoi) is there, preventing the rains.
claims.statement_id: Jika sebuah desa dilanda kekeringan, artinya di sana ada strigoaică (strigoi perempuan) yang menghalangi hujan.
claims.quote: Dacă într-un sat este secetă, înseamnă că acolo este o strigoaică (împiedică ploile)

claims.statement: In February 2004, a woman from Marotinu de Sus in Dolj County claimed she had been visited by her late uncle.
claims.statement_id: Pada Februari 2004, seorang perempuan dari desa Marotinu de Sus di Distrik Dolj mengaku didatangi mendiang pamannya.
claims.quote: In February 2004, a woman from the village of Marotinu de Sus in Dolj County claimed that she had been visited by her late uncle

claims.statement: Dolj County police later arrested six family members who took part in the ritual, charging them with "disturbing the peace of the dead".
claims.statement_id: Polisi Distrik Dolj kemudian menangkap enam anggota keluarga yang ikut dalam ritual itu dengan dakwaan "mengganggu ketenangan orang mati".
claims.quote: Dolj County police later arrested six of the family members who participated in the ritual, charging them with "disturbing the peace of the dead".

claims.statement: A revolutionary activist carpeted his apartment with braids of garlic, allegedly as a traditional remedy against strigoi.
claims.statement_id: Seorang aktivis revolusi melapisi apartemennya dengan jalinan bawang putih, konon sebagai penangkal tradisional terhadap strigoi.
claims.quote: carpeted his own apartment with braids of garlic, allegedly as a traditional remedy against the strigoi.

claims.statement: Otila Hedeşan notes the same augmentative suffix in the related terms moroi and bosorcoi, seen as part of the same "mythological micro-system".
claims.statement_id: Otila Hedeşan mencatat bahwa akhiran pembesar yang sama muncul pada istilah terkait moroi dan bosorcoi, yang dianggap bagian dari "sistem mikro mitologis" yang sama.
claims.quote: Otila Hedeşan notes that the same augmentative suffix appears in the related terms moroi and bosorcoi (borrowed from Hungarian boszorka) and considers this parallel derivation to indicate membership in the same "mythological micro-system."

claims.statement: Astghik is a prominent goddess of ancient Armenian mythology, revered as the embodiment of beauty, love, fertility and water.
claims.statement_id: Astghik adalah dewi penting dalam mitologi Armenia kuno yang dihormati sebagai perwujudan kecantikan, cinta, kesuburan, dan air.
claims.quote: a prominent goddess in ancient Armenian mythology, is revered as the embodiment of beauty, love, fertility, and water.

claims.statement: Astghik is also known as the bride of the warrior god Vahagn, who represents fire and thunder.
claims.statement_id: Astghik juga dikenal sebagai pengantin dewa perang Vahagn, yang melambangkan api dan guntur.
claims.quote: Astghik is also known as the bride of the warrior god Vahagn, who represents fire and thunder.

claims.statement: She was often identified with Aphrodite and the planet Venus.
claims.statement_id: Ia sering disamakan dengan Aphrodite dan planet Venus.
claims.quote: She was often identified with Aphrodite and the planet Venus

claims.statement: The celebration honouring Astghik is called Vardavar, when people drench each other with water as a purification ritual.
claims.statement_id: Perayaan untuk menghormati Astghik disebut Vardavar, ketika orang saling menyiram air sebagai ritual penyucian.
claims.quote: The celebration honoring Astghik is called Vardavar, during which people drench each other with water as a ritual of 'purification.'

claims.statement: One tradition says she was Noah's daughter, born after his flood.
claims.statement_id: Satu tradisi menyebutnya putri Nuh, yang lahir setelah air bah.
claims.quote: One tradition says she was Noah's daughter, born after his flood.

claims.statement: The name Astghik (Աստղիկ) derives from Old Armenian astgh (Աստղ), "star", and can be read as "little star".
claims.statement_id: Nama Astghik (Աստղիկ) berasal dari kata Armenia Kuno astgh (Աստղ), "bintang", sehingga dapat dimaknai "bintang kecil".
claims.quote: The name "Astghik" (Աստղիկ) is derived from the Old Armenian word "astgh" (Աստղ), meaning "star." ... Thus, "Astghik" can be interpreted as "little star,"

claims.statement: Originally Astghik was the goddess of the creation of heaven and earth, but she later became a deity of love, beauty and fertility.
claims.statement_id: Pada mulanya Astghik adalah dewi penciptaan langit dan bumi, tetapi kemudian berubah menjadi dewi cinta, kecantikan, dan kesuburan.
claims.quote: Originally, Astghik was the goddess of creation of heaven and earth, however, later she was transformed into a deity of love, beauty, and fertility.

claims.statement: With the rise of Aramazd as chief creator god and Anahit as moon goddess, Astghik's position diminished.
claims.statement_id: Dengan bangkitnya Aramazd sebagai dewa pencipta utama dan Anahit sebagai dewi bulan, kedudukan Astghik menurun.
claims.quote: With the rise of Aramazd as the chief creator god and Anahit as the moon goddess, Astghik's position diminished.

claims.statement: Astghik used to bathe in a stream, often nude, and her beauty was so captivating that young men from nearby villages gathered to watch her.
claims.statement_id: Astghik biasa mandi di sungai kecil, sering tanpa busana, dan kecantikannya begitu memikat sehingga para pemuda dari desa sekitar berkumpul untuk melihatnya.
claims.quote: Astghik had a habit of bathing in a stream, often in the nude. Her beauty was so captivating that young men from nearby villages would gather to watch her.

claims.statement: To stop the young men getting a better view, she created a thick fog over the area; it became permanent, and the place came to be known as Msho Dasht.
claims.statement_id: Untuk menghalangi pandangan para pemuda, ia menciptakan kabut tebal yang menutupi daerah itu; kabut itu menetap, dan tempat itu dikenal sebagai Msho Dasht.
claims.quote: To prevent the young men from getting a better view, she created a thick fog that covered the area. This fog became a permanent feature of the place, and the location came to be known as "Msho Dasht".

claims.statement: Astghik's main temple was at Ashtishat, north of Muş in Turkey; it was also dedicated to Vahagn, her lover or husband.
claims.statement_id: Kuil utama Astghik berada di Ashtishat (阿什季沙特), di utara kota Muş di Turki; kuil itu juga diperuntukkan bagi Vahagn, kekasih atau suaminya.
claims.quote: 她的主要神庙在阿什季沙特，位于土耳其穆什城以北，这座寺庙是瓦哈格恩，太阳神、她的情人或丈夫专用的

claims.statement: Within the Armenian pantheon, Astghik is the only goddess whose name has a clear Armenian linguistic origin.
claims.statement_id: Di antara dewa-dewi Armenia, Astghik adalah satu-satunya dewi yang namanya jelas berasal dari bahasa Armenia.
claims.quote: Dentro del panteón armenio, Astghik es la única diosa cuyo nombre tiene un claro origen lingüístico armenio.

claims.statement: She is considered the personification of the planet Venus, and sources identify her as goddess of love and motherhood.
claims.statement_id: Ia dianggap personifikasi planet Venus, dan sumber-sumber menyebutnya dewi cinta dan keibuan.
claims.quote: Se la considera la personificación del planeta Venus, y las fuentes la identifican como la diosa del amor y la maternidad.

claims.statement: Her husband was Vahagn, and the two shared a temple complex in Taron.
claims.statement_id: Suaminya adalah Vahagn, dan keduanya berbagi kompleks kuil di Taron.
claims.quote: Su esposo era Vahagn, y ambos compartían un complejo de templos en Taron

claims.statement: In the late pre-Christian period she became the goddess of love, virginal beauty, and springs and sources of water.
claims.statement_id: Pada akhir masa pra-Kristen, ia menjadi dewi cinta, kecantikan perawan, serta mata air dan sumber air.
claims.quote: En el período precristiano tardío, se convirtió en la diosa del amor, la belleza virginal y los manantiales y fuentes de agua.

claims.statement: Astghik was the Armenian goddess of fertility and love, and consort of Vahagn.
claims.statement_id: Astghik adalah dewi kesuburan dan cinta Armenia, dan pasangan Vahagn.
claims.quote: era la diosa armenia de la fertilidad y el amor, y consorte de Vahagn.

claims.statement: Her name is written Astłik or Astghik.
claims.statement_id: Namanya ditulis Astłik atau Astghik.
claims.quote: Astłik or Astghik (Armenian: Աստղիկ ) a prominent goddess

claims.statement: Hiisi is a term in Finnic mythologies, originally denoting sacred places and later various mythological beings.
claims.statement_id: Hiisi adalah istilah dalam mitologi Finnik yang semula menunjuk tempat-tempat keramat dan kemudian berbagai jenis makhluk mitos.
claims.quote: is a term in Finnic mythologies, originally denoting sacred localities and later on various types of mythological entities.

claims.statement: In later, Christian-influenced folklore they are depicted as demonic or trickster-like beings, often the original pagan inhabitants of the land, similar to mythological giants.
claims.statement_id: Dalam folklor kemudian yang dipengaruhi Kristen, mereka digambarkan sebagai makhluk bersifat iblis atau penipu, sering penghuni asli tanah itu yang masih kafir, mirip raksasa mitologis.
claims.quote: In later, Christian-influenced folklore, they are depicted as demonic or trickster-like entities, often the autochthonous, pagan inhabitants of the land, similar in this respect to mythological giants.

claims.statement: They are found near jutting promontories, ominous crevasses, large boulders, potholes, woods, hills and other striking features or rough terrain.
claims.statement_id: Mereka berada di dekat tanjung yang menonjol, celah yang menyeramkan, batu besar, lubang batu, hutan, bukit, dan bentuk alam mencolok atau medan kasar lainnya.
claims.quote: They are found near salient promontories, ominous crevasses, large boulders, potholes, woods, hills, and other outstanding geographical features or rough terrain.

claims.statement: Hiisi was originally a spirit of hill forests; in Estonian hiis means a sacred grove, usually on high ground.
claims.statement_id: Hiisi semula roh hutan perbukitan; dalam bahasa Estonia hiis berarti hutan kecil keramat, biasanya di tanah tinggi.
claims.quote: Hiisi was originally a spirit of hill forests (Abercromby 1898). In Estonian hiis (or his) means a sacred grove of trees, usually on elevated ground.

claims.statement: More recent speculation by Mauno Koski and others links Finnish Hiisi and Estonian Hiis mainly with burial sites or sacred areas tied to them.
claims.statement_id: Dugaan yang lebih baru oleh Mauno Koski dan lainnya mengaitkan Hiisi (Finlandia) dan Hiis (Estonia) terutama dengan tempat pemakaman atau kawasan keramat yang terkait dengannya.
claims.quote: More recent speculation, by Mauno Koski and others, associates the Finnish "Hiisi" and the Estonian "Hiis" primarily with burial sites, or sacred areas associated with burial sites

claims.statement: Hiisi's evil nature is supposed to have been magnified over time from the Christianization of Finland in the 12th and 13th centuries; more recently it has been nearly identical to a Christian devil, or the Devil.
claims.statement_id: Sifat jahat Hiisi diduga makin diperbesar seiring waktu, sejak Kristenisasi Finlandia pada abad ke-12 dan ke-13; belakangan sifatnya hampir sama dengan iblis Kristen, bahkan Iblis sendiri.
claims.quote: It has been supposed that Hiisi's evil nature has been magnified over time, starting with the Christianization of Finland in the 12th and 13th centuries. In more recent times his nature has been nearly identical with that of a Christian devil, or even the Devil.

claims.statement: In Bishop Mikael Agricola's list of Finnish pagan gods, Hiisi is said to be a god of forest game or fur, an attribute shared with a similar god, Tapio.
claims.statement_id: Dalam daftar dewa pagan Finlandia susunan Uskup Mikael Agricola, Hiisi disebut dewa hewan buruan hutan atau bulu, sifat yang juga dimiliki dewa serupa, Tapio.
claims.quote: In Bishop Mikael Agricola's list of Finnish pagan gods Hiisi is said to have been a god of forest game or fur, sharing this attribute with a similar god, Tapio.

claims.statement: Oral folklore about hiisi mostly describes beings dwelling at hiisi sites, typically trolls or giants, and many stories tell how odd rock formations and landscape features were made by them.
claims.statement_id: Folklor lisan tentang hiisi kebanyakan menggambarkan makhluk penghuni situs hiisi, biasanya troll atau raksasa, dan banyak cerita mengisahkan bagaimana formasi batu aneh dan bentang alam tercipta oleh ulah mereka.
claims.quote: Oral folklore concerning hiisi mostly describes creatures that dwelt in hiisi sites, typically trolls or giants. Many of the stories describe how odd rock formations or other features of the landscape were created by the actions of these creatures.

claims.statement: There are tales of the cape of Hiidennokka being made by giants throwing rocks; one takes a Christian turn, the giants throwing rocks into the sea to stop people going to church by boat.
claims.statement_id: Ada kisah tentang tanjung Hiidennokka yang terbentuk karena raksasa melempar batu; satu kisah bernuansa Kristen, ketika raksasa melempar batu ke laut agar orang tidak dapat ke gereja dengan perahu.
claims.quote: as well as tales of how the cape of Hiidennokka was created by giants throwing rocks. One of these tales takes on a Christian element, as the giants throw rocks into the sea to prevent people going to church by boat.
