claims.statement: Hiidet could travel in a noisy procession and attack people who did not give way; a hiisi could come in and steal if a door was left open; anyone chased by a hiisi should seek safety on cultivated land.
claims.statement_id: Hiidet dapat bepergian dalam arak-arakan riuh dan menyerang orang yang tidak memberi jalan; jika pintu dibiarkan terbuka, hiisi bisa masuk dan mencuri; orang yang dikejar hiisi sebaiknya berlindung di lahan garapan.
claims.quote: Hiidet could travel in a noisy procession and attack people who did not give way to them. If somebody left their door open, a hiisi could come inside and steal something. If you were chased by a hiisi, you should seek safety in a cultivated area.

claims.statement: Anyone chased by a hiisi can find refuge in a cultivated area; in Finnish folklore it is the cultivated areas that are blessed.
claims.statement_id: Siapa pun yang dikejar hiisi dapat berlindung di lahan garapan; dalam folklor Finlandia, lahan garapanlah yang dianggap diberkati.
claims.quote: Toute personne poursuivie par un hiisi peut trouver refuge dans une zone cultivée. Ainsi dans le folklore finnois, ce sont les zones cultivées qui sont bénites

claims.statement: They passed into folklore as purely evil spirits vaguely like trolls; in this later view hiidet were often small, though others were gigantic.
claims.statement_id: Mereka masuk ke folklor sebagai roh yang sepenuhnya jahat, agak mirip troll; menurut pandangan kemudian ini, hiidet sering berukuran kecil, tetapi ada yang raksasa.
claims.quote: they passed into folklore as purely evil spirits vaguely analogous to trolls. According to this later view, hiidet were often small in size, but others were gigantic.

claims.statement: Hiisi, son of the giant Kaleva, lives in the forest at hidden places of worship and is tamer and conqueror of wild beasts; he is a form of Lempo, god of malice.
claims.statement_id: Hiisi, putra raksasa Kaleva, tinggal di hutan di tempat-tempat pemujaan tersembunyi dan menjadi penjinak serta penakluk binatang liar; ia perwujudan Lempo, dewa kejahatan.
claims.quote: Hiisi, Sohn des Riesen Kaleva, wohnt im Wald an versteckten Anbetungsstätten und ist Zähmer und Bezwinger der wilden Tiere. Er ist eine Erscheinungsform von Lempo, dem Gott der Bosheit.

claims.statement: In the 13th and 14th cantos of the Kalevala, Lemminkäinen hunts Hiisi's elk (or deer).
claims.statement_id: Dalam nyanyian ke-13 dan ke-14 Kalevala, Lemminkäinen memburu rusa elk (atau rusa) milik Hiisi.
claims.quote: Im 13. und 14. Gesang des Kalevala verfolgt Lemminkäinen Hiisis Elch (oder Hirsch).

claims.statement: Finnish folk mythology distinguished forest, water and mountain hiisis.
claims.statement_id: Mitologi rakyat Finlandia membedakan hiisi hutan, hiisi air, dan hiisi gunung.
claims.quote: Die finnische Volksmythologie unterschied Wald-, Wasser- und Berghiisis.

claims.statement: The term hiidenkirnu ("Hiisi's butter churn") denotes a narrow, deep cleft in rock.
claims.statement_id: Istilah hiidenkirnu ("tong mentega Hiisi") menunjuk celah sempit dan dalam di batu.
claims.quote: Der Ausdruck hiidenkirnu (Gletschertopf, „Butterfass des Hiisi“) bezeichnet eine schmale und tiefe Kluft in einem Felsen.

claims.statement: In Finnish spells ("magic songs") Hiisi is often linked with a hill or mountain, and as a personage with hills and mountains as their owner or ruler.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mantra (lagu sihir) orang Finlandia, Hiisi sering dikaitkan dengan bukit atau gunung, dan sebagai tokoh ia juga dihubungkan dengan bukit dan gunung sebagai pemilik atau penguasanya.
claims.quote: In the spells ("magic songs") of the Finns the term Hiisi is often used in association with a hill or mountain, as a personage he also associated with the hills and mountains, such as the owner or ruler of the same.

claims.statement: Hiisi, plural hiidet, is a term of Balto-Finnic folklore.
claims.statement_id: Hiisi, jamaknya hiidet, adalah istilah folklor Balto-Finnik.
claims.quote: Hiisi, au pluriel hiidet, est un terme du folklore balto-finnois

claims.statement: Toell the Great is a mythological giant hero who lived on the Estonian island of Saaremaa.
claims.statement_id: Tõll yang Agung adalah pahlawan raksasa mitologis yang tinggal di Pulau Saaremaa, Estonia.
claims.quote: is a mythological giant hero who lived on the Estonian island of Saaremaa.

claims.statement: Suur Tõll lived with his wife Piret in the coastal village of Tõlluste by the Baltic Sea and tossed huge rocks everywhere, mostly at his archenemy Vanatühi (the Devil) or other enemies of the Saaremaa islanders.
claims.statement_id: Suur Tõll tinggal bersama istrinya, Piret, di desa pesisir Tõlluste di tepi Laut Baltik, dan melemparkan batu besar ke mana-mana, terutama ke arah musuh bebuyutannya Vanatühi (Iblis) atau musuh lain penduduk Saaremaa.
claims.quote: Suur Tõll lived with his wife Piret in the coastal village of Tõlluste (Tölluste) by the Baltic Sea. He tossed huge rocks everywhere, mostly aiming for his archenemy Vanatühi (The Devil) or other enemies of the local Saaremaa islanders.

claims.statement: Though king of Saaremaa, Tõll lived as a common farmer; he often visited his brother Leiger on neighbouring Hiiumaa (Dagö).
claims.statement_id: Walaupun raja Saaremaa, Tõll hidup sebagai petani biasa; ia sering mengunjungi saudaranya Leiger di pulau tetangga Hiiumaa (Dagö).
claims.quote: Although Tõll was the king of Saaremaa, he lived as a common farmer. He often visited his brother Leiger on the neighboring Hiiumaa (Dagö) island.

claims.statement: He was so tall he could almost walk there (the Soela Strait has passages only 2–3 m deep and is about 6 km across); his walking stick was a 5-fathom spruce trunk.
claims.statement_id: Ia begitu tinggi sehingga hampir bisa berjalan ke sana (Selat Soela hanya sedalam 2–3 m di beberapa jalur dan lebarnya sekitar 6 km); tongkatnya batang cemara sepanjang 5 depa.
claims.quote: He was so tall that he could almost walk there (the Soela Strait has passageways only 2-3m deep, and is about 6km across). His walking stick was a 5 fathom spruce tree trunk.

claims.statement: Tõll was always kind and ready to help but very hot-tempered; he loved cabbage, beer and the sauna.
claims.statement_id: Tõll selalu baik hati dan siap menolong, tetapi sangat mudah marah; ia gemar makan kubis, minum bir, dan mandi sauna.
claims.quote: Tõll was always kind and ready to help, but very hot-tempered. He loved to eat cabbage, drink beer, and go to the sauna

claims.statement: When an enemy beheaded him, Suur Tõll put his head on his sword and walked to his grave, said to be somewhere in Tõlluste.
claims.statement_id: Ketika musuh memenggal kepalanya, Suur Tõll meletakkan kepalanya di atas pedang dan berjalan ke kuburnya, yang konon berada di Tõlluste.
claims.quote: When an enemy decapitated him, Suur Tõll put his head on his sword and walked to his grave, which is supposed to be somewhere in Tõlluste.

claims.statement: On dying, Tõll promised to rise from the grave to help people in war; naughty children mocked him by shouting that there was a war in the yard, so he rose, grew angry, returned to his grave and swore never to come back.
claims.statement_id: Saat meninggal, Tõll berjanji bangkit dari kubur untuk menolong rakyat bila perang; anak-anak nakal mengolok-oloknya dengan berteriak bahwa ada perang di halaman, sehingga ia bangkit, marah, kembali ke kubur, dan bersumpah tak akan kembali.
claims.quote: When Suur Tõll died, he promised to rise from the grave and help people in case of war. However, naughty children made fun of him by yelling "Tõll, Tõll, wake up, there is a war in the yard". Suur Tõll rose, grew angry and went back to his grave, swearing never to come back.

claims.statement: It is supposed that the Suur Tõll stories are based on a historical person, possibly an ancient, very tall ruler of Saaremaa.
claims.statement_id: Diduga kisah-kisah Suur Tõll berdasar pada tokoh sejarah, mungkin penguasa kuno Saaremaa yang juga sangat tinggi.
claims.quote: It is supposed that stories about Suur Tõll are based on a historical person, possibly an ancient ruler of Saaremaa, who was also very tall.

claims.statement: In Ninase village two old windmills have been reshaped into Tõll and Piret, and Saaremaa newlyweds go there to honour their island's mythical heroes.
claims.statement_id: Di desa Ninase ada dua kincir angin tua yang dibentuk menjadi sosok Tõll dan Piret, dan pengantin baru Saaremaa datang ke sana untuk menghormati pahlawan mitos pulau mereka.
claims.quote: In the village of Ninase, there are two old windmills reshaped into the figures of Tõll and Piret. Newlyweds of Saaremaa go there to pay tribute to the mythical heroes of their island.

claims.statement: Toell the Great inspired the cartoon film Suur Tõll (Tallinnfilm, 1980).
claims.statement_id: Tõll yang Agung mengilhami film kartun Suur Tõll (Tallinnfilm, 1980).
claims.quote: Toell the Great has inspired the cartoon movie Suur Tõll (Tallinnfilm 1980).

claims.statement: Suur Tõll ("the great Tõll") is a giant of Estonian mythology from the Estonian island of Saaremaa.
claims.statement_id: Suur Tõll ("Tõll yang Agung") adalah raksasa dalam mitologi Estonia dari Pulau Saaremaa.
claims.quote: Der Suur Tõll („Der große Tõll“) ist in der estnischen Mythologie ein Riese von der estnischen Insel Saaremaa.

claims.statement: Because reliable evidence on Estonian mythology is lacking, the story of the giant Suur Tõll rests on folk tradition.
claims.statement_id: Karena kesaksian andal tentang mitologi Estonia kurang, kisah raksasa Suur Tõll bersandar pada tradisi rakyat.
claims.quote: Da verlässliche Zeugnisse über die estnische Mythologie fehlen, beruht die Geschichte vom Riesen Suur Tõll auf der Volksüberlieferung.

claims.statement: He threw great stones at his opponent, Vanatühi or Vanapagan, who represented the diabolical.
claims.statement_id: Ia melempar batu besar ke arah lawannya, Vanatühi atau Vanapagan, yang mewakili kejahatan iblis.
claims.quote: Mit großen Steinen warf er nach seinem Gegner, dem Vanatühi oder Vanapagan, der das Diabolische repräsentierte.

claims.statement: The origin of the name Tõll is unclear; some evidence points to an Estonian corruption of the name of the old Baltic German noble family von Toll.
claims.statement_id: Asal nama Tõll tidak jelas; sebagian petunjuk mengarah pada pelesetan Estonia dari nama keluarga bangsawan Jerman-Baltik lama, von Toll.
claims.quote: Die Herkunft des Namens Tõll ist ungeklärt. Manches deutet auf eine estnische Verballhornung des Namens der alteingesessenen adligen deutschbaltischen Familie von Toll hin.

claims.statement: In 2002 Estonian sculptor Tauno Kangro made a larger-than-life, playful monument to the giant and his wife on the waterfront of Kuressaare, the island capital.
claims.statement_id: Pada 2002 pematung Estonia Tauno Kangro membuat monumen jenaka lebih besar dari manusia untuk sang raksasa dan istrinya di promenade pantai Kuressaare, ibu kota pulau itu.
claims.quote: 2002 schuf der estnische Bildhauer Tauno Kangro ein übermannsgroßes, schelmisches Denkmal für den Riesen und seine Frau an der Uferpromenade der Inselhauptstadt Kuressaare.

claims.statement: Suur Tõll is a positive figure of the mythology.
claims.statement_id: Suur Tõll adalah tokoh mitologi yang berwatak positif.
claims.quote: Der Suur Tõll ist eine positive Gestalt der Mythologie.

claims.statement: The ala is a female mythological being in Bulgarian, Macedonian and Serbian folklore; ale are demons of bad weather whose main aim is to lead hail-producing thunderclouds over fields, vineyards or orchards to destroy or loot the crops.
claims.statement_id: Ala adalah makhluk mitologis perempuan dalam folklor orang Bulgaria, Makedonia, dan Serbia; ale dianggap iblis cuaca buruk yang tujuan utamanya menggiring awan guntur pembawa hujan es ke ladang, kebun anggur, atau kebun buah untuk menghancurkan atau menjarah panen.
claims.quote: is a female mythological creature recorded in the folklore of Bulgarians, Macedonians, and Serbs. Ale are considered demons of bad weather whose main purpose is to lead hail-producing thunderclouds in the direction of fields, vineyards, or orchards to destroy the crops, or loot and take them away.

claims.statement: Ale are extremely voracious and especially like to eat children; they are believed to sometimes try devouring the Sun or Moon, causing eclipses, and the world would end if they succeeded.
claims.statement_id: Ale sangat rakus dan terutama suka memakan anak-anak; mereka dipercaya kadang mencoba melahap Matahari atau Bulan sehingga terjadi gerhana, dan dunia akan berakhir jika mereka berhasil.
claims.quote: Extremely voracious, ale particularly like to eat children, though their gluttony is not limited to Earth. It is believed they sometimes try devouring the Sun or the Moon, causing eclipses, and that it would mean the end of the world should they succeed.

claims.statement: Meeting an ala endangers mental or physical health or even life, but her favour can be won with respect and trust, and she makes her favourites rich and saves their lives in times of trouble.
claims.statement_id: Bertemu ala membahayakan kesehatan jiwa atau raga, bahkan nyawa; namun kebaikannya dapat diraih dengan mendekatinya secara hormat dan percaya, dan ia membuat orang kesayangannya kaya serta menyelamatkan nyawa mereka saat kesulitan.
claims.quote: When people encounter an ala, their mental or physical health, or even life, are in peril; however, her favor can be gained by approaching her with respect and trust. Being in a good relationship with an ala is very beneficial, because she makes her favorites rich and saves their lives in times of trouble.

claims.statement: An ala may look like a black wind, a gigantic creature of unclear form, a huge-mouthed humanlike or snakelike monster, a dragoness or a raven; she may also take human or animal shapes and possess a person's body.
claims.statement_id: Ala bisa berwujud angin hitam, makhluk raksasa yang bentuknya tak jelas, monster bermulut besar yang mirip manusia atau ular, naga betina, atau gagak; ia juga bisa mengambil berbagai rupa manusia atau hewan dan merasuki tubuh seseorang.
claims.quote: A given ala may look like a black wind, a gigantic creature of indistinct form, a huge-mouthed, humanlike, or snakelike monster, a dragoness, or a raven. An ala may also assume various human or animal shapes, and can even possess a person's body.

claims.statement: The variety of the ala's appearances is believed to stem from her being a synthesis of a Slavic bad-weather demon and a similar demon of the central Balkans' pre-Slavic population.
claims.statement_id: Keragaman wujud ala diduga karena ia perpaduan iblis cuaca buruk Slavia dengan iblis serupa dari penduduk pra-Slavia di Balkan tengah.
claims.quote: It is believed that the diversity of appearances described is due to the ala's being a synthesis of a Slavic demon of bad weather and a similar demon of the central Balkans pre-Slavic population.

claims.statement: Ale are said to live in the clouds or in a lake, spring, hidden remote place, forest, inhospitable mountain, cave or gigantic tree.
claims.statement_id: Ale dikatakan tinggal di awan, atau di danau, mata air, tempat terpencil tersembunyi, hutan, gunung yang tak ramah, gua, atau pohon raksasa.
claims.quote: Ale are said to live in the clouds, or in a lake, spring, hidden remote place, forest, inhospitable mountain, cave, or gigantic tree.

claims.statement: Ale are usually hostile to humans, but they have powerful foes able to defeat them, like dragons; in Christianized tales Saint Elijah takes the dragons' role, and sometimes both fight ale together.
claims.statement_id: Ale biasanya memusuhi manusia, tetapi mereka punya musuh kuat yang dapat mengalahkan mereka, seperti naga; dalam kisah yang dikristenkan, Santo Elia mengambil peran naga, dan kadang keduanya melawan ale bersama.
claims.quote: While ale are usually hostile towards humans, they do have other powerful enemies that can defeat them, like dragons. In Christianized tales, St. Elijah takes the dragons' role, but in some cases the saint and the dragons fight ale together.

claims.statement: Eagles are also regarded as defenders against ale, chasing them from fields and so keeping hail clouds away.
claims.statement_id: Elang juga dianggap pelindung terhadap ale, mengusir mereka dari ladang sehingga awan hujan es tidak datang.
claims.quote: Eagles are also regarded as defenders against ale, chasing them away from fields and thus preventing them from bringing hail clouds overhead.

claims.statement: In folk tales with a humanlike ala, her personality resembles the Russian Baba Yaga.
claims.statement_id: Dalam dongeng dengan ala berwujud manusia, wataknya mirip Baba Yaga dari Rusia.
claims.quote: In folk tales with a humanlike ala, her personality is similar to that of the Russian Baba Yaga.

claims.statement: The name may instead come from the Greek word for hail, χάλαζα.
claims.statement_id: Nama ala mungkin berasal dari kata Yunani untuk hujan es, χάλαζα.
claims.quote: The name may instead stem from the Greek word for hail, χάλαζα

claims.statement: According to Serbian scholar Marta Bjeletić, ala and hala come from Proto-South-Slavic *xala, from the Proto-Slavic root *xal-, denoting the fury of the elements.
claims.statement_id: Menurut ahli Serbia Marta Bjeletić, ala dan hala berasal dari kata benda Proto-Slavia Selatan *xala, yang diturunkan dari akar Proto-Slavia *xal-, yang menandakan amukan unsur-unsur alam.
claims.quote: According to Serbian scholar Marta Bjeletić, ala and hala stem from the noun *xala in Proto-South-Slavic ... That noun was derived from the Proto-Slavic root *xal-, denoting the fury of the elements.

claims.statement: Per several dictionaries the demon's name comes from Turkish ala (snake), a view rejected because that word lacks the h-sound.
claims.statement_id: Menurut beberapa kamus, nama iblis ini berasal dari kata Turki ala (ular), meskipun pendapat itu ditolak karena kata tersebut tidak memiliki bunyi h.
claims.quote: the demon’s name comes from the Turkish word ‘ala’ (snake) as that word lacks the h-sound

claims.statement: A very common opinion is that the ala is the dragon's sister and looks more or less like him.
claims.statement_id: Pendapat yang sangat umum adalah bahwa ala saudara perempuan naga dan rupanya kurang lebih mirip dengannya.
claims.quote: A very common opinion is that the ala is the sister of the dragon, and looks more or less like him.

claims.statement: In Bulgarian tradition, thunderstorms and hail clouds were read as a battle between the good dragon or eagle and the evil ala.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi Bulgaria, badai guntur dan awan hujan es ditafsirkan sebagai pertempuran antara naga atau elang yang baik dan ala yang jahat.
claims.quote: In Bulgarian tradition, thunderstorms and hail clouds were interpreted as a battle between the good dragon or eagle and the evil ala.

claims.statement: An ala, or hala (plural ale or hali), is a female mythological creature of Bulgarian, Macedonian and Serbian folklore.
claims.statement_id: Ala, atau hala (jamak ale atau hali), adalah makhluk mitologis perempuan dalam folklor Bulgaria, Makedonia, dan Serbia.
claims.quote: Une ala, ou hala (pluriel : ale ou hali), est une créature mythologique féminine présente dans le folklore bulgare, macédonien et serbe.

claims.statement: Ale are considered demons of bad weather whose chief aim is to drive hail clouds over fields, vineyards or orchards to destroy the crops.
claims.statement_id: Ale dianggap iblis cuaca buruk yang tujuan utamanya menggiring awan hujan es ke ladang, kebun anggur, atau kebun buah untuk menghancurkan panen.
claims.quote: Les ale sont considérés comme les démons du mauvais temps dont le principal but est de conduire des nuages de grêle vers des champs, des vignobles ou des vergers afin de détruire les récoltes.

claims.statement: Serbs in Kosovo believed the ala lowers her tail to the ground and hides her head in the clouds; anyone who saw her head went instantly insane.
claims.statement_id: Orang Serbia di Kosovo percaya bahwa ala menjulurkan ekornya ke tanah dan menyembunyikan kepalanya di awan; siapa pun yang melihat kepalanya langsung menjadi gila.
claims.quote: Serbs in Kosovo believed that the ala lowers her tail to the ground and hides her head in the clouds. Anyone who saw her head became instantly insane.

claims.statement: Goldhorn is a legendary white chamois buck, or alternatively an Alpine ibex, whose realm was the heights of Mount Triglav, Slovenia's highest mountain and the highest peak of the Julian Alps.
claims.statement_id: Goldhorn adalah chamois jantan putih legendaris, atau menurut versi lain ibex Alpen, yang wilayahnya di ketinggian Gunung Triglav, gunung tertinggi di Slovenia dan puncak tertinggi Alpen Julian.
claims.quote: is a legendary white chamois buck, or alternatively, an Alpine ibex, that had his realm in the heights of Mount Triglav, the highest mountain in Slovenia and the highest peak of the Julian Alps.

claims.statement: The legend is well known throughout Slovenia (especially Carinthia), and in Austrian Carinthia and Italian Friuli-Venezia Giulia.
claims.statement_id: Legenda ini dikenal luas di seluruh Slovenia (khususnya Carinthia), juga di Carinthia Austria dan Friuli-Venezia Giulia Italia.
claims.quote: The legend is well known throughout Slovenia (specifically Carinthia), as well as in Austrian Carinthia, and Italian Friuli-Venezia Giulia.

claims.statement: The Zlatorog story was first written down, adapted to late Romantic style and published by Karl Deschmann (Karel Dežman) in the Laibacher Zeitung no. 43 on 21 February 1868.
claims.statement_id: Kisah Zlatorog pertama kali ditulis, disesuaikan dengan gaya Romantik akhir, dan diterbitkan oleh Karl Deschmann (Karel Dežman) di Laibacher Zeitung no. 43 pada 21 Februari 1868.
claims.quote: The story about Zlatorog was first written down, adapted to the late Romantic style and published by Karl Deschmann (Karel Dežman) in the Laibacher Zeitung, no. 43, on 21 February 1868.

claims.statement: Goldhorn's golden horns were the key to a treasure hidden in the mountains around Triglav.
claims.statement_id: Tanduk emas Goldhorn adalah kunci menuju harta yang tersembunyi di pegunungan sekitar Triglav.
claims.quote: Goldhorn's golden horns were the key to a treasure hidden in the mountains around Triglav.

claims.statement: A brave young hunter from the Trenta Valley won a beautiful girl's heart with flowers, but one day a rich merchant from Venice courted her with golden jewellery and dancing.
claims.statement_id: Seorang pemburu muda pemberani dari Lembah Trenta memenangkan hati gadis cantik dengan bunga, tetapi suatu hari saudagar kaya dari Venesia merebut perhatiannya dengan perhiasan emas dan tarian.
claims.quote: A young and brave hunter from the Trenta Valley fell in love with a beautiful girl and managed to win her heart by bringing her beautiful flowers. However, one day, a rich merchant from Venice came by and tried to gain her attention by giving her golden jewelry and dancing with her.

claims.statement: Persuaded by another hunter, the "green hunter", said to have doomed several honest lads, he decided that very night to seek Goldhorn and claim its treasure.
claims.statement_id: Dibujuk pemburu lain, si "pemburu hijau" yang konon telah mencelakai beberapa pemuda jujur, ia memutuskan malam itu juga mencari Goldhorn dan merebut hartanya.
claims.quote: Persuaded by another hunter, called the green hunter, who was said to have brought about the fate of several honest boys, he decided to go that very night to find Goldhorn and claim his treasure.

claims.statement: The green hunter pushed him to catch Goldhorn before it ate the magic Triglav flowers growing from its blood, but too late: Goldhorn had eaten one, gaining tremendous life power.
claims.statement_id: Pemburu hijau mendesaknya menangkap Goldhorn sebelum hewan itu memakan bunga ajaib Triglav yang tumbuh dari darahnya, tetapi terlambat: Goldhorn sudah memakan satu dan bunga itu memberinya daya hidup yang luar biasa.
claims.quote: The green hunter forced him on to catch the Goldhorn before it ate the magic Triglav flowers that grew from its blood, but it was too late. The Goldhorn had already eaten one and the flower gave it tremendous life power.

claims.statement: It ran at the hunter, who, dazzled by its golden horns, lost his balance and fell from the mountain; the river Soča carried his body to the vale.
claims.statement_id: Goldhorn berlari ke arah si pemburu, yang silau oleh kilau tanduk emasnya, kehilangan keseimbangan, dan jatuh dari gunung; Sungai Soča membawa jasadnya ke lembah.
claims.quote: It ran towards the hunter, who being blinded by the bliss of its golden horns, lost balance and fell from the mountain. The river Soča brought his corpse to the vale.

claims.statement: The Goldhorn story was put into verse by Rudolf Baumbach, published in 1877 and his most popular work; Camilla and Eduard Lucerna turned it into an opera.
claims.statement_id: Kisah Goldhorn digubah menjadi puisi oleh Rudolf Baumbach dan terbit pada 1877, menjadi karyanya yang paling populer; Camilla dan Eduard Lucerna menjadikannya opera.
claims.quote: The story of Goldhorn was put into verses by Rudolf Baumbach and published in 1877, becoming his most popular work. It was turned into an opera by Camilla and Eduard Lucerna.

claims.statement: The first full-length Slovene-language film, recorded by Janko Ravnik in 1931, was titled In the Kingdom of the Goldhorn.
claims.statement_id: Film panjang pertama berbahasa Slovenia, direkam Janko Ravnik pada 1931, berjudul In the Kingdom of the Goldhorn.
claims.quote: The first Slovene-language, full-length film, recorded in 1931 by Janko Ravnik, was titled In the Kingdom of the Goldhorn.

claims.statement: Zlatorog is also a beer brand produced by the Laško Brewery.
claims.statement_id: Zlatorog juga merupakan merek bir produksi pabrik bir Laško.
claims.quote: Zlatorog is also a brand of beer produced by the Laško Brewery.

claims.statement: Zlatorog (German: Goldhorn) is a legendary figure from the Slovenian Alps.
claims.statement_id: Zlatorog (bahasa Jerman: Goldhorn) adalah tokoh legenda dari Pegunungan Alpen Slovenia.
claims.quote: Zlatorog (deutsch: Goldhorn) ist eine Sagengestalt aus den slowenischen Alpen.

claims.statement: He had golden horns, owned a garden high on Triglav and was guardian of a hidden treasure.
claims.statement_id: Ia bertanduk emas, memiliki taman tinggi di Triglav, dan menjadi penjaga harta tersembunyi.
claims.quote: Er hatte goldene Hörner, besaß hoch oben am Triglav einen Garten und war Hüter eines verborgenen Schatzes.

claims.statement: From the slain chamois's blood a wonder flower sprang up at once and gave Zlatorog back his life; in a rage he killed the wrongdoer, then destroyed his mountain garden and was never seen again.
claims.statement_id: Dari darah chamois yang terbunuh seketika tumbuh bunga ajaib yang menghidupkan Zlatorog kembali; dengan murka ia membunuh si penjahat, lalu menghancurkan taman gunungnya dan tak pernah terlihat lagi.
claims.quote: Aus dem Blut des getöteten Gamsbocks wuchs auf der Stelle eine Wunderblume, die Zlatorog das Leben zurückgab. In rasender Wut tötete Zlatorog den Übeltäter. Hernach zerstörte er seinen Gebirgsgarten und ward nie mehr gesehen.

claims.statement: Zlatorog means "golden horn" in Slovene; the legend is famous in Slovenia, especially the Koroška region.
claims.statement_id: Zlatorog (ズラトロク) dalam bahasa Slovenia berarti "tanduk emas"; legendanya terkenal di Slovenia, terutama wilayah Koroška.
claims.quote: ズラトロクとは、スロベニア語で「金の角」を意味する。この伝説は、スロベニア、特にコロシュカ地方で有名であり

claims.statement: In Slovene folklore he is called Goldhorn or Goldenhorn.
claims.statement_id: Dalam folklor Slovenia ia disebut Goldhorn atau Goldenhorn.
claims.quote: In Slovene folklore, Goldhorn or Goldenhorn

claims.statement: Drekavac (literally "the screamer"), also called drekalo, krekavac, zdrekavac or zrikavac, is a South Slavic mythical creature; the name comes from the verb drečati ("to screech").
claims.statement_id: Drekavac (harfiah "si penjerit"), juga disebut drekalo, krekavac, zdrekavac, atau zrikavac, adalah makhluk mitos Slavia Selatan; namanya diturunkan dari kata kerja drečati ("menjerit").
claims.quote: Drekavac (literally "the screamer" or "the screecher"), also called drekalo, krekavac, zdrekavac or zrikavac, is a mythical creature in South Slavic mythology. The name is derived from the verb "drečati" ("to screech").

claims.statement: In some folk tales it is an undead man who leaves his grave by night to haunt the living.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebagian cerita rakyat ia digambarkan sebagai lelaki mayat hidup yang keluar dari kubur pada malam hari untuk menghantui orang hidup.
claims.quote: In some folk tales it is depicted as an undead man who emerges from his grave by night to haunt the living.

claims.statement: In others it is an unbaptised child rising from its grave at night to haunt its parents, sometimes heard begging people passing cemeteries to baptise it and end its misery.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita lain ia anak yang belum dibaptis yang bangkit dari kubur pada malam hari untuk menghantui orang tuanya, dan kadang terdengar memohon kepada orang yang lewat di kuburan agar membaptisnya.
claims.quote: In others the revenant is portrayed as unbaptised child which rises from its grave at night to haunt its parents and can also sometimes be heard entreating people passing cemeteries to baptise it and thus end its misery.

claims.statement: In eastern Serbia it is depicted as a humanoid canine walking on its back legs.
claims.statement_id: Di Serbia timur ia digambarkan sebagai makhluk anjing mirip manusia yang berjalan dengan kaki belakang.
claims.quote: In Eastern Serbia it has been depicted in the form of a humanoid canine creature that walks on its back legs.

claims.statement: Around Arilje it is depicted as a long-necked, long-legged creature with a cat-like head.
claims.statement_id: Di sekitar Arilje ia digambarkan sebagai makhluk berleher dan berkaki panjang dengan kepala seperti kucing.
claims.quote: In the vicinity of Arilje it has been depicted in form of a long-necked long-legged creature with a cat-like head.

claims.statement: Around Gruža it is a dappled, elongated, spindle-thin creature with an oversized head; it cannot fly and is believed to be a dead child's soul.
claims.statement_id: Di sekitar Gruža ia berupa makhluk bertubuh belang, panjang, dan kurus dengan kepala terlalu besar; makhluk ini tidak bisa terbang dan dipercaya arwah anak yang mati.
claims.quote: In the vicinity of Gruža it has been depicted in the form of a creature having a dappled, elongated and spindle-thin body with a disproportionately large head. This creature can't fly and it is believed to be the soul of a dead child.

claims.statement: The drekavac was originally thought to come from the souls of sinful men or children who died unbaptised.
claims.statement_id: Drekavac semula dipercaya berasal dari jiwa orang berdosa atau anak yang mati tanpa dibaptis.
claims.quote: The drekavac was originally thought to have come from the souls of sinful men, or from children who died unbaptised.

claims.statement: It was believed to be visible only at night, especially in the twelve days of Christmas ("unbaptised days") and early spring, when other demons and mythical beings were thought more active.
claims.statement_id: Ia dipercaya hanya tampak pada malam hari, terutama pada dua belas hari Natal ("hari tanpa baptis") dan awal musim semi, ketika setan dan makhluk mitos lain dianggap lebih aktif.
claims.quote: It was popularly believed to be visible only at night, especially during the twelve days of Christmas (called unbaptised days in Serbo-Croatian) and in early spring, when other demons and mythical creatures were believed to be more active.

claims.statement: In child form it predicts a death, in animal form cattle disease; it avoids dogs and bright light, and a person its shadow falls on will sicken and die.
claims.statement_id: Dalam rupa anak ia meramalkan kematian seseorang, dalam rupa hewan ia meramalkan penyakit ternak; ia menghindari anjing dan cahaya terang, dan orang yang terkena bayangannya akan sakit lalu meninggal.
claims.quote: When assuming the form of a child, it predicts someone's death, while in its animal form, it predicts cattle disease. The drekavac is believed to avoid dogs and bright light. Also, it is believed that if the shadow of drekavac falls upon some person then that person will turn sick and die.

claims.statement: Though mostly used in cautionary tales for children, some adults still believe it exists.
claims.statement_id: Walaupun makhluk ini terutama dipakai dalam cerita peringatan untuk anak-anak, ada orang dewasa yang masih memercayai keberadaannya.
claims.quote: Although the creature is mostly used in cautionary tales for children, there are also some adults who still believe in its existence.

claims.statement: In 1992 villagers in Krvavica reportedly found remains of an animal unknown in the area and claimed it was a drekavac; it later proved to be a rotten fox carcass.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1992 dilaporkan bahwa penduduk Krvavica menemukan sisa hewan yang tak dikenal di daerah itu dan menyebutnya drekavac; belakangan terungkap itu hanya bangkai rubah yang membusuk.
claims.quote: In 1992, it was reported that in the Krvavica, the villagers found remains of an animal unlike any known from the area, and claimed it was a drekavac. ... Later, it was revealed to be just a rotten carcass of a fox.

claims.statement: Its legend is found mainly among the people of Serbia (from Šumadija to Kosovo), Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia and Montenegro.
claims.statement_id: Legendanya terutama dikenal di kalangan penduduk Serbia (dari Choumadie atau Šumadija sampai Kosovo), Bosnia-Herzegovina, Kroasia, dan Montenegro.
claims.quote: Sa légende se retrouve essentiellement parmi les habitants de la Serbie (de la Choumadie jusqu'au Kosovo), de la Bosnie-Herzégovine, de la Croatie et du Monténégro.

claims.statement: The drekavac is a mythical creature of South Slavic folklore; in the common view it is the soul of a dead unbaptised infant.
claims.statement_id: Drekavac adalah makhluk mitos dari folklor Slavia Selatan; menurut anggapan yang tersebar luas, ia arwah bayi yang mati tanpa dibaptis.
claims.quote: мифическое существо из фольклора южных славян, по распространённому представлению — душа мёртвого некрещёного младенца.

claims.statement: Around Prijepolje, Lešak and Dragačevo it is an apparition in the form of a dappled foal, dog, cat or bird.
claims.statement_id: Di sekitar Prijepolje, Lešak, dan Dragačevo ia digambarkan sebagai penampakan berupa anak kuda belang, anjing, kucing, atau burung.
claims.quote: In the vicinity of Prijepolje, Lešak and Dragačevo it has been depicted as an apparition that can be seen in form of a dappled foal, dog, cat, or bird.

claims.statement: The Mermaid of Warsaw is a symbol of Warsaw, shown on the city's coat of arms and in many statues and other images.
claims.statement_id: Putri Duyung Warsawa adalah lambang Warsawa, ditampilkan pada lambang kota serta dalam sejumlah patung dan gambar lain.
claims.quote: is a symbol of Warsaw, represented on the city's coat of arms as well as in a number of statues and other imagery.

claims.statement: Polish syrenka is a cognate of siren, but she is more properly a freshwater mermaid called a melusina.
claims.statement_id: Kata Polandia syrenka seakar dengan "siren", tetapi sosok ini lebih tepat disebut melusina, putri duyung air tawar.
claims.quote: Polish syrenka is a cognate of siren, but she is more properly a fresh-water mermaid called melusina.

claims.statement: A melusina is a mythical winged, fish-tailed freshwater spirit living in rivers or wells.
claims.statement_id: Melusina adalah roh air tawar mitis yang bersayap dan berekor ikan, hidup di sungai atau sumur.
claims.quote: A melusina is a mythical freshwater winged and fish-tailed spirit who lives in rivers or wells.

claims.statement: In 1390 the Warsaw arms showed a creature with bird legs and a dragon-scaled torso; the 1459 seal had female features, a bird torso, human hands, a fishtail and bird legs and claws; the first mermaid dates from 1622.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1390 lambang Warsawa memuat makhluk berkaki burung dengan tubuh bersisik naga; segel 1459 berciri perempuan, bertubuh burung, bertangan manusia, berekor ikan, berkaki dan bercakar burung; penggambaran putri duyung pertama berasal dari 1622.
claims.quote: A creature was on Warsaw's coat of arms in 1390. It showed an animal with a bird's legs and a torso covered with dragon scales. The seal of 1459 had feminine characteristics, a bird torso, human hands, a fishtail, and bird legs and claws. The first presentation of a mermaid dates from 1622.

claims.statement: The coat of arms was probably inspired by the 2nd-century book Physiologus.
claims.statement_id: Ilham lambang kota ini kemungkinan berasal dari buku Physiologus abad ke-2.
claims.quote: The inspiration for the coat of arms was probably derived from the 2nd-century book Physiologus.

claims.statement: City literature and guides say the mermaid chose to stay after stopping on a riverbank near the Old Town; fishermen saw something making waves, tangling nets and freeing their fish, planned to trap it, then heard her sing and fell in love.
claims.statement_id: Menurut literatur dan pemandu wisata kota, putri duyung itu memutuskan menetap setelah singgah di tepi sungai dekat Kota Tua; para nelayan melihat sesuatu membuat gelombang, mengusutkan jaring, dan melepaskan ikan, lalu berniat menangkapnya, tetapi jatuh cinta setelah mendengar nyanyiannya.
claims.quote: The City's literature and tour guides say the mermaid decided to stay after stopping on a riverbank near the Old Town. Fishermen noticed something was creating waves, tangling nets, and releasing their fish. They planned to trap the animal, then heard her singing and fell in love.

claims.statement: A rich merchant caught and imprisoned the mermaid; hearing her cries, the fishermen rescued her, and ever since, armed with sword and shield, she has stood ready to protect the city and its people.
claims.statement_id: Seorang saudagar kaya menangkap dan mengurung putri duyung itu; mendengar tangisnya, para nelayan menyelamatkannya, dan sejak itu ia, bersenjata pedang dan perisai, siap membantu melindungi kota dan warganya.
claims.quote: A rich merchant trapped and imprisoned the mermaid. Hearing her cries, the fishermen rescued her. Ever since, the mermaid, armed with a sword and a shield, has been ready to help protect the city and its residents.

claims.statement: The legend is sometimes extended to say the Little Mermaid in Copenhagen is the Warsaw mermaid's sister, the two parting ways from the Baltic Sea.
claims.statement_id: Kadang legenda ini diperluas dengan menyebut Putri Duyung Kecil di Kopenhagen sebagai saudari putri duyung Warsawa, dan keduanya berpisah jalan dari Laut Baltik.
claims.quote: Sometimes this legend is expanded to say the Little Mermaid in Copenhagen is the Warsaw mermaid's sister and they went separate ways from the Baltic Sea.

claims.statement: Another says she helped a prince lost while hunting, and he founded the city in her honour.
claims.statement_id: Legenda lain menyebut ia menolong seorang pangeran yang tersesat saat berburu, dan pangeran itu mendirikan kota untuk menghormatinya.
claims.quote: Another states she helped a prince lost hunting and he founded the city in her honour.

claims.statement: The sculpture in Warsaw's Old Town Square was designed by Warsaw sculptor Konstanty Hegel.
claims.statement_id: Patung di alun-alun Kota Tua Warsawa dirancang oleh pematung Warsawa Konstanty Hegel.
claims.quote: The sculpture in Warsaw's Old Town Square was designed by Varsovian sculptor Konstanty Hegel.

claims.statement: This gunmetal statue was erected in April 1939 in Powiśle near the Vistula; it is by Ludwika Nitschowa, modelled by the poet Krystyna Krahelska.
claims.statement_id: Patung dari perunggu senapan ini didirikan pada April 1939 di Powiśle dekat Sungai Vistula; karya Ludwika Nitschowa dengan model penyair Krystyna Krahelska.
claims.quote: This statue, made of gunmetal, was erected in April 1939 in Powiśle near the Vistula river. The sculpture is by Ludwika Nitschowa and posed by poet Krystyna Krahelska.

claims.statement: In her left hand (linken Hand) she holds a shield (Schild), in her right a sword (Schwert).
claims.statement_id: Di tangan kiri (linken Hand) ia memegang perisai (Schild), di tangan kanan sebilah pedang (Schwert).
claims.quote: In der linken Hand hält sie einen Schild, in der rechten ein Schwert.

claims.statement: The Warsaw mermaid (Polish: Warszawska Syrenka) is a symbolic figure of Warsaw and, as a sea-woman, the figure on the Warsaw coat of arms.
claims.statement_id: Putri Duyung Warsawa (bahasa Polandia: Warszawska Syrenka) adalah tokoh lambang Warsawa dan, dalam wujud perempuan laut, menjadi sosok pada lambang kota Warsawa.
claims.quote: Die Warschauer Seejungfer (polnisch: Warszawska Syrenka) ist eine Symbolgestalt von Warschau und in Form einer Meerfrau Gestalt des Warschauer Stadtwappens.

claims.statement: The current form, a woman with a fish tail, dates from 1622 and is still in use today.
claims.statement_id: Wujud saat ini, perempuan berekor ikan, berasal dari tahun 1622 dan berlaku sampai sekarang.
claims.quote: Die aktuelle Gestalt einer Frau mit einem Fischschwanz stammt aus dem Jahre 1622. Diese Anordnung gilt bis heute.

claims.statement: In Slavic mythology the polevik or polewik are field spirits appearing as deformed creatures with differently coloured eyes and grass for hair; they appear at noon or sunset, dressed all in black or all in white.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Slavia, polevik atau polewik adalah roh ladang yang tampak sebagai makhluk cacat dengan mata berlainan warna dan rumput sebagai pengganti rambut; mereka muncul pada tengah hari atau matahari terbenam dan berpakaian serba hitam atau serba putih.
claims.quote: Polevik or Polewik in Slavic mythology are field spirits that appear as a deformed creatures with different coloured eyes and grass instead of hair. They appear either at noon or sunset and wear either all black or all white suits.

claims.statement: South Russian folklore describes them as green-haired field spirits; local belief says they lead wanderers astray, give them diseases, or ride over sleepers with their horses.
claims.statement_id: Cerita rakyat Rusia selatan menggambarkan mereka sebagai roh ladang berambut hijau; menurut kepercayaan setempat mereka menyesatkan pengembara di ladang, menularkan penyakit, atau menggilas orang yang tertidur dengan kuda mereka.
claims.quote: They are also described in south Russian folklore as field spirits with green hair. According to local beliefs they lead wandering people in a field astray, give them diseases or ride them over with their horses if they are found asleep.

claims.statement: A person who falls asleep at work after drinking may be murdered by the polevik; appeasing it needs two eggs, a rooster, a toad and a crow placed in a ditch unseen.
claims.statement_id: Orang yang tertidur saat bekerja setelah minum bisa dibunuh polevik; untuk menenangkannya diperlukan dua telur, seekor ayam jantan, seekor kodok, dan seekor gagak yang ditaruh di parit tanpa dilihat orang.
claims.quote: If a person falls asleep on the job after drinking, the Polewiki might murder them. Appeasing the Polewiki requires two eggs, a rooster, a toad, and a crow placed in a ditch when no one is looking.

claims.statement: The polevik or polevoy (Belarusian palyavik, Ukrainian polovyk) is the spirit-master of the field in East Slavic mythology.
claims.statement_id: Polevik atau polevoy (bahasa Belarus: paljavik, bahasa Ukraina: polovyk) adalah roh penguasa ladang dalam mitologi Slavia Timur.
claims.quote: Полеви́к, полево́й (бел. паляві́к, укр. польови́к)  — дух-хозяин поля в мифологии восточных славян.

claims.statement: There are fragmentary beliefs that the polevik guarded the field and influenced its fertility and the well-being of livestock grazing on it.
claims.statement_id: Ada keyakinan yang terpisah-pisah bahwa polevik menjaga ladang, memengaruhi kesuburannya dan kesejahteraan ternak yang merumput di sana.
claims.quote: Есть отрывочные представления о том, что полевик охранял поле, влиял на его плодородие и благополучие пасущегося на нём скота

claims.statement: Towards people the polevik was mostly hostile: it could frighten, lead off the road and even kill, and harm livestock and crops.
claims.statement_id: Terhadap manusia polevik umumnya bermusuhan: ia bisa menakut-nakuti, menyesatkan dari jalan, bahkan membunuh, serta merusak ternak dan tanaman.
claims.quote: К человеку полевой относился в основном враждебно: мог напугать, сбить с дороги и даже убить, а также навредить скотине и посевам

claims.statement: It is described mainly as a human-like being with some animal, plant and demonic traits, sometimes accompanied by strong wind and sparks or lights.
claims.statement_id: Polevik digambarkan terutama sebagai makhluk mirip manusia dengan sejumlah ciri hewan, tumbuhan, dan iblis, kadang disertai angin kencang dan percikan api atau cahaya.
claims.quote: Он описывается в основном как человекоподобное существо с отдельными животными, растительными и демоничными чертами, которого иногда сопровождает сильный ветер и искры или огоньки

claims.statement: The polevik stands in contrast to the noon demoness of the fields, Poludnisa.
claims.statement_id: Polevik dibandingkan secara berlawanan dengan Poludnitsa (Poludnisa), iblis perempuan ladang yang muncul pada tengah hari.
claims.quote: Polevik stands in contrast to the demoness of fields appearing at noon: Poludnisa

claims.statement: Beliefs about the polevik were rare, so the image that has reached us is rather vague.
claims.statement_id: Kepercayaan tentang polevik jarang ditemukan, sehingga gambaran yang sampai kepada kita cukup kabur.
claims.quote: Представления о полевике встречались редко, и, соответственно, дошедший до нас образ довольно смутен

claims.statement: In some places people asked the polevik to watch grazing livestock, and elsewhere brought it gifts so it would favour a good harvest.
claims.statement_id: Di beberapa tempat orang meminta polevik menjaga ternak yang merumput, dan di tempat lain ia diberi persembahan agar memberi panen yang baik.
claims.quote: В некоторых местах к полевому обращались с просьбой приглядеть за пасущейся скотиной, а кое-где ему приносили дары, чтобы он поблагоприятствовал хорошему урожаю.

claims.statement: Bies, bes (Russian) or bijes (Croatian) is an evil spirit or demon in Slavic mythology; under Christian influence the word often became synonymous with chort.
claims.statement_id: Bies, bes (bahasa Rusia), atau bijes (bahasa Kroasia) adalah roh jahat atau iblis dalam mitologi Slavia; di bawah pengaruh agama Kristen kata ini sering bersinonim dengan chort.
claims.quote: is an evil spirit or demon in Slavic mythology. Under the influence of Christianity the word often became synonymous with chort.

claims.statement: After Christianity was accepted, the bies (like chort or czort) was identified with the devil, corresponding to the Ancient Greek daimon.
claims.statement_id: Setelah agama Kristen diterima, bies (sama dengan chort atau czort) disamakan dengan iblis, sepadan dengan makhluk yang dalam bahasa Yunani Kuno disebut daimon.
claims.quote: After the acceptance of Christianity the bies (same as chort or czort) became identified with the devil, corresponding to the being referred to in Ancient Greek, as either daimon

claims.statement: In Slovenian (bes), Croatian (bijes) and Serbian (bes) the word means "rage", "fury"; it comes from Proto-Slavic běsъ.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Slovenia (bes), Kroasia (bijes), dan Serbia (bes), kata ini berarti "amarah" atau "kemurkaan"; asalnya dari kata Slavia Purba (proto-Slavic) běsъ.
claims.quote: In Slovenian (bes), Croatian (bijes) and Serbian (bes) the word means "rage", "fury". It comes from the proto-Slavic běsъ.

claims.statement: In Slavic folk demonology the idea of the bes developed under the influence of the written (church) tradition, converging and merging with beliefs about the chort and the devil.
claims.statement_id: Dalam demonologi rakyat Slavia, gambaran tentang bes berkembang di bawah pengaruh tradisi tulis (gereja), mendekat dan berbaur dengan kepercayaan tentang chort dan iblis.
claims.quote: В народной демонологии славян представления о бесе развивались под влиянием книжной (церковной) традиции, сближаясь и смешиваясь с поверьями о чёрте, дьяволе.

claims.statement: According to Christian teaching, demons can "enter" a person, which is called "possession by demons".
claims.statement_id: Menurut ajaran Kristen, bes dapat "masuk" ke dalam diri manusia, yang disebut "kerasukan bes".
claims.quote: Согласно христианскому учению, бесы могут «вселяться» в человека, это называется «одержимость бесами» или «беснованием»

claims.statement: In old Slavic mythological depictions the biesy are evil spirits, lesser demonic characters and personifications of forces hostile to humans, with all kinds of superhuman abilities.
claims.statement_id: Dalam gambaran mitologis Slavia kuno, biesy adalah roh jahat, tokoh iblis tingkat rendah, dan perwujudan kekuatan yang memusuhi manusia, dengan segala macam kemampuan adikodrati.
claims.quote: In altslawischen mythologischen Darstellungen sind Biesy böse Geister, niedere dämonische Charaktere und Personifizierungen menschenfeindlicher Kräfte, die alle Arten von übermenschlichen Fähigkeiten haben.

claims.statement: The biesy had no fixed image; in folklore they combined human and animal features.
claims.statement_id: Biesy tidak memiliki rupa yang tetap; dalam cerita rakyat mereka memadukan ciri manusia dan hewan.
claims.quote: Biesy hatten kein festes Bild. In der Folklore kombinierten sie menschliche und tierische Merkmale.

claims.statement: In the 2015 video game The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, fiends (called bies in the original) are massive horned predators with hypnotic and self-healing powers.
claims.statement_id: Dalam gim video The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt (2015), makhluk "fiend" (dalam versi asli disebut bies) adalah pemangsa bertanduk raksasa dengan kekuatan hipnotis dan penyembuhan diri.
claims.quote: In the 2015 videogame The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, fiends (called bies in the original version) are massive horned predators who possess hypnotic and self-healing powers.

claims.statement: Possessing demons drive a person to harmful excess in behaviour and various mental illnesses.
claims.statement_id: Bes yang merasuk mendorong manusia pada perilaku berlebihan yang merugikan dan berbagai penyakit jiwa.
claims.quote: Вселившиеся бесы влекут человека к вредному излишеству в поведении и различным психическим болезням.

claims.statement: Iku-Turso refers to one or multiple giants in Finnish mythology; in the Kalevala it is a malevolent sea monster.
claims.statement_id: Iku-Turso merujuk pada satu atau beberapa raksasa dalam mitologi Finlandia; dalam Kalevala, Iku-Turso adalah monster laut yang jahat.
claims.quote: refers to one or multiple giants in Finnish mythology. In the Kalevala, Iku-Turso is a malevolent sea monster.

claims.statement: Iku-Turso is also known as Iku-Tursas, Iki-Tursas, Meritursas, Tursas and Turisas, among others.
claims.statement_id: Iku-Turso juga dikenal antara lain sebagai Iku-Tursas, Iki-Tursas, Meritursas, Tursas, dan Turisas.
claims.quote: also known as Iku-Tursas, Iki-Tursas, Meritursas, Tursas, Turisas among others

claims.statement: The name Turisas is probably an early loanword from Proto-Germanic *þurisaz, "giant".
claims.statement_id: Nama Turisas kemungkinan kata pinjaman awal dari bahasa Proto-Jermanik (Proto-Germanic) *þurisaz, "raksasa".
claims.quote: The name Turisas is probably an early loanword from the Proto-Germanic *þurisaz 'giant'.

claims.statement: Tursas or multiple tursaat are linked to epithets: partalainen ("the one who lives on the brink" or "the bearded one"), Tuonen härkä ("the ox of Tuoni"), tuhatpää ("thousand-headed"), tuhatsarvi ("thousand-horned").
claims.statement_id: Tursas atau para tursaat dikaitkan dengan beberapa julukan: partalainen ("yang tinggal di tepi" atau "yang berjanggut"), Tuonen härkä ("lembu Tuoni"), tuhatpää ("berkepala seribu"), dan tuhatsarvi ("bertanduk seribu").
claims.quote: Tursas or multiple tursaat are connected to multiple epithets: partalainen 'the one who lives on the brink', or alternatively, 'the bearded one', Tuonen härkä 'the ox of Tuoni', tuhatpää 'thousand-headed', tuhatsarvi 'thousand-horned'.

claims.statement: Another song mentions Meri-Tursas, "Sea Tursas", who impregnates Loviatar, Maiden of North, with waves as she seeks relief in water; Loviatar then gives birth to the diseases of the world.
claims.statement_id: Satu lagu menyebut Meri-Tursas ("Tursas Laut") yang menghamili Loviatar, Gadis dari Utara (Maiden of North), melalui ombak saat ia mencari kelegaan dari rasa sakit di air; akibatnya Loviatar melahirkan penyakit-penyakit dunia.
claims.quote: Another song mentions Meri-Tursas 'Sea Tursas' who impregnates Maiden of North Loviatar with waves when she is seeking relief for her pain in water. As a result, Loviatar gives birth to the diseases of the world.

claims.statement: In Mikael Agricola's list of Tavastian gods, Turisas is the god of war ("Turisas brought victory through war"); it has been suggested he is the Scandinavian war god Tyr, but this is not widely supported today.
claims.statement_id: Dalam daftar dewa Tavastia (Tavastie) karya Mikael Agricola, Turisas disebut dewa perang ("Turisas memberi kemenangan dalam perang"); ada usulan bahwa ia sama dengan Tyr, dewa perang Skandinavia, tetapi teori ini kini tidak banyak didukung.
claims.quote: Dans la liste des dieux de Tavastie, de Mikael Agricola, il est mentionné comme le dieu de la guerre: Turisas voiton antoi sodast « Turisas a apporté la victoire par la guerre ». Il a été suggéré que le dieu de cette liste est le même que le dieu scandinave de la guerre Tyr ; cependant, cette théorie n'est pas largement soutenue aujourd'hui.

claims.statement: Iku-Turso is a malevolent sea monster of Finnish mythology.
claims.statement_id: Iku-Turso adalah monster laut yang jahat dalam mitologi Finlandia.
claims.quote: Iku-Turso est un monstre marin maléfique de la mythologie finnoise.

claims.statement: According to Anna-Leena Siikala, Turisas and Tursas were likely originally two different beings that got mixed in runic songs.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Anna-Leena Siikala, Turisas dan Tursas kemungkinan semula dua makhluk berbeda yang kemudian tercampur dalam lagu-lagu runik.
claims.quote: According to Anna-Leena Siikala, it is likely that Turisas and Tursas were originally two different beings who got mixed with each other in runic songs.

claims.statement: Its appearance remains uncertain, but several epithets are used to describe it.
claims.statement_id: Wujudnya tetap tidak pasti, tetapi beberapa julukan dipakai untuk menggambarkannya.
claims.quote: Son apparence reste incertaine, mais plusieurs épithètes sont utilisés pour le décrire

claims.statement: There is no scholarly consensus whether the multiple mentions of Tursas in runic songs refer to one being or several.
claims.statement_id: Para ahli belum sepakat apakah berbagai penyebutan Tursas dalam lagu-lagu runik merujuk pada satu makhluk atau beberapa makhluk berbeda.
claims.quote: There is no consensus among scholars if the multiple Tursas mentions in runic songs refer to one being or multiple different ones.

claims.statement: In 1551 Mikael Agricola mentioned Turisas as the god of war ("Turisas brought victory in war").
claims.statement_id: Pada tahun 1551, Mikael Agricola menyebut Turisas sebagai dewa perang ("Turisas memberi kemenangan dalam perang").
claims.quote: In 1551, Mikael Agricola mentioned Turisas as the god of war: Turisas voiton antoi sodast 'Turisas brought victory in war'.

claims.statement: Sava Savanović is one of the most famous vampires in Balkan and Serbian folklore.
claims.statement_id: Sava Savanović (Сава Савановић) adalah salah satu vampir paling terkenal dalam cerita rakyat Balkan dan Serbia.
claims.quote: is one of the most famous vampires in Balkan and Serbian folklore.

claims.statement: Sava Savanović was said to have lived in an old watermill on the Rogačica river at Zarožje village, Bajina Bašta, killing and drinking the blood of millers who came to mill grain.
claims.statement_id: Sava Savanović konon tinggal di kincir air tua di Sungai Rogačica, desa Zarožje, wilayah Bajina Bašta, dan membunuh serta meminum darah para penggiling yang datang menggiling biji-bijian.
claims.quote: Sava Savanović was said to have lived in an old watermill on the Rogačica river, at Zarožje village in the municipality of Bajina Bašta. It was said that he killed and drank the blood of the millers when they came to mill their grains.

claims.statement: Sava Savanović remains the best-known vampire in Serbia today.
claims.statement_id: Sava Savanović hingga kini tetap vampir yang paling dikenal di Serbia.
claims.quote: Sava Savanović still remains as the best known vampire in Serbia today.

claims.statement: The stories were passed down only orally and differ in place and actors, but all share a core: a man from the village of Zarožje.
claims.statement_id: Kisah-kisahnya hanya diwariskan secara lisan dan berbeda soal tempat dan pelaku, tetapi semuanya punya inti yang sama: seorang laki-laki dari desa Zarožje.
claims.quote: Sie wurden ausschließlich mündlich überliefert und unterscheiden sich bezüglich Ort und den beteiligten Akteuren, haben aber alle eine gemeinsame Kerngeschichte: in allen Geschichten geht es um einen Mann aus dem Dorf Zarožje

claims.statement: After millers in the watermills on the Rogačica were repeatedly found dead with bite marks on their necks, villagers concluded that Sava had become a vampire.
claims.statement_id: Setelah para penggiling di kincir air Sungai Rogačica berulang kali ditemukan tewas dengan bekas gigitan di leher, penduduk segera yakin bahwa Sava telah menjadi vampir.
claims.quote: Nachdem jedoch wiederholt Müller in den Wassermühlen am Fluss Rogačica tot aufgefunden wurden, welche alle Bissspuren am Hals aufwiesen, war für die Bewohner schnell klar: Sava war ein Vampir geworden.

claims.statement: In all versions Sava Savanović's grave was opened and an undecayed corpse found; to break the curse a sharpened stake was driven through the vampire's heart.
claims.statement_id: Dalam semua versi, kubur Sava Savanović dibuka dan di dalamnya ditemukan jasad yang tidak membusuk; untuk mematahkan kutukan, sebuah pancang runcing ditancapkan ke jantung vampir itu.
claims.quote: Allen Versionen ist gleich, dass das Grab von Sava Savanović geöffnet wurde und man darin einen unverwesten Leichnam vorfand. Um den Fluch zu brechen, wurde dem Vampir ein spitzer Pfahl durch das Herz geschlagen.

claims.statement: Although usually said to be the first Serbian vampire, there are claims he was pre-dated in Serbian folklore by Petar Blagojević of Kisiljevo, who died in 1725.
claims.statement_id: Meski ia biasanya disebut vampir Serbia pertama, ada klaim bahwa dalam cerita rakyat Serbia ia didahului oleh Petar Blagojević dari Kisiljevo, yang meninggal pada 1725.
claims.quote: Although he is usually said to have been the first Serbian vampire, there are claims that he was pre-dated in Serbian folklore by Petar Blagojević from Kisiljevo, who died in 1725.

claims.statement: Sava Savanović appears in the story Posle devedeset godina ("Ninety Years Later") by the Serbian realist writer Milovan Glišić, and in the horror film Leptirica inspired by it.
claims.statement_id: Sava Savanović muncul dalam cerita Posle devedeset godina ("Sembilan Puluh Tahun Kemudian") karya penulis realis Serbia Milovan Glišić, dan dalam film horor Leptirica yang terilhami cerita itu.
claims.quote: Sava Savanović appears in the story Posle devedeset godina ("Ninety Years Later"), written by the Serbian realist writer Milovan Glišić, and in the horror film Leptirica inspired by the story.

claims.statement: The mill collapsed in 2012, and the municipal authorities issued a tongue-in-cheek warning that Savanović was now free to look for a new home.
claims.statement_id: Kincir air itu runtuh pada 2012, dan pemerintah kota mengeluarkan peringatan kesehatan bernada bercanda bahwa Savanović kini bebas mencari rumah baru.
claims.quote: The first finished project was the road, but just a month after it was completed, the mill collapsed in 2012. The municipal authorities issued a tongue-in-cheek public health warning, advising people that Savanović was now free to look for a new home.

claims.statement: Leptirica is a 1973 TV horror film.
claims.statement_id: Leptirica adalah film horor televisi tahun 1973.
claims.quote: TV-Horrorfilm Leptirica von 1973

issues.message: Diusulkan dilewati: Bukan makhluk: menurut sumber, táltos adalah manusia ("a person with supernatural power who acts as a spiritual mediator, akin to a shaman"), perantara spiritual seperti dukun/syaman yang dipilih sejak lahir. Sesuai aturan 3 Oktober 2026 (§12), manusia tidak dimasukkan. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T%C3%A1ltos).

claims.statement: Ahti is a water god in Finnish mythology; in the Kalevala he is called Ahto so as not to confuse him with the separate character Ahti Saarelainen.
claims.statement_id: Ahti adalah dewa air dalam mitologi Finlandia; dalam Kalevala ia disebut Ahto agar tidak tertukar dengan tokoh lain, Ahti Saarelainen.
claims.quote: Ahti is a water god in Finnish mythology. In the Kalevala, he is referred to with the name Ahto in order to not confuse him with the separate character Ahti Saarelainen.

claims.statement: Ahti was first mentioned in writing in 1551 by Mikael Agricola as the one who gave fish from water; Ganander called him a sea haltija who gave fish and whom shipwrecked fishermen called on for help.
claims.statement_id: Ahti pertama kali disebut secara tertulis pada 1551 oleh Mikael Agricola sebagai pemberi ikan dari air; Ganander menyebutnya haltija (roh) laut yang memberi ikan dan dimintai tolong oleh nelayan yang karam.
claims.quote: Ahti was first mentioned in writing in 1551 by Mikael Agricola as the one who gave fish from water (Achti wedhest caloia toi). Ganander called Ahti a sea haltija who gave fish and who shipwrecked fishermen called for help.

claims.statement: As a giver of fish he appears only in runic songs from Kainuu, addressed as "Golden King of the Sea, merciful Ahti of the Sea" and asked to give perches.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai pemberi ikan, ia hanya muncul dalam lagu-lagu runik dari Kainuu, disapa "Raja Emas Laut, Ahti Laut yang pengasih" dan dimintai ikan perch.
claims.quote: In this function, as a giver of fish, he only appears in runic songs from Kainuu, addressed as Meren kultanen kuninkas, / Meren Ahti armollinen 'Golden King of the Sea, merciful Ahti of the Sea' and asked to give perches.

claims.statement: Healing spells invoke him under several guises, such as Ahti of the Sea, of Water, of the Forest, of the Land and of the Wind.
claims.statement_id: Ahti juga muncul dalam mantra penyembuhan dalam berbagai wujud: Ahti Laut, Air, Hutan, Tanah, dan Angin.
claims.quote: Ahti also appears in healing spells in various forms: Ahti of the Sea, Water, Forest, Land, and Wind.

claims.statement: A later theory derives Ahti's name from the verb ahtaa, "to hang fishnets to dry", which would make Ahti a god guaranteeing luck in seining.
claims.statement_id: Menurut teori yang lebih kemudian, nama Ahti bisa berasal dari kata kerja ahtaa, "menggantung jaring ikan untuk dikeringkan", sehingga Ahti menjadi dewa yang menjamin keberuntungan dalam menjaring ikan.
claims.quote: According to a later theory, Ahti's name could come from the verb ahtaa 'to hang fishnets to dry'. A net drying rack is ahde. Similar words are found across Uralic languages. This would make Ahti a god who guarantees luck in seining.

claims.statement: In Finnish mythology Ahti or Ahto is the god of the sea and fishing, depicted as a man with a beard of moss; he is Vellamo's husband and both live in the undersea palace of Ahtola.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Finlandia, Ahti atau Ahto adalah dewa laut dan perikanan; ia digambarkan sebagai laki-laki berjanggut lumut, suami Vellamo, dan keduanya tinggal di istana bawah laut Ahtola.
claims.quote: Dans la mythologie finlandaise, Ahti ou Ahto est le dieu de la mer et de la pêche. Il est représenté comme un homme avec une barbe de mousse. Il est l'époux de Vellamo et ils demeurent tous deux dans le palais sous-marin de Ahtola.

claims.statement: Ahti is one of the heroic figures compiled by Elias Lönnrot in the Kalevala to create the character Lemminkäinen.
claims.statement_id: Ahti adalah salah satu tokoh kepahlawanan yang dihimpun Elias Lönnrot dalam Kalevala untuk membentuk tokoh Lemminkäinen (Lemminkaïnen).
claims.quote: Ahti est une des figures héroïques compilées par Elias Lönnrot dans le Kalevala pour créer le personnage de Lemminkaïnen.

claims.statement: The initial theory derived Ahti from the North Germanic word ahva, "water", or the same word family (ægir, "sea").
claims.statement_id: Teori awal mencari asal nama Ahti pada kata Jermanik Utara ahva, "air", atau rumpun kata yang sama (ægir, "laut").
claims.quote: Initial theory for the origin of the name Ahti was in the North Germanic word ahva 'water', or in the same family of words (ægir, 'sea').

claims.statement: Aitvaras is a nature spirit in Lithuanian mythology, also known as Atvaras, Damavykas, Pūkis, Sparyžius, Koklikas, Gausinėlis, Žaltvikšas and Spirukas, and identical to the Latvian Pūķis.
claims.statement_id: Aitvaras adalah roh alam dalam mitologi Lituania, juga dikenal dengan nama lain seperti Atvaras, Damavykas, Pūkis, Sparyžius, Koklikas, Gausinėlis, Žaltvikšas, dan Spirukas, serta identik dengan Pūķis dari Latvia.
claims.quote: Aitvaras is a nature spirit in Lithuanian mythology. It is also known by other names, such as Atvaras, Damavykas, Pūkis, Sparyžius, Koklikas, Gausinėlis, Žaltvikšas, and Spirukas, and is identical to the Latvian Pūķis.

claims.statement: An aitvaras looks like a white or black rooster with a meteor-like fiery tail; it is said to hatch from the egg of a 9- to 15-year-old rooster, and when it dies it becomes a spark.
claims.statement_id: Aitvaras tampak seperti ayam jantan putih atau hitam dengan ekor menyala seperti meteor; konon ia menetas dari telur ayam jantan berumur 9 hingga 15 tahun, dan jika mati ia menjadi percikan api.
claims.quote: An Aitvaras looks like a white or black rooster with a fiery tail like a meteor. An Aitvaras is said to hatch from an egg of a 9- to 15-year-old rooster. If an Aitvaras dies, it becomes a spark.

claims.statement: This Lithuanian creature is often described as a bird with a dragon's appearance outdoors; it lodges in a house, usually refuses to leave, and brings both good and bad luck, supplying stolen gold and grain that often get the household into trouble.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk Lituania ini sering digambarkan sebagai burung yang di luar rumah berpenampilan naga; ia menetap di rumah dan biasanya menolak pergi, membawa keberuntungan dan kesialan bagi penghuninya dengan memasok emas dan gandum curian yang sering menyusahkan keluarga itu.
claims.quote: In many cases, this Lithuanian creature is described as a bird with the appearance of a dragon outdoors. An Aitvaras will lodge itself in a house and most often refuse to leave. It brings both good and bad luck to the inhabitants of the house, providing its adopted home with stolen gold and grain, often getting the household into trouble.

claims.statement: The being was first mentioned in 1547 by Martynas Mažvydas.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini pertama kali disebut pada 1547 oleh Martynas Mažvydas.
claims.quote: Erstmals erwähnt wurde das Wesen 1547 von Martynas Mažvydas.

claims.statement: The aitvaras moves by flying and is mostly fiery but can change its appearance; it brings grain and other wealth, sometimes stolen from neighbours, and if angered burns the house down.
claims.statement_id: Aitvaras bergerak dengan terbang dan umumnya berapi, tetapi dapat mengubah penampilannya; ia membawa gandum dan kekayaan lain yang kadang dicuri dari tetangga, dan jika dibuat marah ia membakar rumah.
claims.quote: Der Aitvaras bewegt sich fliegend und er ist zumeist feurig, kann aber sein Aussehen ändern. Er bringt Getreide und anderen Reichtum, den er aber mitunter dem Nachbarn entwendet. Wird er verzürnt, brennt er das Haus nieder.

claims.statement: The aitvaras is hatched from the egg of a seven-year-old rooster or the testicle of a black stallion, or lured by feeding it egg dishes.
claims.statement_id: Aitvaras ditetaskan dari telur ayam jantan berumur tujuh tahun atau dari buah zakar kuda jantan hitam, atau dipikat dengan diberi makan hidangan telur.
claims.quote: Der Aitvaras wird aus dem Ei eines siebenjährigen Hahnes oder aus dem Hoden eines schwarzen Hengstes ausgebrütet oder durch Füttern mit Eierspeise angelockt.

claims.statement: According to many sources, an aitvaras could be bought from the devil in exchange for the buyer's soul.
claims.statement_id: Menurut banyak sumber, aitvaras dapat dibeli dari iblis dengan menukar jiwa pembelinya.
claims.quote: Selon de nombreuses sources, les Aitvaras pouvaient être achetés auprès du diable, en échange de l'âme de l'acheteur.

claims.statement: The children's toy kite ("Drachen") is accordingly called aitvaras in Lithuanian.
claims.statement_id: Mainan anak layang-layang ("Drachen") dalam bahasa Lituania disebut aitvaras.
claims.quote: das Kinderspielzeug „Drachen“ heißt entsprechend im Litauischen aitvaras

claims.statement: Algirdas Julien Greimas studied this figure in Des dieux et des hommes, comparing it with the kaukai (plural of kaukas), chthonic dwarfs of Lithuanian tradition.
claims.statement_id: Algirdas Julien Greimas mengkaji tokoh ini dalam Des dieux et des hommes dengan membandingkannya dengan kaukai (jamak dari kaukas), semacam makhluk kerdil dunia bawah dalam tradisi Lituania.
claims.quote: Algirdas Julien Greimas a consacré une étude à cette figure mythologique dans Des dieux et des hommes, en la mettant en regard des kaukai (pluriel de kaukas), sortes de nains chthoniens de la tradition lituanienne

claims.statement: In Romanian folklore a balaur (pl. balauri) is a kind of many-headed dragon or monstrous serpent, sometimes said to have wings; it usually has about three heads, but some legends give seven or even twelve.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Rumania, balaur (jamak: balauri) adalah sejenis naga berkepala banyak atau ular monster, kadang disebut bersayap; kepalanya biasanya sekitar tiga, tetapi menurut beberapa legenda bisa tujuh atau bahkan dua belas.
claims.quote: in Romanian folklore is a type of many-headed dragon or monstrous serpent, sometimes said to be equipped with wings. The number of heads is usually around three, but they can also have seven heads or even twelve heads according to some legends.

claims.statement: In Romanian the word balaur can also refer to any monster-like creature.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Rumania, kata balaur juga dapat dipakai untuk makhluk apa pun yang mirip monster.
claims.quote: Dalam bahasa Rumania, kata balaur juga dapat digunakan untuk merujuk makhluk apapun yang mirip monster.

claims.statement: In folktales the balaur is typically evil, demanding or abducting young maidens or the princess, and defeated by heroes such as Saint George or the fair youth Făt-Frumos.
claims.statement_id: Dalam dongeng, balaur biasanya jahat, meminta atau menculik gadis muda atau putri, dan dikalahkan oleh pahlawan seperti Santo Georgius (Saint George) atau pemuda tampan Făt-Frumos.
claims.quote: The balaur in folktale is typically evil, demanding or abducting young maidens or the princess, and defeated by the hero such as Saint George or the fair youth Făt-Frumos.

claims.statement: In Romanian folklore the balaur or balaurul is a serpentine being guarding treasures and princesses.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Rumania, balaur atau balaurul adalah makhluk mirip ular yang menjaga harta dan putri.
claims.quote: in Romanian folklore the balaur or balaurul is a serpentine being who guards treasures and princesses

claims.statement: According to folklorist Tudor Pamfile there are three types of balauri: water-, land- and air-dwelling; one of the first type is a seven-headed monster dwelling in a village well and demanding maidens as sacrifice.
claims.statement_id: Menurut folklorist Tudor Pamfile, ada tiga jenis balaur dalam tradisi rakyat: penghuni air, darat, dan udara; salah satu jenis pertama adalah monster berkepala tujuh yang tinggal di sumur desa dan meminta gadis sebagai korban.
claims.quote: According to folklorist Tudor Pamfile, there are three types of balauri in folk tradition: water-, land-, and air-dwelling. A type of balaur of the first type is a seven-headed monster that dwells in the well of a village, demanding maidens as sacrifice

claims.statement: The balaur is often associated with weather and is also called hala or ala, usually a Slavic term for a weather demon; this is Pamfile's air-dwelling "third type", and when two balauri fight in the air, damage such as uprooted trees follows.
claims.statement_id: Balaur sering dikaitkan dengan cuaca dan disebut juga hala atau ala, istilah Slavia untuk iblis cuaca; inilah "jenis ketiga" Pamfile yang tinggal di udara, dan bila dua balaur bertarung di udara timbul kerusakan cuaca seperti pohon tercabut.
claims.quote: The balaur is often associated with the weather and is alternatively called hala or ala, which is usually a Slavic term for a weather demon. This is the type Pamfile calls the "third type" that is air-dwelling. When two balauri meet and fight in the air, there ensues various meteorological damages such as uprooting of trees

claims.statement: The balaur and the zmeu are often confounded with each other.
claims.statement_id: Balaur dan zmeu sering tertukar satu sama lain.
claims.quote: It is noted that the balaur and the zmeu are often confounded with each other.

claims.statement: A balaur was controlled by these weather-controlling sorcerers with "a golden rein".
claims.statement_id: Balaur dikendalikan oleh para penyihir pengendali cuaca (Solomonari) dengan "tali kekang emas".
claims.quote: A balaur was controlled by these weather-controlling sorcerers using "a golden rein"

claims.statement: There are legends that the balaur can produce precious stones from its saliva, and it is said that whoever slays it will be forgiven a sin.
claims.statement_id: Ada legenda bahwa balaur dapat menghasilkan batu permata dari air liurnya, dan konon siapa pun yang berhasil membunuhnya akan diampuni satu dosanya.
claims.quote: There are also legends about the balaur in which they can produce precious stones from their saliva. Also, it is said that whoever manages to slay it will be forgiven a sin.

claims.statement: In this source's version of the classification, the land balaur lives far from farmland, often in the mountains, forging or guarding precious stones and metals; the third type is the winged zmeu that controls clouds to bring storms.
claims.statement_id: Menurut pembagian Pamfile versi sumber ini, balaur darat tinggal jauh dari lahan pertanian, sering di pegunungan, dan menempa atau menjaga batu permata dan logam; jenis ketiganya adalah zmeu bersayap yang mengendalikan awan untuk memunculkan badai.
claims.quote: Le balaur de terre qui vit loin des terres cultivables, souvent dans la montagne, et forge ou garde des pierres précieuses et des métaux. Le zmeu ailé qui contrôle les nuages pour faire apparaître les orages.

claims.statement: According to some sources the balaur (instead of the zmeu) is the mount of the weather-controlling Solomonari.
claims.statement_id: Menurut sebagian sumber, balaur (bukan zmeu) adalah tunggangan para Solomonari yang mengendalikan cuaca.
claims.quote: The balaur (instead of the zmeu) is the vehicle of the weather-controlling Solomonari according to some sources.

claims.statement: A chort is an anthropomorphic malign spirit or demon in Slavic folk tradition, often depicted like Christian devils with horns, hooves and a skinny tail; a single chort is sometimes a son of Chernobog and Mara, and in folk Christianity chorts are lesser minions of Satan.
claims.statement_id: Chort (bahasa Rusia чёрт, bahasa Polandia czart, bahasa Ceko čert) adalah roh jahat atau iblis berwujud manusia dalam tradisi rakyat Slavia, sering digambarkan seperti iblis Kristen dengan tanduk, kuku belah, dan ekor kurus; dalam mitologi Slavia satu chort kadang disebut putra dewa Chernobog dan dewi Mara, dan dalam Kristen rakyat mereka dianggap antek rendahan Iblis (Satan).
claims.quote: is an anthropomorphic malign spirit or demon in Slavic folk tradition. Chorts are often depicted identically to Christian devils, with horns, hooves, and a skinny tail. In Slavic mythology, a singular chort is sometimes identified as a son of the god Chernobog and the goddess Mara. In folk Christianity, they are considered lesser minions of Satan.

claims.statement: One theory: it is the past passive participle of an unattested verb (nouns *čarъ, *čara, "magic, sorcery"), the exact equivalent of Lithuanian kerė́ti, "to bewitch".
claims.statement_id: Satu teori: kata *čьrtъ adalah partisipel pasif dari kata kerja tak terbukti (bentuk benda *čarъ, *čara, "sihir") yang setara persis dengan kata Lituania kerė́ti, "menyihir".
claims.quote: One is that it is the past passive participle of an unattested verb (nouns: *čarъ, *čara ("magic, sorcery")) that is the exact equivalent of the Lithuanian kerė́ti ("to bewitch").

claims.statement: Another: it is a substantivised t-participle of *ker- ("to cut, to chop"), perhaps from a chort imagined lame (one leg shorter).
claims.statement_id: Teori lain: kata ini partisipel-t yang dibendakan dari *ker- ("memotong, mencincang"), mungkin karena chort dibayangkan pincang (satu kakinya lebih pendek).
claims.quote: Another is that it is a substantivized t-participle of *ker- (to cut, to chop), which could be derived from a chort imagined as being lame (having one leg shorter).

claims.statement: In Czech and Slovak folk tales the čert is not evil per se; it often tempts characters to sell their souls for something (money, power, completion of a task).
claims.statement_id: Dalam dongeng Ceko dan Slowakia, čert tidak jahat semata; ia sering membujuk tokoh menjual jiwa demi sesuatu (uang, kekuasaan, penyelesaian tugas).
claims.quote: In Czech and Slovak folk tales, čert is not an evil character per se. It is often trying to tease characters in selling their souls in exchange for something (money, power, completion of a task).

claims.statement: Another hypothesis derives Proto-Slavic *čьrtъ from *čersti / čьrtǫ, "to draw a line, furrow", reconstructing it as a supernatural Draughtsman determining human fate.
claims.statement_id: Menurut hipotesis lain, kata Slavia Purba *čьrtъ diturunkan dari *čersti / čьrtǫ, "menggaris, membuat alur", sehingga *čьrtъ dapat ditafsirkan sebagai "Juru Gambar" adikodrati penentu nasib manusia.
